# CONFESSIONS BOOK ONE

...diligently keep the commandments of the Lord our God whom you have left; they subsequently add:

They also claim that the promises of renewal for the same church have been fulfilled. I would like to know here who those men are, living in such holy and apostolic institutions, in which the church is rightly judged to have been renewed. The **Waldensians** <note>original: "Valdenses" — A medieval spiritual movement that sought to return to apostolic poverty, later deemed heretical by the Roman Catholic Church and seen as a precursor to the Reformation.</note> themselves do not admit us to this praise; indeed, they fight against us on behalf of that idea. They therefore make themselves the pupils of the renewed church. But since the "heads" of such great errors—as we say and will more conveniently prove in another place—are found among them, it is most certain that with whatever madness they previously imputed the losses of the church to our side, with that same madness they now arrogantly claim the renewal of the same for their own assemblies. To refute this most vain presumption, let them know that the time of the church's renewal is by no means signified as being in our own century. 

**"Tell us,"** say the disciples in the Gospel, **"when will these things be? And what will be the sign of your coming and of the end of the age?"** <note>Matthew 24:3</note> And Jesus, answering, said to them: **"See that no one deceives you. For many will come in my name saying, 'I am the Christ,' and will deceive many."** And a little later: **"And many false prophets will arise and deceive many, and because iniquity will abound, the charity of many will grow cold. But he who perseveres until the end, he shall be saved. And this Gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in the whole world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come. When you see the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place (let him who reads understand)..."** And a little later: **"Then if anyone says to you, 'Behold, here is Christ,' or 'There,' do not believe it. For false Christs and false prophets will arise and give great signs and wonders, so as to lead into error, if possible, even the elect."**

Paul the Apostle also writes thus in the second [letter] to the Thessalonians about those times: **"Let no one deceive you in any way, for unless the falling away comes first and the man of sin is revealed, the son of perdition <note>A title often associated with the Antichrist.</note>, who opposes and exalts himself above everything that is called God or that is worshipped, so that he sits in the temple of God, showing himself as if he were God."** And a little later: **"And then that wicked one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus shall slay with the spirit of his mouth and destroy by the brightness of his coming—he whose coming is according to the working of Satan in all power, signs, and lying wonders, and in every seduction of iniquity for those who perish, because they did not receive the love of truth that they might be saved. Therefore God will send them the operation of error so that they believe a lie, that all may be judged who did not believe the truth but consented to iniquity."**

The Lord Christ shows that they will be the foremost of all and will consent to iniquity: **"I have come in the name of my Father and you did not receive me. If another comes in his own name, him you will receive."** <note>John 5:43</note> Therefore, from the testimonies of such manifest prophecy, the Gospel, and the Apostle—since that son of perdition has not yet appeared, since the whole expectation of the Jews still remains for their Messiah (who will drive them mad with lying signs), and finally since that most atrocious tribulation which is to happen to those confessing Christ is still held in the secrets of God—we boldly say that the time of the church's renewal is still expected in the future. 

For that <term>restoration|The Latin "restitutio" implies a returning to a former, purer state.</term> of ancient Christian holiness is not to be understood as anything other than after that wicked one has been destroyed and Israel, mocked by its final error, has begun to recognize the true Messiah, Jesus Christ. Regarding this renewal, the most certain signs and the most certain prophecies of all the prophets have now preceded from ancient ages. And as the Apostle most aptly demonstrates in that [letter] to the Romans: **"I say then, have they stumbled so as to fall? God forbid! But through their fall, salvation has come to the Gentiles to provoke them to jealousy. Now if their fall is riches for the world and their diminishing is riches for the Gentiles, how much more their fullness!"** And again: **"If their loss is the reconciliation of the world, what shall their acceptance be but life from the dead?"** And again: **"For blindness has happened in Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles should come in, and so all Israel shall be saved, as it is written: There shall come out of Zion he who shall turn away iniquity from Jacob."** <note>Romans 11:11-26</note> And this is why our Lord and Savior, when speaking to his disciples about the last times, immediately added: **"This Gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in the entire world as a testimony to all nations."**

# AGAINST THE ERRORS OF THE WALDENSIANS AND...

This will be the **renewal of the church** <term>renovatio ecclesiae: a theological concept referring to the restoration of the church to its original purity or a future state of perfection</term> that we accept, which will be celebrated in the universal gathering of both peoples <note>The "two peoples" refers to the traditional Christian view of the eventual union of Jews and Gentiles into one faith.</note> into the Christian faith, so that what was written again might be fully fulfilled: *And I have other sheep that are not of this fold; them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice, and there shall be one sheepfold and one shepherd.* <note>John 10:16</note> Therefore, let the **Waldensians** <note>original: "Valdenses"</note> begone; let their proud presumption begone, which they have turned against the authority of Scripture at this time to our hatred, with equal madness and lying, upon themselves and that most narrow clandestine assembly of theirs. Nothing in the present prophecy signifies anything about them, except that: *False Christs and false prophets shall arise whose coming is according to the working of Satan.* <note>Matthew 24:24; 2 Thessalonians 2:9</note> The Waldensians have followed this part of the prophecy, composing lies beyond the Scriptures to their own destruction. Furthermore, if the renewal of the church is believed to be fulfilled in them, let us by the same right believe it was fulfilled as many times in previous centuries as **Manichaeus**, **Montanus**, **Arius**, **Nestorius**, or **Eutyches** <note>These are names of famous historical heretics from the early church: Manichaeus (Manichaeism), Montanus (Montanism), Arius (Arianism), Nestorius (Nestorianism), and Eutyches (Monophysitism).</note> introduced their pestilential dogmas into the purity of the faith. Certainly, a renewal was made whenever heresies were suppressed in the church, but not one in which the heretics could boast—rather the Catholics. Yet, it was not such a renewal as we have proven from the Scriptures will occur at the end of the age in the calling of all nations and Jews. But even the Waldensians feared that this insane presumption would be held against them; therefore, fleeing and as if correcting themselves, they add:

-> "Neither do we arrogate so much to ourselves that we wish to be called or to become the Catholic Church among whom alone salvation is stored. Instead, we labor with anxious diligence to be made participants in ecclesiastical truth." <-

Truly, I am moved to pity for our patience, that we endure so lightly being occupied with such a rustic fiction. For in this trickery, by which they presently wish to hold our eyes, nothing more common, nothing cruder, or nothing less consistent with itself could be objected to us: its illusion will be uncovered by even a slight little questioning. You ask the Waldensians: Do you believe the ecclesiastical **keys** <note>The "keys of the kingdom," representing the authority to forgive sins or excommunicate.</note> are placed solely with the successor of Peter and the Roman Pontiff, the Vicar of Christ? Do you believe, in accordance with the Christian faith, in the adoration of saints, in prayers for the dead, or in the truth of the **Sacrament of the Altar**? <note>The Eucharist or Holy Communion.</note> "We do not believe," they say. Where then is the **communion of saints**? We believe the same things as the saints in everything we believe; the Waldensians believe against the saints in whatever they do not believe with us. We hold the faith of the saints, for which we now dispute against the Waldensian: the present writings and monuments, which between the confessions of both of us, decree with a certain judgment this day. The church cannot consist here and there in this diversity; if it does, Christ is divided. For we Christians and those heretics were not baptized into one body. But Paul says: *One body and one spirit, as you are called in one hope of your calling; one Lord, one faith, one baptism.* <note>Ephesians 4:4-5</note> Therefore, it is necessary that the church consist whole and entire with one of us; it will never consist with both. Truly, why do they elude us? Why do they prevaricate? Let them pour out openly what they conceive in secret; finally, even against their will, we understand their deceits. For with what conscience can they believe salvation is stored in another part than that from which they have placed the salvation—that is, the renewal—of the church?

Finally, standing in the order of obedience, to be subject to its rulers with intimate love. And this, I say, they play at from an obscure corner. For if they wish to be understood as referring to our rulers, they could certainly have found those who should be followed holily under Christian obedience, under whom they might be initiated in a Catholic manner, and where priests might be rightly anointed and confirmed by the **episcopal laying on of hands**. <note>The traditional Catholic method of ordaining priests and bishops through apostolic succession.</note> They should follow these as examples of priestly power and innocence for a right conscience toward God, without the public infamy of heresy. But if they flee from there, let them confess that they betray their whole cause and cast themselves into obstinate rebel- <meta>catchword: rebel</meta>

### CONFESSIONS, BOOK ONE

...if they did not find someone to follow. This is both strange and miserable: that all shame for what is right and all consciousness of the Gospel is so denied to us, as if we were born equally with **Tartarus** <term>Tartarus: in classical mythology and early Christian writing, a name for the deepest abyss of Hell</term> for **Gehenna** <term>Gehenna: a term for Hell, derived from the Valley of Hinnom near Jerusalem</term>. Finally, we are believed to wander away from Christian salvation—away from Christ, from the Apostles, and from the teachers of the Church—just as much as those in Tartarus, according to these most impure Waldensians.

[**As for the evil workers—whom we have found to be enemies of the Bride <note>The "Bride" refers to the Church, based on the biblical metaphor of the Church as the Bride of Christ.</note> and her truth—we fear to be subject to or obey them out of fear of eternal damnation, and finally, for the sake of obedience to Christ and his Church in those matters where they think, speak, and act against the law of God.**] <note>The text in brackets represents the Waldensian position being quoted or summarized by the author.</note>

Indeed, they are found to be subject to or obey no ecclesiastical authority. Therefore, they grant nothing of what is fair and good to any of our people. They consider us and all our things as impure, which I judge to be no secret; for when the Waldensians saw that they could not withdraw from the Christian commonwealth with any appearance of honor, they instead accused it of being dishonorable. From this starting point, they now criminalize the entire Christian state. From this premise, whatever the priests do—whether they sit, whether they stand, whether they walk; add also whether they dine or sleep—they drag it all into vice. Whatever they pray, whatever sacred rites they perform, whatever they do to conform themselves to the divine will, they drag it all into vice. Whatever we Christians are baptized into in the faith of the Trinity, whatever of the Gospel we believe, whatever consciousness of the fair and just we hold toward God and man—they drag it all into vice. If we commit any depravity or ignorance out of human weakness, even though we accuse ourselves of it through penance <term>penance: the Catholic sacrament of confession and repentance for sins</term> before God for our cleansing, they nonetheless drag it all into vice.

Nothing profits us toward the innocence which the Waldensians, with ill-advised madness, have snatched from the Christian world, unless we put on the name of the Waldensians. This "novel name" carries such weight today over the name of "Christian" that they would have us believe that even if the Apostles, the martyrs, and all sanctity were to return, they would have to return under the single name in which the Waldensians have conspired today; they want it believed that people will only be saved again under this faction.

What is the reason for them to exclude Christ, the Apostles, and all salvation from us so violently? "Because," they say, "we do not fear to submit to or obey evil workers." From this they hold us; from this our innocence is overturned. This is a great cause—indeed, the greatest—if it can be shown to be rightly and faithfully taken up according to examples and the Scriptures.

Therefore, let us search for those "evils" for which they claim they had to abandon the workers of the Christian cause in favor of obedience to Christ and the Church. And here indeed they say nothing, but in another work against the teacher **Augustine** <note>St. Augustine of Hippo (354–430 AD), a central doctor of the Church whose writings on the nature of the Church were used to refute dissenters.</note> they say similar things: **Avarice**, luxury in all things, and profiting from sacred things. Will they also add idolatry? Will they add the impurity of the **Manichaeans**? The blasphemies of **Arius**? The filth of **Muhammad**? <note>original: "Maumectis spuritias." Medieval polemics often grouped Islam with Christian heresies.</note> The sacrileges of the **Antichrist**?

Certainly not. If they had found such things, they might have withdrawn their obedience with impunity—indeed, they would have stayed away even through the greatest crime, just as the Apostle says: *But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed <note>original: "Anathema sit"</note>. As I said before, so say I now again: If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.* <note>Galatians 1:8-9</note>

But if they are greedy, or if they are wealthy contrary to their profession (as is thought), even if they think, speak, or act so, they are not like an infidel or those whom the Apostle Paul said were "accursed." Rather, they do whatever can be done or charged against human weakness. Surely whoever believes in the remission of sins will be forced to confess that avarice, luxury, or all things committed out of the weakness of the flesh are forgiven—just as forgiveness was granted to the woman caught in adultery, and granted to the tax collectors, and to all those whom Christ our Savior commanded us to forgive not just seven times, but seventy-times-seven times. These are not "enemies of the Bride and the truth," as the Waldensians have said with excessive bitterness, but "sons of mercy," sons of God, of whom we read: *I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven...*

# AGAINST THE ERRORS OF THE WALDENSIANS AND...

...over one sinner who does penance than over ninety-nine righteous ones who do not need penance. In accordance with the example of the woman taken in adultery, Christ does not permit even a stone to be thrown at these people by the severity of the Law. Yet these Waldensians dare not only to stone them and deliver them to the destruction of the flesh—so that the spirit might nonetheless be saved—but even to condemn them as enemies of the Bride <note>original: "hostes sponsae"; the "Bride" is a traditional metaphor for the Church.</note> and of the truth for an unforgivable offense. 

And yet those accusers, who refer everything to the example of Christ—and rightly so, if only they did it correctly—ought to imitate that Gospel command: **Be merciful, just as your heavenly Father is merciful.** But hatred for our people has shaken them; while they indulge this hatred and seek from every available matter a fire to use against apostolic power, they instead blow up a fire of apostasy <term>apostasy: the formal desertion or abandonment of one's religion or faith</term> for themselves. For being ignorant of the justice of God and seeking to establish their own, they are not subject to the justice of God. 

But let us return again to the beginning. Let us grant them what they most desire to be granted: suppose the ecclesiastical Rectors <note>Rectors: here meaning bishops, priests, and other Church leaders.</note> of this time are enemies of the truth and of the Bride; suppose they are those who, according to their impenitent hearts, treasure up wrath for themselves in the final days. Not even for that reason should they have cast out reverence for the Church. For were not the Scribes and Pharisees such men in the synagogue? And yet, did Christ ever encourage the people to cast away the Law and the ceremonies of the Temple? 

Does Christ not cry out "Woe!" eight times against the evil presiding officers of the synagogue? **Woe to you,** he says, **scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who shut the kingdom of heaven before men; for you do not enter, nor do you allow those entering to go in,** and so forth. Likewise, in another place: **Look and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.** Finally, concluding his entire judgment of them in a short chapter in the Gospel of John, he said: **You are of your father the devil, and you wish to do the desires of your father.** 

Regarding these same faithless men whom he judged to be on the side of the devil, he says again in Matthew: **Go, show yourself to the priest and offer your gift which Moses commanded as a testimony to them.** And again: **The scribes and Pharisees have sat upon the chair of Moses <note>The "Chair of Moses" refers to the authority of the Jewish teachers to interpret the Law.</note>; therefore, observe and do all things whatsoever they say to you, but do not do according to their works; for they speak, but they do not do.** 

If the Waldensians truly strive to feel and act in obedience to Christ and the Church according to the authority of such scriptures, they ought not, with a clear conscience, disturb any evil workers simply because they handle ecclesiastical power. Christ, who (as the Waldensians say) strictly observed his Church in the days of his flesh, freed them from all fear by his own example. Thus, no fear—not even a "holy" fear as they call it—nor any horror of Gehenna <term>Gehenna: a term for Hell or a place of fiery torment</term> should henceforth have more power among them to despise the rectors than the doctrine of Christ has to retain them. 

We have spoken in this place in favor of the rectors—or rather, in favor of the ecclesiastical hierarchy—against the Waldensians, who profane that hierarchy with most deadly rashness among all sorts of filthy and soiled "bench-workers" <note>original: "sellularios"; this refers to manual laborers or artisans who work sitting at a bench, used here as a class-based insult against the uneducated Waldensian leaders.</note>.

We have heard their faith; we have heard the poisons of their confession regarding the order of the priesthood. But perhaps I should not yet have said "poisons" until I had proved they were poisons. Yet let me call them poisons, because they take this topic—the weightiest topic, upon which the whole Christian matter hangs, as the Apostle [Paul] testifies: *For when the priesthood is changed, it is necessary that a change of the law also be made* <note>A reference to Hebrews 7:12, a key verse used in debates about religious authority.</note>—and by transferring this priesthood to themselves, they have made it entirely foreign to us. They use words—which we must often complain about—that are so slippery that, just as a **crab** <note>original: "Cancer"</note> crawls away if you loosen your grip, and just as an **eel** <note>original: "Murena"</note> slips out if you squeeze it, so does their uncertain opinion slide between two meanings. 

For behold, we wish to take the most obvious sense for the sake of Christian simplicity, which they now try to use to bait us, as if they were saying: "The ordination of the priesthood proceeds in truth from the High Bishop and great priest"—that is, the Apostolic Vicar on earth <note>The Pope</note>—so that the Vicar in the seat of Peter is the one in the place of Christ’s embassy, and he is the one to whom the remaining things they subjoin apply. Truly, while we labor to fight against those Waldensians from this defense, and to prove that their dismal priesthood is not derived from that High Bishop and great priest, suddenly everything vanishes. They frustrate us and turn their traps against us. Our simplicity is mocked by that entire assembly, because we believed they were so forgetful of themselves that they would overthrew themselves with their own logic. 

Therefore, because of these men who have gone against us in all things, we are forced to seek another meaning by which they might make us "impious" and themselves "pious" for the sake of the business they have undertaken. And so, they understand "the ordination of the priesthood to proceed in truth from the High Bishop and great priest" to mean **Christ**. We say the same: we confess equally that Christ is the High Pontiff and the High Priest from whom all power of the sacred rites and every priesthood has flowed, like from a head into the body of the Church—so they should not think they are telling us something we do not know. 

But they have not yet embraced all the rights of the legitimate priesthood by saying this; they have not yet satisfied the expectation of the faithful. There remains something hidden under the fraud of that sentence which they utter with their usual treachery on their own behalf and against us—that is, against the Church hierarchy. For they understand that the ordination of the priesthood proceeds from Christ in such a sense that it does not only come from that succession which has proceeded in a continuous line from the Apostles to this day. Rather, they believe that whoever might be a boaster of a holier life <note>The author is criticizing the Waldensian belief that personal "holiness" is what makes a priest, not an official appointment by the Church.</note> possesses the power of **binding and loosing** <note>original: "ligandi & soluendi"; the spiritual authority to forgive or retain sins.</note> through those same words, receiving it immediately from Christ just as the Apostles did.

To Peter, however, he speaks uniquely:

For the <term>power of loosing and binding</term> <note>The authority to forgive sins or excommunicate, and to create binding church laws.</note> is not outside the Apostles and those to whom the Apostles handed it down by <term>legitimate succession</term> <note>The doctrine that authority is passed down in an unbroken chain from the Apostles to modern bishops.</note>. Nor is that authority outside Peter and his seat <note>original: "sedem," referring to the Holy See or the Papacy.</note>, that authority which the Savior secretly commended to him as the head over the other Apostles: "To you I will give the keys of the kingdom of heaven" and "Feed my sheep."

Those, however, who do not permit Christ this ecclesiastical substitution—who do not permit that saying of Job: "God speaks once, and the second time he does not repeat the same thing"—but wish the authority of the keys to be given indiscriminately to the Apostles as common members of the Church, not according to a prerogative of power granted to them, must necessarily admit that the Apostles acted arrogantly and to the deception of the rest of the saints. For from the beginning, they transferred the ordination of the Churches only into their own power, which they alone nonetheless had not received. Indeed, the saints of the primitive church at that time would have been granting the Apostles such great authority with a foolish simplicity, if they themselves did not also assume the priesthood with similar power based on the purity of their lives. They say: "There were no vices among the priests then." Nevertheless, it is permitted to do holily, outside of vice, in every way whatever we do of the Gospel. It is permitted for anyone at any time to exercise whatever we have received equally with the Apostles—whatever the Apostles had transferred solely into their own power beyond the Gospel.

Therefore, whether all and each of those **Waldensians** are priests, or whether any one out of them all received consecration immediately from Christ for the sake of all—which they might then [pour into others by the contribution of power with words fit for this purpose and the imposition of hands] <note>original: "contributione potestatis aptis ad hoc verbis et manuum impositione trans funderēt"</note>—certainly, neither all and each of them, nor that single one, are admitted according to the evangelical constitution and the tradition of the Church, or according to the examples of the saints. For if all and each of them are found to be such according to the canon which the Waldensians have prescribed here for priests, then by their own merit, they will already have been consecrated by Christ regardless of the imposition of hands by that single individual. If they do not admit this regarding everyone, we shall not admit it regarding that one man: that he should have the means from a source where the many could not have it.

Perhaps that single individual will have recourse to our priesthood, from which—by stealthy works, like **Prometheus** <note>In Greek mythology, Prometheus stole fire from the gods to give to humanity; here, the author accuses the Waldensian founder of stealing the "fire" of priestly authority from the Catholic Church.</note> returning to earth with fire stolen from the sun—he might have carried back sacred power to his own people. Certainly, he could not have brought it back except from a Bishop. For the divine **Dionysius** <note>Refers to Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite, an influential mystical theologian thought at the time to be the convert of St. Paul.</note> says in *The Ecclesiastical Hierarchy*:

> Wherefore the divine law has perhaps eternally distributed the holiness of pontifical ordinations, the preparation of the divine ointment, and the sacred consecration of the altar to the offices and virtues of the most reverend pontiffs.

What do our Waldensians mutter here? What do they murmur obscurely from their corner? I have brought that forward for one reason, and it is confessed by three: from where comes their oil of confirmation, their oil of extreme unction, and from where the consecration of their sacred altar? Those heads of their confession regarding confirmation and extreme unction are profane; they lack all those things just as they lack **Bishops**. "Your gatherings are wicked," says God through **Isaiah**: "My soul has hated your new moons and your solemnities; they have become a burden to me, I am weary of enduring them" <note>A reference to Isaiah 1:13–14, used here to delegitimize Waldensian worship.</note>. Let them show an Apostolic Bishop—who, even if he has departed from human affairs, is still found in the catalog of sacred ordinations of that time—whoever he was among the Waldensians who brought back from our people both himself as a Bishop and then such great power for making more priests. Truly, what Catholic ordination could that single man expect, which all and each of them do not expect? Namely, the very same vices of ours that terrified all of them also terrified this one man from being consecrated by our people; and yet, he could not have it from elsewhere by any eternal lot of divine law. Finally, he did not have it from Christ either; since [the contribution of power with fit words and the imposition of hands for strengthening] were especially lacking to that primary leader. There are more things here that are relevant to those Waldensians; they rise up, or finally, they break out...

-># CONFESSIONS, BOOK ONE,<-

Do they desire, for instance, to remove the old anointing? To take up new rites unknown to apostolic monuments? To stir up strange opinions against the decrees of the saints under this new assembly? They ought to have preserved themselves without vice so that the Church, renewed in them, might not fall just as it has in us. Finally, if they could have been taught in all these things by divine illumination—all of which they demanded be confirmed by the predictions of the prophets, the gospels, and canonical revelations—yet they do not show these things from the scriptures here or in any other place. Instead, they cast the cause onto empty cavils, as when they say: <insert>indeed, we fear to obey evil workers, whom we have caught as enemies of the bride <note>The "bride" is a traditional metaphor for the Christian Church.</note> and her truth, out of fear of eternal damnation</insert> and many similar things so pressing. Therefore, they truly "hold a wolf by the ears" <note>original: "lupum de auribus tenent." A classical proverb meaning to be in a situation where it is equally dangerous to hold on or let go.</note>, a wolf they can neither hold nor dare to release. I do not wish to dwell on this now, as we have been wordy enough; but from another dispute, into which I hasten with the full weight of the case—and to which I so often defer so many things—I wish to examine everything from head to heel <note>original: "de capite ad vnguem," literally "from head to fingernail," meaning thoroughly.</note> in its proper place.

At this point, I only needed to mention that those **Waldensians** <note>A medieval Christian movement that was often persecuted for its beliefs, which predated the Protestant Reformation.</note> who wanted the Royal Majesty to look for their secrets in this confession, nevertheless most studiously led the most pious Prince away from their deepest secrets with shrouds of words, like childish amusements. For regarding the veneration of the saints, the prayers for the dead, the sacrament of the Body and Blood of Christ, the holy Church, and now the order of priests—all of which are most destructive and hateful matters that cause them the greatest ill-will—they have either kept a deep silence or, as I said, left them in doubt through shrouds of words. If we think any unworthiness has been admitted here, we shall judge it to have been admitted not so much on the part of those who wished to use the given opportunity for their own benefit, but on the part of those to whom these things are addressed—those who have the power to tolerate such things. How it could be done with any glory to this day, that those Waldensians could draw out the ears of our people for so long with impunity, is not for a private person to say. The provinces of the Christian name, which hear these same things with great sorrow of mind and see this pestilence and these mockeries always being repressed yet always sustained, will judge more easily. Let us, however, approach their main point concerning the **Communion of Saints**, under which they write the following:

It is clear, therefore, that only the elect—participants in true faith, grace, and justice through the merit of Christ—belong to the glory of eternal salvation. Just as they communicate in the sacraments for the evidence of faith, even if they should be in a state of seduction, the damnation of torment will not seize them. But the evil, who possess an "unformed faith," even though they may communicate in truth through sacraments, dignities, administrations, and public customs, as long as they are devoid of true faith, they participate unworthily like **Hypocrites**. If they have been moved by an erroneous spirit, they fall into seduction and deception under that same guidance.

It seems to me that with these words, like a final trumpet blast, they have separated the goats from the sheep according to the Gospel voice. Therefore, we must inquire who those "elect" participants of true faith, grace, and justice are. Just as I shall establish who belongs to the side of merit, they shall show the evil of unformed faith from their own group. For those Waldensians write such things about themselves: [Moreover, we believe in Christ when, knowing Him as our God and Savior, we embrace all His words with full faith, loving Him also with perfect charity, and are joined in the love of faith with His faithful members; finally, we worship Christ our Redeemer with honor worthy of Him, dissuaded by His prohibition and bound by His command.] By the judgment of these things, they themselves would presently be the truly elect.

But we do not demand such grace from those who cannot be in seduction at all, since we do not recede even "by a fingernail" <note>original: "de vngue." I say, we who do not recede from Apostolic doctrine even by a fingernail! Yet they themselves make us fall into seduction and deception, primarily when we have emulated those in error. But how, even by their own opinion, shall we be in seduction when we communicate in the truth? For they write thus: <insert>But the evil ones of unformed faith, although they have communicated in the truth through sacraments, dignities, administrations, and public customs...</insert>. For what is "communication in the truth" if not our assumption into the mystical body of Christ? We were assumed in baptism; we were assumed in the participation of the sacraments; we were assumed into the communion of saints in that faith which they left to us, attested by martyrdoms and miracles. Our Bishops and priests are worth as much to us as their cobblers <term>Cerdones: traditionally meaning "handicraftsmen" or "cobblers," used here as a derogatory term for the Waldensian lay-preachers who lacked formal theological training.</term> can never be to them. We stand upon the foundation of Christ; whatever foundation is not of Christ, we equally detest and ignore. Let them search us for the foundation of any heretics and see if we confess to any; we confess to none. Who, then, shall cast us out from the foundation of Christ which the Apostles preached, and which our fathers, received from their fathers’ fathers, passed down to us? 

We sin, I confess—let those Waldensians be against the testimony of the scriptures—since we all offend in many things. And "if we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves and the truth is not in us" <note>A quotation from 1 John 1:8.</note>. Let them be "just" boastfully according to their own conscience, while we are "just" through our sinners’ state and without lying. If, therefore, we offend Christ unpardonably by every sin, where will be the faith by which we believe in the remission of sins? Where will the Sacrament of Penance <note>The rite of confession and reconciliation.</note> be? But Christ knew that those called to the Gospel would sin; therefore, he left us these remedies, just as Wisdom said: <insert>For God did not make death, nor does He rejoice in the perdition of the living; for He created all things that they might exist</insert>. They go up into the temple to pray, both Pharisees and tax collectors alike. # THE FIRST BOOK OF CONFESSIONS
h 5.

"Be merciful to me, a sinner." <note>original: "propitiús eſto mihi peccatori." A reference to the humble prayer of the tax collector in Luke 18:13, contrasted with the pride of the Pharisee.</note> But what does mercy decree here concerning the merit of both? "Amen, I say to you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other." For these reasons, I shall consider that I have reclaimed the Christian people and restored them to the place of Christ's communion and truth; otherwise, they might have been placed among the goats on the left hand of that terrible judgment, existing among the wicked with a formless faith, led by those Waldensians who are truly Pharisees and truly hypocrites. 

Therefore, let us return to the beginning, inquiring whether they themselves deserve to be judged as truly elect, or as true participants in faith, grace, and justice. In the first place, if they are of the communion of the saints, who taught them this saying: <insert>Even if they were in seduction, the damnation of torment shall not take hold of them</insert>? This is certainly not an Apostolic sentiment. Did not that master, the serpent—more cunning than all the living creatures of the earth—teach it to them? He who said to the woman: "Why did God command you that you should not eat from every tree of Paradise?" To whom the woman responded: "We eat of the fruit of the trees which are in Paradise; but concerning the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of Paradise, God commanded us that we should not eat, and that we should not touch it, lest perhaps we die." But the serpent said to the woman: "You shall by no means die by death. For God knows that on whatever day you eat from it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like gods, knowing good and evil." 

Christ the Lord and our Savior sent the Apostles into the whole world under this mandate: "Going forth, preach, saying that the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand." But he also added authority to the mandate, saying: "He who hears you, hears me; and he who spurns you, spurns me; and he who spurns me, spurns Him who sent me." Our Waldensians followed this voice of the Gospel in the time of their ancestors many ages ago; they moved within the breadth of Apostolic doctrine and fed upon every tree of Paradise—that is, every ecclesiastical commentator. There was only one tree of the knowledge of good and evil which God forbade them to taste: "Do not be wise in your own conceit," <note>original: "Ne ſis ſapiens apud temetipſum." A warning against intellectual pride and private interpretation over Church tradition.</note> but "destroy counsels and every height that exalts itself against the knowledge of God, and bring every intellect into captivity in obedience to Christ." 

Our people are being tested by this precept for the first time in our age. The serpent comes and asks: "Why do you obey the Gospel?" We obey, "lest perhaps we die," because it shall be more tolerable for Sodom on that day than for that city which did not receive the preaching Apostles. There, that serpent—who had said to the woman "By no means," but "you shall be like gods knowing good and evil"—spoke to the Waldensians with a different sentence but with equal fraud: "You shall by no means die by death; <insert>for even if you are in seduction, the damnation of torment shall not take hold of you</insert>." Persuaded by this voice through the desires of their own senses, they went away. 

But the divine sentence followed immediately: "Woe to you who are wise in your own eyes, and prudent in your own sight." Thus, they lost everything at once: participation in the true faith, the communication of the sacraments, and even that "seduction" which they interpreted as a better hope. For God adds again: "Behold, Adam has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. Now, therefore, lest perhaps he put forth his hand and take also from the tree of life, and eat, and live forever," the Lord sent him out of the Paradise of pleasure. In truth, our Waldensians have become "knowers of good and evil" so that they might follow the one but despise the other. Thus, they are likewise excluded from this tree of life, which is Christ. Christ says of himself: "I am the way, and the truth, and the life." If those Waldensians hold the way, they also hold the truth; for there is no way except the truth of Jesus.

Following the previous page’s argument that the Waldensians follow a "satanic" logic by claiming that being misled (seduction) excuses one from damnation, the author now lists specific Waldensian "errors" and compares them to ancient heresies already condemned by the Church Fathers and biblical history.</meta>

# AGAINST THE ERRORS OF THE WALDENSIANS AND...

Christ is not seduction, but truth. Therefore, he who is in seduction does not have the truth in him; where there is no "way and truth," there is no "life." <note>original: "via & veritas non est vita." A reference to John 14:6: "I am the way, the truth, and the life."</note> Because the one Christ is the way, the truth, and the life, our Waldensians <note>The Waldensians were a medieval movement that lived in poverty and preached without Church authorization; they are seen here as dangerous heretics.</note> have cast themselves into seduction by their own desire, and have gone off the path. Now, out of that seduction, they wish to escape the damnation of torment; yet how much better it would have been had they escaped through the truth! But the truth did not please them; they preferred seduction. 

The Waldensians deny the veneration of the saints—this is seduction. The blessed Jerome <note>Saint Jerome (c. 342–420 AD), the translator of the Vulgate Bible and a staunch defender of Church tradition.</note> condemned this a thousand years ago in the case of the heretic Vigilantius. They do not accept images of the saints or prayers <term>suffrages: intercessory prayers or works offered on behalf of the deceased</term> for the dead—this is seduction. This Greek impiety <note>The author likely refers to the Iconoclasm or the theological differences of the Eastern Orthodox "Greek" Church.</note> the Church has condemned more than once. Finally, Christ the Lord condemned it from heaven when he removed Greek disobedience from the earth by means of the most cruel Turk <note>A common 15th- and 16th-century view that the Ottoman conquest of Constantinople was a divine punishment for the "errors" of the Greek Church.</note>, just as he once transferred Samaria and Ephraim to the Assyrians because of their golden calves. 

Regarding the Sacrament of the Altar <note>The Eucharist or Holy Communion.</note>, they do not believe rightly—this is seduction. The Church extinguished this same error in a certain Berengarius <note>Berengarius of Tours (d. 1088), who was condemned for challenging the doctrine of the Real Presence of Christ in the Eucharist.</note>, its very author, four hundred and fifty years ago. They preach that the Holy Spirit is separate from the Father and the Son—this is seduction, and a sacrilegious fragment of Arianism. <note>Arianism was an early Christian heresy that denied the full divinity of Christ and the orthodox understanding of the Trinity.</note> God drove this out through the infamous death of its author, Arius, and later the whole world thrust it into the outer darkness of eternal oblivion. 

They rashly claim for themselves the priesthood, the keys to the kingdom of heaven, and all rural magistracy—this is seduction. The avenging fire suppressed this in Korah; sudden death in Uzzah; and foul leprosy in King Uzziah. <note>These are biblical examples of individuals punished by God for usurping priestly or divine roles: Korah (Numbers 16), Uzzah (2 Samuel 6), and Uzziah (2 Chronicles 26).</note> They have brought back all the ancient and condemned impieties by which they might openly raise their horns against God, against the saints, and against the Church. 

And yet, they hope that the damnation of torment will not seize them despite their seduction! They have gathered to themselves no less impiety than the famous leaders of heresy, yet they hope for truth. If the damnation of torment does not seize them there in their seduction, then we should recall for the same cause the hateful heads of the ancient errors: Basilides, Marcion, Cerdo, and Valentinus <note>Famous leaders of Gnostic movements in the early Church (2nd century AD).</note>, whom even a rebellious soul understands to have been impious. Let us restore them, along with these Waldensians, to the fellowship of Christ and the communion of the saints—men whom the prince of the Apostles, Peter, along with John, Paul, Jude the brother of James, and Ignatius, held as enemies of the truth as long as they lived. Striking them everywhere in their preaching and letters with apostolic judgment, they cast them out from the communion of the saints and the Church by the decree of the Holy Spirit.

And our Waldensians, who also took up the same struggle of impiety against the Apostles—against Ignatius, Dionysius, Origen, Jerome, Augustine, and Gregory <note>A list of the major "Church Fathers" whose writings defined orthodox Christian doctrine.</note>—just as the ancient heretics did: Christ has said, "He who rejects you, rejects me; and he who rejects me, rejects him who sent me." <note>Luke 10:16.</note> It follows entirely that, along with those wicked heads of error, our Waldensians should likewise be excluded from the communion of the saints and the communication of the sacraments. They are by no means <insert>elect, or true participants of faith, grace, and justice in the merit of Christ toward the glory of eternal salvation</insert>. By no means should they henceforth flatter themselves with that voice of their Master <note>likely referring to their own leaders or the "serpent" mentioned on the previous page</note> which says, <insert>even if you were in seduction, the damnation of torment shall not take hold of you</insert>. 

On the contrary, those who by their own presumption have now placed themselves among the lambs shall, by the invincible judgment of Christ, the saints, and the Church, be transferred to the goats on that final day—even if, as Saint Jerome said, they have shaved their beards. <note>A metaphor for outward religious appearance or "sheep's clothing."</note>

Having addressed such matters, we have struck out their Waldensian confession in those points which seemed more serious to us. Now, we move to their epilogue...

### BOOK ONE OF THE CONFESSIONS

...let us descend [to consider their claims]. But not everything there is frivolous, nor are all the seams which they have sewn together from every side to better hide themselves behind the fox <note>original: "de vulpe." A common biblical metaphor for heretics from Song of Solomon 2:15, "Catch the foxes for us, the little foxes that spoil the vineyards."</note>; rather, we shall pursue a few items out of the many, and do so as briefly as we can. Therefore, at the very beginning, they speak thus:

->**"This, O Most Illustrious King, is the profession of our faith, which we hold in our hearts as Catholic, and which has its foundation in the scriptures of faith."**<-

Certainly, if we have said anything up to this point to refute their inventions, or to establish our own cause—the Christian cause—we have dared nothing outside the testimony of the scriptures. As far as we are aware, we have corrupted nothing, distorted nothing, and forced nothing foreign into service; we have constructed everything as whole, consistent with itself, and natural. Every uncertainty, slipperiness, and affectation—the unique plague for which we speak, and the unique defense of lies beyond which the Waldensians <note>The Waldensians (Valdenses) were a medieval religious movement that emphasized poverty and lay preaching. By the time of this text, they were often associated with early Protestant ideas.</note> could do nothing—we have shunned. Our open and pure speech stands everywhere as a witness to our open and pure mind. If they themselves could prove as much, they would have won; but far be it from falsehood to be able to prove so much. Therefore, it will soon be at the door that we shall prove those very scriptures—in which they now glory and by which those wicked men turn being a Christian into a crime—were used by them through fraud, restoring those scriptures to their own right, their true meaning, and their natural liberty.

Furthermore, they say: "Let your Majesty know that the cause of the division is not the outward forms of religion or superstitious rites. Rather, the only obstacles were to the most holy faith and its ministries. We are truly separated from that Catholic faith so that we may freely carry out the intercessions <term>suffrages: intercessory prayers or religious works offered for the benefit of others</term> and sacraments ordained by Christ."

They have not yet persuaded us that they departed from us out of a desire for a holier life, despite having sweated much over their confession. Nor will they persuade us through any other booklet—which they now again insist upon with sacrilegious animosity, coming forth into open contention, no longer as suppliants or fearing for themselves, but as victors after the King's efforts to expel them had subsided and they had been spared public punishment through the wicked intercession of someone or other. For indeed, if the Catholic faith or the Christian religion has been an obstacle to that other "faith" which those Waldensians, defiled by every foulness of error, boast of, then whoever <insert>desires to freely carry out the intercessions and sacraments ordained by Christ</insert> ought to be separated from the Catholic faith. Yet those Waldensians are convicted of violating and denying apostolic doctrine and the ecclesiastical order of the Apostles; and yet, they claim only the Waldensians freely carry out the intercessions and sacraments of Christ. But there is, as the Apostle says, "only one Lord, one faith, one baptism" <note>original: "vnus dñs, vna fides, vnū baptisma." A quote from Ephesians 4:5 used to argue for the unity of the Church.</note>. Therefore, [according to them], the blood of Christ was ineffective in prior centuries and only began to work redemption in this century among those Waldensians! 

Let us therefore recall the early Church; let us recall the promised Holy Spirit of the Father and the apostolic preaching. Let us recall this faith never interrupted for fifteen hundred years, which the martyrs confessed, and the holy Fathers, bishops of every order, priests, monks, kings, princes, peoples and cities, clergy, laity, virgins, widows, and matrons. Through fasts, continence, chastity, and abstinence from all things that make life delightful; through hair-shirts, poverty, the retreats of the wilderness, hunger, heat, thirst, cold, nakedness, and every most difficult life—let us recall that faith which God approved as acceptable to Himself by miracles astounding to all of nature. Let us recall from heaven—if indeed we believe those received into heaven out of this faith are there now, both the ancient innocents and those closer to us—Hilary, Jerome, Martin, Am<unclear>s</unclear> <note>These refer to Saint Hilary of Poitiers, Saint Jerome, and Saint Martin of Tours. The "Am..." likely refers to Saint Ambrose of Milan, common authorities cited against heresy.</note>

He contrasts their "new" faith with the long history of saints, martyrs, and miracles that support the established Church.</summary>

# AGAINST THE ERRORS OF THE WALDENSIANS AND...

...shall we condemn [saints like] Ambrose, Augustine, and Gregory, or the more recent Dominic, Francis, and that most pious father, Bonaventure? <note>These are the "Doctors of the Church" and founders of major religious orders (Dominicans and Franciscans), whom the author holds up as models of true Christianity.</note> Shall we also condemn the piety toward God and all the virtues of our most pious Prince Vladislaus? <note>Vladislaus II Jagiellon (1456–1516), King of Bohemia and later Hungary.</note> No one is found more religious than his majesty, even while wearing the royal purple, amidst the license and pride of the court; he knows nothing of Waldensian superstition. He is entirely Christian, most Christian. Let those Waldensians come forward; let them contend with His Royal Majesty. Let them show that he, because of his obedience [to the Church], seeks out "impediments" to the Christian faith, he who seeks the way to heaven by the merit of his virtues.

Consider his majesty’s brothers, those most religious princes, Casimir and Frederick. <note>Saint Casimir (d. 1484), the patron saint of Poland and Lithuania, and Cardinal Frederick Jagiellon.</note> The latter, the Most Reverend Cardinal and Bishop of Krakow, brought an unsullied celibacy from his royal cradle, his royal education, and his royal wealth. As for Casimir, while still in his youth, he fell into a terminal illness. At that time, all the physicians persuaded him that one thing alone—the breaking of his vow of chastity—would be his salvation and health. But he despised a remedy offered from such a seductive comfort. He preferred to die rather than betray his most holy vow. <note>Casimir was famously celebrated for choosing death over breaking his vow of celibate purity, a popular hagiographic story of the time.</note> Let our Waldensians—those common laborers—dare to object that the preservation of chastity amidst royal purple is an "impediment" to Christian observance, as if he had lost the comforts of this life through a vain faith and the reward of chastity in the next.

Consider Saint Francis. I mention him as one among many because he lived in very recent times, when all those things were present in the Church that our Waldensians today so bitterly accuse, and through which they even consider it a crime to be a Christian. This Francis chose the "Narrow Way" <note>original: "Artam viam." A reference to Matthew 7:14, "Narrow is the way which leads to life."</note>—not in the way our Waldensians lyingly claim for themselves, but <insert>truly the narrow way—he preferred to choose a life that was somber and mocked, which Christ the Redeemer and finally the Church, His bride, walked, though she is condemned and cast off by the world.</insert> He walked following the marked footsteps of Christ, <insert>rather than tasting and pursuing the momentary charms of the age.</insert>

Let them put forward any of their own "saints" to compare with Francis; yet Francis achieved his merit within the Church for Christ. Neither his dignities—as they call them—nor administrations, nor public customs ever hindered his innocence. He never believed that <insert>on account of some holy fear, or on account of some horror of the abyss [Hell]</insert> or because of any impediment whatsoever that might prevent him from freely serving Christ, he should strip himself of the Church. For it was in the Church that he was reborn to life, in the Church that he communed with the Body and Blood [of Christ], and it was from the gate and the keys of the Church that he passed to God once his mortality was cast off.

Therefore, whenever our Waldensians write such things <insert>as "If holy fear did not restrain us, and the horror of the abyss as well, we would embrace the liberty of the world, in which the opportunity is given to live as one wishes with all its vanities,"</insert> and in this present passage: "Moreover, let your majesty know that it is not a species of religion or superstitious rites, but only the impediments to faith that stand in our way." <insert>Whatever they say in this manner, they are lying and inventing; they satisfy themselves with hatred for our institutions. All the Christian common-folk know—and those who have fled from the Waldensians to us know—that the Church is a hindrance to no one, but rather that one's own habits hinder salvation. No one is given the liberty to live just as they wish. On this point, all of Christianity, and all public evangelical sermons from every pulpit, rebuke them, convict them, and show them to be liars.</insert>

We are taught, led, and exhorted toward virtues; we are untaught our vices. We are led away and discouraged from crime; we are corrected and argued with. We submit ourselves to the priest and confess our ignorances—and there, we are much more free. Or, if they do not understand the word: we are much more severely questioned regarding our deeds. Nothing of ours is left out. Everything stands in the hand of the priest: if we walked too proudly, if we envied a neighbor's possession, if we were drunkards, if we were brawlers, or if we acted too petulantly toward a wife—wherever we went following our own "liberty," we suffer censure for it. We stand [accountable] for what belongs to another...

Finally, if they truly wish to press us regarding liberty or any "impediment" to the most holy faith, they will not press us on the grounds that we do not more harshly restrain luxury, gambling, and the enticements of the world and the flesh—for which Christ has everywhere been a merciful physician. Rather, they will press us from the other side: that when they first conceived that falling away and heresy—that virus—among us, which they were secretly laboring to bring forth, we did not notice it. We did not rebuke that unbridled liberty of theirs, in which they clearly lived however they pleased. 

We are now convicted of having "hindered" the Christian faith because of this error—because of these Waldensians, these deserters, schismatics, seducers, mockers of the saints, and blasphemers. -> "Although," they say, "we seek true stability and immobility in the faith, nevertheless, a more certain truth, once recognized, puts to flight a detestable stubbornness." <-

Indeed, if those men held impious opinions on abstruse questions of the Law and the Prophets—questions which had either not yet been attempted or not yet resolved by the most famous ecclesiastical commentators—we would grant pardon to their error. But they err in those most manifest matters in which the whole canon of Scriptures, all their interpreters, and the judgment of the Church agree. This is the same Church that confesses these truths and has condemned these same errors in other heretics of the past. It is the truth in which the whole Christian world has hitherto consented. 

In order for those Waldensians to attack these truths, they found it necessary to falsify some testimonies of the sacred canon, pass over others, and erase others entirely. In such matters, so clearly decreed and so manifest, they certainly cannot be said to "err" accidentally; rather, they resist intentionally. They truly resist to their own destruction and to our mockery. We rebuke the fact that they transcribed certain things from the apostolic authors here, while on the very next page, the most direct testimonies against them were placed. If, therefore, they were truly working to inquire after the truth, they ought to have followed these things, not despised them, nor called into question what was not in question. But if they passed over them with their eyes wide open, then both their previous statements and the following ones they subjoin are equally "covered lies":

-> "We stand ready for human instruction and we wish to be taught from the sacred traditions of the Law; we strive to be led to a sound sense of the Christian religion, nor indeed will such labor toward us seem vain or ungrateful." <-

...whatever knowledge they offer is vain, a promise empty of truth; they mock us with these things, and with these things they keep themselves suspended away from us. This served their interests well under the fear of the King: that any private individual, whoever might finally be thought a worthy judge of such a great matter and whose opinion they would accept, could bring nothing new in so clear a matter beyond the public consensus. He would bring the same things that they currently know, the things they hear from public consensus—which they despise, mock, and to which they offer opposing views. What new discernment, then—not to say madness—would this be: that those who did not entrust themselves to the whole Christian world should entrust themselves to a private individual? 

What they promise are lies; they are trifles and mere posturings. They have so often before confessed: [**that they strive for the truth they have recognized, that they have obtained the true faith by the breath of the Holy Spirit, that they have been chosen as members of the Church, that they love Christ with clear knowledge of God and unfeigned faith, and that they have guarded all his revealed truths for eternal glory with members inspired by Him.**] Now, by a new marvel, forgetting themselves, they turn back against themselves. They suspend this recognized truth, this living faith, this clear knowledge, and this revealed truth upon human judges once again. They turn these things back against themselves; either they were vain then, or they are liars now. If they were vain then, and now they sincerely expect to be taught better things, they shall be proven guilty of wickedness: because they previously took up arms against the truth before they had explored what the truth was. Or, if they think they were truthful then, they will certainly be deceptive now. But even then—

*Nor should anyone think us to be so captured by such rash stubbornness that we would in no way yield to clear truth.*

I say: even in that, they lie to us, since they never agree with such great authors, with such authority of the Church itself, or with such consensus of all Christendom. Therefore, nothing remains for them from which they might expect a reason for clear truth. For, so we may know they expect nothing of Christian truth or salvation from our people, they confess they have made a departure <note>original: "discessionem"</note> from the Roman Church. 

But what a "departure"! It is the one the Apostle <note>Referring to St. Paul in 2 Thessalonians 2:3.</note> speaks of: *so that the man of sin may be revealed, the son of perdition, who opposes and exalts himself above all that is called God or that is worshiped.* <note>original: "vt reuclct~ hō peccati filiꝰ p̃ditionis q̃ aduerſat̃ et extollit̃ ſupra om̃e q̃d dicit̃ deꝰ aut q̃d colit̃."</note> A "happy" departure for our Waldensians <note term="Waldensians">Followers of Peter Waldo who sought a return to apostolic poverty but were declared heretics for rejecting Church hierarchy.</note>, just as I hear the Apostle: where there is a departure, there the man of sin is revealed; on that side, the son of perdition opposes God; from that side comes the departure. What then more clearly frees them from being judged as heretics <note term="heretic">Someone whose beliefs go against the established doctrine of the Church.</note> than the stubbornness of their own will? In what heresy or stubbornness we may recognize them even more clearly from these words which they add:

**"For,"** they say, **"we do not forge new dogmas or recent inventions of the Christian religion against the law of God so that we might gain honor, wealth, dignities, or popular favor. For indeed, such a thing is not characteristic of a man who is a true worshiper, but of a heretic himself, who understands neither sound faith nor the true worship of God, but rather seeks earthly and fleeting riches, which he refuses to leave of his own accord at the voice of the Lord, but defends even to the shedding of the blood of many men. But we are of a far different mind, for not only do we studiously abstain from shedding human blood, but even by divine command, we patiently cast aside our faith and fleeting wealth, praying for our persecutors, for the sake of obtaining eternal life."**

This passage is weightier than it appears to a careless reader. If anyone reviews it thoughtfully, he will see how many words feel like the stings of so many scorpions. Nevertheless, at this point, we will not uncover all its fraud—not because they do not sufficiently irritate or provoke us, but because they are still attempting every means of flight. Later, however, when they have descended from their little book into an open place, then we also shall strike through these things and everything we set aside here in one stroke with our full strength. Therefore, we shall be content for the present to show, from the testimony of the matters above, that the Waldensians...

Have they ever wished to be taught by a Christian under such a foul judgment of us? Do they not disparage with their present words? Do they not defile? Do they not tear apart? Is this concord? When they also accuse us of being greedy for human blood? 

I believe that it is through our indulgence that they live in profound peace—they who, nevertheless, because of their hatred of us which they bring forth from every page, and whose strength grows more pestilential daily according to their number, ought to have been repressed long ago in the beginning for the sake of public safety. Therefore, we endure those Waldensians—the despisers of all the saints, of the most glorious Virgin Mother of Christ (God and man), and of divine power—as if they were our greatest crime. The Lord through Moses commanded the people of Israel: "If you hear in one of your cities, which the Lord your God will give you to inhabit, some saying: 'The sons of Belial <note>A biblical term meaning "worthless" or "wicked," often used to describe those who lead others into idolatry.</note> have gone out from the midst of you and have turned away the inhabitants of your city, saying: "Let us go and serve foreign gods whom you do not know"; seek out the truth of the matter carefully and diligently. Whatever furniture there may be, you shall gather into the middle of its streets, and you shall burn it with the city itself, so that you consume everything for the Lord your God, and let it be a perpetual mound of ruin.' <note>Original: *tumulus sempiternus*. This is a direct reference to the law on apostate cities in Deuteronomy 13:12-16.</note>" By these authorities, we restore our own innocence, which those Waldensians had cast out from us even unto bloody cruelty.

However, above all the things by which I have shown their confessed hatred and their most foul judgment of us, I wish, at the end of our entire dispute, to prove by evident signs and their very own recent words, that they clearly aim for sedition and the shedding of the blood of those whom they have once come to loathe through their schism. To these schismatics—though their own affairs are still narrow and constrained—no nobility of ours, no dignity of birth, no honesty of education, nor the immense care for maintaining the fame and virtue of our ancestors has seemed holy enough to prevent them from opening the vents of such hatred against us. Yet it is from the character of these very things that our men are called to the majesty of the Purple <note>Refers to the high status of Cardinals or high-ranking secular officials.</note>, to the administration of provinces, to civil magistracies, to the miter <note>Original: *infulam*, a sacred headband or miter signifying priestly or high religious office.</note>, and to the priesthoods. They, as the vilest of men from a common tavern, treat us with every insult and, most recently, they have fashioned a hostile and clearly murderous cruelty against us. 

Indeed, if we had sated our eyes upon their tortures with barbaric pleasure; if they had been led into the arena and condemned to the beasts; if, for the investigation of their more covered blasphemies and the more hidden counsels of this new schism, we had wondered what they would finally bring forth (since we know nothing is more violent than religion in either establishing or overturning states, peoples, provinces, and empires); if, for the sake of investigating such great matters, they had been suspended on the rack <term>eculeum: a wooden rack used for torture to extract confessions</term>, their whole bodies torn with iron claws, with fire, and with "scorpions" <note>A "scorpion" was a type of knotted or spiked whip used in Roman-style punishment.</note> until their skin, flesh, and wasted health flowed down into punishments; if they had been cast back into a foul prison, into chains and shackles with bare nerves and bones; if on the following day, while their senses and wounds were still fresh, they had been dragged back to the previous day’s punishments; then, perhaps, they might have justly found cause for that atrocious name they give the authors of such an inquiry. 

But now, they are leniently guarded, as if they bore chains for a drunken brawl and not for sacrilegious impiety against God and the Church and for a seditious circumvention of the public state. Yet they so pray to the Royal Majesty that he might restrain the "cruelty" of his enemies; and not content with that, they ask that the Royal Majesty might not disdain to let them lead a mild and—as they put it—tranquil life. 

Naturally, this is so that we might nourish the "chicks" who, having become stronger, might brush the chaff into our eyes as if from a threshing floor, and so turn calamity upon our heads and those of our posterity. By these means, we have laid out the curves and the rugged paths of that famous confession of the Waldensians into a straight and level plain. In this manner, they "will" and "will not"; they wish to be everywhere exactly like themselves, yet they do not wish to be caught in it. They act as if they are coming forward, but they always keep themselves hidden behind curious words. This is proved to be in no way the duty of a "good conscience" such as they pretend to have. They deceive our simplicity; they are shifty, treacherous, and liars, exercising themselves through all evil arts. Therefore, let them by no means hereafter mock us with their feigned simplicity and innocence as they were accustomed to do before. But again, we shall show all these things from a new beginning and much more clearly.

# BOOK TWO ON CHOICE,
## ON THE CHOICE OF THE ONE AND TRUE RELIGION AND THE VENERATION OF SAINTS
### BOOK TWO,

<margin>religion</margin> Others have understood religion in different ways. We, according to its universality, might not incongruously say that **Religion** is the worship of some superior nature, which we believe has power over the fulfillment of our prayers. We consider that nothing is more ancient than religion after the creation of man, nor more true, as it was born at the same time as man. For we do not say that it began only after man was made into a "living soul," but that there, through his innate and perfect wisdom, he dedicated his first vital work of **Adoration** to God the Creator. This is consistent with what is written in the Book of Job concerning the Angels: *when the morning stars praised me together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy.* <note>Job 38:7. The author suggests worship existed even before the physical world was fully formed.</note> Certainly, it began either here or where the commandment began, when the Lord God commanded him, saying: *Of every tree of Paradise you shall eat, but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat; for in whatever day you eat from it, you shall die the death.* <note>Genesis 2:16-17.</note> Here was religion: where there was care, where there was obedience, and finally, where there was fear of nearly transgressing the commandment. This was later corrupted when, having despised their Creator, men *changed the glory of the incorruptible God into the likeness of the image of corruptible man, and of birds, four-footed beasts, and serpents.* <note>A quotation from Romans 1:23, describing the origin of idolatry.</note> But as to when that first happened, I believe it was as soon as distrust began—when the fratricide **Cain** <note>Original: *Chain*. The biblical Cain, son of Adam.</note> said to the Lord: *My iniquity is greater than that I may deserve pardon; behold, you cast me out this day from the face of the earth, and I shall be hidden from your face, and I shall be a wanderer and a fugitive on the earth.* <note>Genesis 4:13-14.</note> For how could Cain thereafter invoke the Lord, whom he distrusted and in whom he did not believe? Finally, it is written in the following passage regarding the birth of **Enos**: *he began to invoke the name of the Lord.* <note>Genesis 4:26. Enos was the son of Seth, grandson of Adam.</note> Therefore, if Enos brought the worship of the one God back into public view, we must believe it had collapsed before him. But what is confessed by all is that **Idolatry** began after the Flood, when one said to another: *Come, let us make for ourselves a city and a tower whose top may reach even unto heaven, and let us celebrate our name before we are scattered into all lands.* <note>Genesis 11:4, the story of the Tower of Babel.</note> There it is also written of **Nimrod**: *He began to be powerful on the earth, and he was a mighty hunter before the Lord.* <note>Genesis 10:8-9. Traditionally, Nimrod was associated with the building of Babel and the origin of tyranny.</note>

Therefore, the first idolatry was the worship of the elements or the celestial bodies, according to what the Book of **Wisdom** says: *vain are all men in whom there is no knowledge of God, and from these things which are seen to be good, they could not understand Him who is; nor, attending to the works, did they acknowledge who was the Artificer. But they thought either fire, or wind, or the swift air, or the circle of the stars, or the great water, or the sun and moon to be the gods that rule the world.* <note>Wisdom of Solomon 13:1-2. This deuterocanonical book was often used to explain the origins of paganism.</note> Afterward, however, other forms emerged in many ways according to the circumstances of each person. For through bitter grief, as the same Book of Wisdom says: *a father, afflicted with quickly taken away son, made an image of him; and him who had then died as a man, he now began to worship as a god, and ordained rites and sacrifices among his servants.* <note>Wisdom 14:15.</note> Then, as time intervened and the ancient custom grew stronger, this error was observed as if it were a law. The fictions of tyrants were also worshipped by the impious; and those whom men could not honor in person because they were far away, they brought their likeness from afar and made an evident image of the King whom they wished to honor, so that by their diligence they might worship the one who was absent as if he were present. The Egyptians, Greeks, and Latins transferred this lust for assigning anything to the gods onto the inventors of the arts; hence **Jupiter**, hence **Mercury**, **Minerva**, **Venus** (the inventress of prostitutes), and **Mars**, the president of arms and homicides, were placed in the heavens; hence also **Laverna**. <note>Laverna was the Roman goddess of thieves and cheats, often invoked to provide cover for their deeds.</note>
