# ON THE PRIESTHOOD AND AGAINST THE WHOLE CHURCH

You act against divine illumination. For just as in human affairs there is craftsman above craftsman, so you judge that in divine matters truth is above truth. Is this not a great delusion—as if you actually expect the Christian world to deliberate now on whether it should follow you? So many most brilliant lights have flourished among the Greeks and Latins and have set forth so much concerning the faith; they neither wished to be deceived themselves nor to deceive others. Now, having rejected and exploded these men as one, you seek new judgments again. 

Behold, therefore, for you there is all of Italy, the Spains, the Gauls, England, Germany, farthest Norway, Poland, and Hungary. Most clear-sighted Kings and most proven geniuses confess with one voice this faith which you attack. Therefore, do you stand by what was promised, or rather do you leap back? You hold these witnesses as hated and infamous; by what right, then, do you consider such great witnesses unsuitable? You who do not admit the consensus of the Christian world, what other more faithful witness will you demand? 

Lest you play the fool, you allow no one to judge such a great matter, but you exercise this judgment from your own obstinate faction. You go "hand and foot" into the blindness of the rich feaster <note>original: "diuitis epulonis," referring to the parable of Dives and Lazarus in Luke 16</note>, who himself thought the Law and the Prophets were of less credit than if someone were sent to his remaining brothers from the dead. But he was demanding a proponent of divine judgments from among the dead, whereas you have Moses and the Prophets, the Gospels and the Apostles, and their sacred interpreters. By all of these, you have been struck down until now regarding your wicked opinions, but everything seems invalid to you. You seek the judgment of another; but since you do not receive it from the living, neither shall one emerge from the underworld. 

Thus, while you promise well regarding your correction, in that same moment you strip yourselves of that promise under such a sophistry, and you defend your perfidy according to your own whim without end. How long will you limp between two sides? <note>original: "claudicatis i duas partes," a reference to Elijah’s challenge to the followers of Baal in 1 Kings 18:21</note> If the Lord is God, follow him; but if Baal, follow him. If our ways are Orthodox, follow ours; if yours, follow yours. Do not play at foreign things. 

But lest even these be notable figments: they say they speak nothing against the orthodox faith, the Blessed Virgin, and the saints of God. Why then do they suppress passages of Holy Scripture? Why do they withdraw faith from Dionysius <note>likely Dionysius the Areopagite, an early Christian theologian</note> and Aurelius Augustine <note>Saint Augustine of Hippo</note>? At the touch of an offense, they leap away. We show these people to be guilty of crimes in external matters. Do they say nothing blasphemous against the glorious Virgin and the saints? Yet what else does their whole treatment of the veneration of the saints do? 

Is it not an unbearable blasphemy that with the same sword <note>original: "macrone," a large blade</note> with which the most holy prophets struck down impure demons, they now—with a blade infected by the blood of demons, so to speak—strive to destroy the most glorious Virgin, the most blessed martyrs, and all the saints? They labor to cast them out from the devotion of mortals equally with the demon. Or is this not also intolerable blasphemy: "they trembled with fear where there was no fear" <note>Psalm 53:5</note>, just as those present do regarding the holy men and women? You, the most contaminated brothel of the devil! Do you so wickedly reproach the saints to Christian piety, and do you think this can be done without blasphemy and with impunity? For we see that such a thing cannot even be done in human affairs—if we reproach one person to another—without injury, without bitterness, and finally without notable contempt. 

You write in another place: <insert>These people are surely ignorant that we have our own priests <note>original: "suos ps̃biteros"</note> by whom we are rightly instructed and partake in the sacrament. We truly reject others for this reason: because they indeed administer the sacraments for a purpose other than what Christ intended, as the works of their ministry, which are openly against the faith, prove.</insert> 

They have admitted a remarkable barbarism from a single little word: "their own" [*suos*]. But let us set this aside; for whoever is suddenly inspired from their weeding-hooks <note>original: "sarculís," implying they are uneducated peasants or farmers</note> is accustomed to speak thus. Let us now only acknowledge the contradictions. Therefore, because you truly reject other priests, by what faith do you later revoke yourselves regarding a certain treatise of theirs on the chalice with these words: 

<insert>Whoever desires further instruction according to a healthy understanding of Holy Scripture concerning the sacrament of the body of our Lord Jesus Christ, it would greatly benefit him to read the treatise which the old Bohemians <note>The "Bohemians" refers to the Hussites, a pre-Reformation movement in Bohemia that shared some views with the Waldensians</note> wrote long ago in the hope of the good God, and holy men against their adversaries, and this with invincible testimonies of the sacred law of God, which begins thus: "To the honor in equity. To the sacrament of the body of our Lord Jesus Christ," which the adversaries of those Bohemians could not [refute].</insert>

# WALDENSIANS: BOOK FOUR

...to resist testimonies by reason and scripture. Except for the single practice of **communion under both kinds** <note>original: "sub utraque specie," the practice of giving both the bread and the wine to the laity, which was a central demand of the Bohemian Hussites</note> by which those **Bohemians** <note>the followers of Jan Hus</note> dissent from the universal Church, whatever else you write against us, you have also written against them. But even in your later confession given to the King, you openly admit that you follow a different path, being separate from both them and from us. Now you refer back to their treatises, though you obey them neither in faith nor in practice; why do you not, because of those "invincible reasons," feel the same as those Bohemians regarding the **sacrament of the altar**? Perverse men! You are constantly shifting from one thing to another just to buy favor; you have no shame, no conscience regarding your own affairs, and no loyalty in your expression. You are the very image of that "turned around" person—turned away from the right. 

But let us follow more such examples. They say in another place: [ "And we, judging that his writing will reach many who, when they read it and do not know our *Apology*, will accept his writing as true, and might thereby offend God—we therefore, fearing lest such an offense be imputed to us for our silence, judged it necessary for us to respond." ] 

**Silent dogs!** Why, I ask, did you not respond out of that same conscience to **Doctor Heinrich**, the inquisitor of heretical pravity? Did he not write a useful work against your errors? Was it not published through the art of printing? Therefore, since his writing reached many, why did you not decide to respond there too, lest those reading it be seduced by error and think ill of you, and thus offend God? But that work remained in the **Latin language**. Therefore, its reading reached only a few—people whose opinions of you you do not care about. I say you do not care, because you cannot thrust your lies upon them—since they are more knowledgeable—and you therefore fear them as being more serious critics. 

In every way, you accuse these men of being tellers of fables in your little books written for the common folk and the simple-minded. By such a **sophism** <note>a clever but false argument</note>, you remove their judgment from yourselves once and for all, and you have striven to make them appear useless so that the common people would believe you over their betters. You use the same arts here with the Christian people as in the **fable of the wolf with the sheep**. For when the sheep were led into a pact, the **mastiffs** <note>original: "Molossos," ancient guard dogs</note> were the only ones with whom peace was not convenient. The guardians of safety were removed; then, freed from the terror of the dogs, the wolves first began to slaughter the defenseless sheep. 

However, the writing of **Doctor Augustine** was issued in your **native language**; for that reason, it could very easily reach the common people. Therefore, you trembled at it all the more, because you were in immediate danger of having your reputation ruined among the populace—the only people among whom you run wild. Perhaps there is another reason why you did not respond then: in that case, you would have had to proceed along a certain path—verse against verse, reason against reason, scripture opposed to scripture. This was a greater labor and a greater sweat than you could endure. 

Therefore, you respond to Doctor Augustine—who attacked you both in general and through his *Epilogue*—so that he might provoke you, who were hiding your own **perfidy** <note>treachery or breach of faith</note> under a borrowed image, to rush out into the open. You saw that because no law of persecution was mentioned, it was left free for you to see what was being built up and by what reasoning. While you were studying how to properly send him out among the common people, you lost your treachery there. For behold: unless he had driven you out into the open with that sort of satire, what would we know of your **sacrileges** today? 

But if you have such a good conscience about your affairs that you neglected Doctor Heinrich in whatever case, behold me! I am here for every rank, and you may respond to me as I enter the lists against you, lest anyone believing our writings should begin to suspect you, and lest you suffer the penalties before God for such a reputation caused by your silence. Dare, then, to step forward, and do not think it a great or laborious task to...

# ON THE PRIESTHOOD AND THE WHOLE CHURCH AGAINST...

...that your whole Synagogue should withstand one man, you say in the next verse: <insert>[ From which everyone ought to understand that if we wanted to be cunning hypocrites and simulators, we could easily push away the things with which he presses us, and many more things to the same effect ]</insert> you say at the beginning. 

And, if I may say so in passing, you are wrong in your history. No one besides you has ever accused the **Sadducees** <note>A Jewish sect during the Second Temple period, often depicted as theological rivals to the Pharisees</note> of being "fickle" or "unstable" [mobiles]. You should have known this from **Josephus** <note>Flavius Josephus (c. 37–100 AD), a Romano-Jewish historian whose works were standard sources for ancient history in the Middle Ages</note> in the second book of *The Jewish War*: "The Sadducees are indeed fierce in their manners, and differ among themselves." Their behavior toward their own kind is as inhumane as toward foreigners. In another place, he calls them "exceedingly harsh," and especially "very cruel in their judgments beyond all other Jews." Therefore, a "fickleness of sense" could by no means be compatible with such fierce manners. 

In truth, it is the **Samaritans** <note>An ethno-religious group often contrasted with the Jews in biblical texts</note> who are noted for this vice of fickleness, as we read in the fourth book of Kings <note>Known as 2 Kings in modern Bibles. The author refers to 2 Kings 17:33-41</note>: "These nations were therefore fearing the Lord, but nevertheless serving their idols." These people, always possessed of a shifting affection, were allies in prosperity but enemies in adversity, depending on whether Jewish public affairs were faring well or poorly. We see this attested in the books of **Ezra** and **Nehemiah**, and most clearly in Josephus’s *Antiquities*, book eleven, near the very end. Indeed, he writes in these words: "For such is the nature of the Samaritans; they deny that they are kinsmen to the Jews when they are submerged in calamities, even though they are speaking the truth <note>The author suggests they only admit the truth when it suits them</note>. But when they see something bright offered to them, then they profess themselves to be partners of the Jewish race."

But enough of refuting your present ignorance; let us rather look back at the discourse we have begun. Those **Waldensians** <note>The Valdenses; a medieval heretical movement that emphasized poverty and lay preaching</note> commend their own constancy in the faith and boast that they are not at all "prevaricating" like Sadducees. If they do not do such a thing, then why, in that *Apology* to the King, did they so carefully detach themselves from our affairs? Why did they want to appear then, under the King's observation, as if they were **"of the cup"**? <term>the cup (sub calice)</term> <note>Referring to Utraquism, the practice of giving the Eucharistic cup to the laity, which was a central demand of the Hussite reformers in Bohemia. The author argues the Waldensians were pretending to be moderate Hussites to avoid persecution.</note> Why did they play along with them then and afterward? Why did they refer themselves to their treatises, when they nevertheless feel differently from them and from us? 

I began with private examples, and in private examples I shall finish. I know one of yours whom I recently challenged regarding the immortality of the soul. When a child was born to him during that time of "Royal fear," he once—with witnesses removed—immersed the infant between the nefarious hands, the complicit hands, of a Waldensian. Then, hiding the Waldensian within his home, he publicly pretended to be "of the cup." Moreover, to create belief in this simulation, on the very day of the birth, in a crowd of friends, he called for a **Schismatic priest**. Under this man, he dipped the infant in the washing of a second baptism. 

There is an estate near us, the lord of which is most devoted to Christian piety and a fierce enemy of this kind of people and their treachery. He banned their "nefarious meetings" under his jurisdiction, decreeing a penalty for those caught. It is a wonder what a silence of those men followed there; today, they want to appear as nothing less than Waldensians, and all suddenly confess themselves to be "under the cup." 

There is a certain **Lawrence of Krasonice**, whom I would not even mention by name in this writing now, were he not himself to be convicted by me for inconstancy of word based on his own letter. In it, he severely protests to **Doctor Heinrich**, the Inquisitor of heretical pravity, because Heinrich, in a certain work of his, called this Lawrence an accomplice and a leader of the Waldensian superstition. The words of the letter are: <insert>[ I saw that remarkable deed of yours, labored over by you with the greatest study and the highest vigilance, and increased and multiplied by booksellers everywhere, in which you abominate the sect of the Waldensians with dire imprecations and strive with all your strength to uproot it and remove it from the midst: and to bear with equanimity this burden of yours, though it be unequal to your shoulders: a desire for victory ]</insert>

# THE FOURTH BOOK ON THE WALDENSIANS

...if you had not joined me to their unity and—which is a more shameful kind of contempt—if you had not defamed me in an ignominious writing, claiming that I am their head and acting as an **Arch-heretic**! <note>A term used for the "chief" of a heretical group; here the author is sarcastically throwing Laurence's own accusations back at him</note> 

Therefore, Laurence, were there no envoys sent from the **Waldensians** <note>A medieval Christian movement that preceded the Reformation, often persecuted by the Roman Church for its views on poverty and apostolic authority</note> who could provide a reason for your opinion, which stands against the **Apostolic faith** and obedience? There certainly were; even your common "Synagogue" <note>original: "Synagoga" – the author uses this term mockingly to describe the Waldensian assembly or sect</note> admits this in the prologue of the work against which we are now writing. Or were you not among those envoys? You certainly were! Your own letter is a witness to this, for in it you write: 

<insert>[ When therefore these things became known to me from others, and having been warned by myself, and relying on the hope of some good coming from our mutual conference, I came with another colleague to you at the Monastery of Saint Michael in **Olomouc** ]</insert> <note>A city in Moravia, a historic region in the Czech Republic</note>

Were you not a Waldensian there? You were! And your fellow Waldensians admit this about you in that same Prologue. Moreover, you defended the Waldensian rebellion against **Doctor Henry** <note>likely Heinrich Institoris, a famous polemicist and inquisitor of the time</note>. Therefore, after all this, you shamelessly complain of "injury" alongside Doctor Henry. You lyingly claim you are not a Waldensian, and you sacrilegiously dissemble and deny the faith you presently profess. 

Behold Laurence, the primary leader of the Waldensian "Synagogue." Behold the usurper of the power of **Peter** <note>referring to the authority of the Pope, who is traditionally seen as the successor to Saint Peter</note> among his accomplices. He is a trifler worthy of God and the Holy Spirit—one who has filled the very list of priests that the Waldensians pre-defined with his own arts and lies, right down to the last thread and number. 

Thus, he is not "cunning," he is not a "hypocrite," he is not a "simulator," he is not one who—after the example of the **Sadducees**—wishes to hide his own faith (or rather his perfidy and the faction in which he has truly conspired)! I do not wish to speak here of the contradictions the Waldensians bring forth regarding the **Sacrament of the Altar** <note>the Eucharist or Holy Communion</note>, because that discussion will be examined in the internal parts of this book. I would say only this: because of their great preoccupation with earthly things, because of their great inconstancy in beliefs, and indeed because of their great and open lies, they shall be judged as no better than their "Sadducees"—and much more harmful, for they play around with a more sacred religion. 

The "innocence" which they boast is theirs according to their confession of God's will shall not deliver them from their perfidy. If they have true innocence, let them testify to it with a Christian sense, and not with mere naked words, which are nothing but a ready tool for defending wrongdoing. But since this matter is not in their hands at all—and as every tree (as they rightly quote from the Gospel) is known by its fruit—no innocence according to God, not even the smallest amount, shall be found in those tricksters regarding the impiety of their errors or the vanity of their words and deeds. 

For the Holy Spirit of discipline will flee from the deceitful. Rather, all things are as **Isaiah** says: <note>The author is quoting the Latin Vulgate Bible, Isaiah 8:12 and 30:1</note> "All that this people speaks is a conspiracy." And again: "Woe to the deserting children, that you should make a plan and not from me, and weave a web and not by my spirit." Therefore I have cried out over this. It is only pride; be still. 

Finally, we prove that the Waldensian sect does not stand by heavenly authority because it has no clear or witnessed beginnings. However, the Faith which is according to God—which runs through the triple state of the world: namely, **Nature, Law, and Gospel** <note>A traditional medieval division of history: the time before the Ten Commandments (Nature), the time of the Old Testament (Law), and the time of Christ (Gospel)</note>—has always come forth in brilliance. Under the state of Nature, its beginnings were the same as those of the world and man, which were most distinguished and beyond dispute. Then, as the malice of men grew and the plague of idolatry arose, and the primitive faith almost fell, it had to be recalled anew into the minds of men. There, it was again confirmed by frequent and stupendous miracles from heaven—the greatest and most witnessed—performed by the hand of the angels and of God’s servant **Moses**, partly in **Egypt** and at the **Red Sea**, and partly at **Mount Sinai**...

->### CONCERNING THE PRIESTHOOD AND THE WHOLE CHURCH AGAINST [THE WALDENSIANS]<-

...to the Tabernacle, and to the entry of the promised land she <note>The "legal religion" or Jewish faith</note> was recalled. Finally, however, even this legal religion, in the fullness of time, came to a halt in its course—according to what the Prophets had foretold—and having performed its sacred duties, it yielded to Christ and the Gospel that came with Him. This evangelical faith also began from the most present work of God. I do not wish to recount the virtues and the stupendous works, beyond the power of nature, of Christ our Savior and Author, and of His Apostles, of whose works the books are full. 

I prefer now to contemplate the inner marks of the evangelical faith: how it was received under Jewish contradiction and under the swords of persecutors, though it was rejected and cut down. Yet, it was preserved—and not merely in a few instances, nor by trembling and hiding itself in some single corner of the world—but, relying on heavenly confidence, with a serene brow, it confessed an undaunted faith. Overcoming all desperate difficulties—which would have been impossible if not for the Supreme Being—it penetrated into all nations and languages, from the Indians to the Spaniards, in great numbers. It brought about a miraculous conversion of souls, a shame for their former life, and the sanctification of a new rebirth. It brought into the world a most clear ray of divine regeneration. The wise men of this world—to whom the cross of Christ was foolishness <note>A reference to 1 Corinthians 1:23: "but we preach Christ crucified, to the Jews a stumbling block and to the Greeks foolishness"</note>—nevertheless, walking through the "foolishness" of the cross of Christ, marveled at this ray as something new and unusual to them. They learned secretly from the labors of our people what they used to dispute learnedly among themselves. 

At this point, if the **Waldensians** <note>original: "Valdenfes"</note> have come forth from their sect on behalf of divine decrees, they ought to have had principles similarly witnessed by divine works; such virtues should have been present among them. Therefore, if indeed they are, or ever were, kindled by the lamp of divine illumination, why does everything about them go in the opposite direction? 

First of all, they are **Headless** <note>original: "Acephali" – a term for a sect without a known leader or "head"</note> and without a leader. The very parent of the Waldensians, the devil, does not know from what source or to what crossroads he conceived them. I say it is not established who the first author of their sedition was, whether he was "black or white" <note>An idiom meaning his identity or character is unknown</note>. <margin>I suspect he was "blackened" by **shoemaker's ink** <term>Atramento Sutario: a jab at the humble, lay origins of the Waldensian movement, traditionally associated with Peter Waldo</term> or by rustic labor.</margin> 

Furthermore, they have settled in the corners of such a narrow province, hoarsely murmuring only to the unrefined common folk. It is by no means holy unless they alone, out of everyone, are allowed to be obscure; unless they alone received a lamp only to put it under a bushel basket <note>A reference to Matthew 5:15</note>. According to the Lord’s judgment, a lamp ought to be placed upon a lampstand—that is, put to a fitting use—so that it may shine for all who are in the house. Why then do you not bring forth your light, so that you might openly argue for the consensus of Christianity? For it is written: *The **Paraclete** <note>The Holy Spirit; original: "paracletus"</note> will teach you all things and suggest to you all things, whatever I have said to you.* And again: *When that Paraclete comes, he will convict the world of sin, of righteousness, and of judgment.* 

Therefore, do this: bring forth your light into the most famous cities, into the ears of princes, into the judgment of Philosophers and Theologians! Practice something of the apostolic example. **Paul**, in the council of **Festus** and King **Agrippa**, said: *"For none of these things were done in a corner."* <note>Acts 26:26</note> Why do you do nothing except from a secret corner? Clearly, to you also, "stolen waters are sweeter," as the Scripture says, "and hidden bread is more pleasant." <note>Proverbs 9:17</note> And you are ignorant that "giants are there," and his guests are in the depths of hell. 

The Law, the Prophets, the Gospels, the Apostles, and the ecclesiastical commentators of the same have conferred upon us so many mysteries concerning the faith, as many as are confirmed by the greatest testimonies of the saints. Emulate the deeds of such great authors! But truly, here you excuse yourselves: "Do not give what is holy to dogs, and do not cast your pearls before swine." <note>Matthew 7:6; the author implies the Waldensians use this verse to justify their secrecy</note> Well then: but do not think that Christ, who said this, left us anything less than the Gospel. We grant you the rest; if you have any greater secrets, send them forth for...

->### THE WALDENSIANS: BOOK FOUR <-

...some public instruction, something that we might compare to our Gospel; do not so crudely begrudge the salvation of your neighbor. Because you harbor such envy, the Law, the Prophets, the Gospels, the Apostles, and the commentators of the Church have not begrudged us their mysteries so reservedly. One of two things must be true: either you accuse them of silence regarding the things they shared, or they will accuse you for your untimely silence and for the things you did not share. Who, however, would not absolve those great authors of both Testaments, who spoke by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit? It follows that you must be seen as the guilty ones, because you have received the grace of God in vain. Like the servants of the master of the house who traveled abroad, you do not spend the commissioned **Mna** <note>A 'Mina' was a unit of currency; the author refers to the Parable of the Talents/Minas from Luke 19, where servants are judged on how they invested their master's money.</note> for holy use, but bury it in the earth even more wickedly. You deserve that rebuke: *Well done, you wicked and lazy servant* <note>original: "Euge serue male & piger"</note>; *cast the useless servant into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.* 

At last, you perceive how most unfairly you excuse yourselves and your knowledge to us from those "dogs and swine" <note>A reference to Matthew 7:6: "Do not give what is holy to dogs, or toss your pearls before swine." The author suggests the Waldensians use this as an excuse for their secrecy.</note> of yours. Indeed, if you have any familiar "Illumination"—and how much you boast of it!—then strive for the same gift as the Apostles. After receiving the heavenly gift, they immediately traveled the whole world within the span of a single human life. The most remote Indian heard them, as did the Parthian, the Persian, the Arab, the Syrian, the Scythian, the Asian, the Egyptian, the Assyrian, the Greek, the Roman, and the Spaniard at the ends of the earth. Nor did they stand for the Christian faith only in ignoble and contemptible rural areas, as if they were ashamed of the world; rather, going out against all the high places of cities, empires, and philosophers with their own strength and the strength of the Gospel, they lived in the most fitting light of the world. 

By some similar example, you should testify that your origins are kin to heaven, lest we think you mere boasters. But you say you "dread the power of the priests," who "threaten fire" and "shut the world off from you." Is it likely that the world willingly invited the Apostles to preach? Or did the Apostles not rather burst through wounds, chains, and deaths despite the resistance of the world? You, too, will conquer everything if you begin by relying on this heavenly helper. In truth, if you were full of that **must** <note>original: "musto"; 'must' is newly fermented wine. Here it refers to the spiritual intoxication of the Apostles at Pentecost.</note> with which the Apostles were filled, you could by no means be contained within those hiding places of your location and your confession. 

The Apostles were full of "must," and lest I take this word lightly, I recall the Gospel where it is written: *neither do they put new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wineskins burst and the wine is spilled. But they put new wine into new wineskins, and both are preserved.* <note>A reference to Matthew 9:17. The author argues that the new grace of the Gospel could not be contained by the "old" structures of the Waldensians.</note> The grace of the Gospel was not to be committed to the practitioners of the old Tabernacle, for it would have been endangered by the sense of the "letter." Therefore, He who put it into the tongue of **Balaam** the soothsayer to bless the people of Israel and not curse them, and He who released the voice of **Caiaphas** into prophecy—that same Spirit moved the "plectrum" <note>A small tool used to pluck a stringed instrument; here used metaphorically for the tongue.</note> of the confused multitude so that, at an unseasonable time of year (say, the month of May), they said, "These men are full of must." For a deeper power lay hidden in that voice, which the Gospel indicated above, and which **Elihu the Buzite** expressed in the Book of Job: 

*I will show my knowledge, for I am full of words, and the spirit of my belly constrains me. Behold, my belly is like must without a vent, which bursts new jars. I will speak, and I will breathe a little; I will open my lips and respond. I will not accept the person of man, nor will I equate God to man.* <note>Quoting Job 32:17-21. Elihu was the younger friend of Job who spoke after the others, claiming he was bursting with divine insight.</note> 

Therefore, the Apostles, full of the new grace of the Gospel, did *not accept the person of man*, but they breathed out into the open. They said to their threats: *If it is right in the sight of God to listen to you rather than to God, you judge. For how can we not speak what we have seen and heard?* Divine grace was boiling over entirely and overflowing; it was not able to contain itself within itself. Indeed, it poured out its own power and flavor from the evangelical vessels of the Apostles into the whole world. Thus, most happily for the whole world...

# ON THE PRIESTHOOD AND THE WHOLE CHURCH AGAINST [HERESIES]

The prophecies of that Psalm:
> *Their sound has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.* <note>Psalm 19:4. The author uses this to show that the true Gospel is universal, not hidden in small sects.</note>

And that of Isaiah:
> *It is too little that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob and convert the remnants of Israel; I have given you as a light to the nations, that you may be my salvation even to the end of the earth.* <note>Isaiah 49:6.</note>

These most blessed prophecies, I say—once that other era (which was certainly unfortunate for the nations) had ended, when:
> *God was known only in Judea; his name was great in Israel* <note>Psalm 76:1. The author is contrasting the localized religion of the Old Testament with the universal reach of Christianity.</note>

—broke forth through the Apostles across the whole world. These things ought today to be spread even further by the same Spirit through the Waldensians; but in truth, they have retreated further back. If we were to yield to Waldensian boasting, the knowledge of God would have finally departed from the world entirely and been cast back into its old narrowness:
> *God is known only in the Waldensian; His name is great among the Pighards.* <note>A mocking parody of the previous Psalm, suggesting the Waldensians have shrunk God's kingdom down to just their own small group.</note>

Let learned ears forgive me for this barbaric word; certainly, I myself am ashamed of this term **Pighard** <term>Pighardus: A derogatory name for the Bohemian Brethren or Waldensians, often associated with the term "Picards."</term>, and I have long ignored it. But here I could no longer avoid it. Therefore, since I have overcome my shame once, I will continue to use this name "Pighard" from now on—a name rightfully owed to those men. For men who are hateful to the Roman See deserve names that are hateful to Roman ears. But let us hasten at last to bring an end to this matter. Christ says to those who would believe in him:
> *Behold, I am with you even until the end of the age.* <note>Matthew 28:20.</note>

Certainly, by this one voice, all heresies are powerfully banished from the Catholic confession. For where were Simon Magus, where was Cerinthus, Manicheus, Arius, or the Pighard—where were all those who were born later out of contention? They were still being cooked in the loins of the devil, their father. Therefore, they fall short of Christ as their author and of this one legitimate beginning from which alone the life-giving faith ought to descend. 

They are themselves witnesses against themselves in our discourse. One says his author is a sorcerer <note>Referring to Simon Magus, often cited as the first heretic.</note>; another names Cerinthus; a third, Manicheus. Individual heresies confess they took the beginnings of their dogma from individual inventors who came after Christ. Even those Pighards no longer call themselves Christians, testifying by that very name that they do not come together under Christ as their author, but under a new and recently discovered beginning. By what help, then, will these heresies defend themselves for their salvation? They are unknown to Christ. They have fabricated things concerning the faith contrary to what the Apostles learned from Christ, and contrary to what Christians learned from the Apostles under the tradition of the faith. 

For example, so you may grasp the matter: that phrase was not in the Church of God before Arius: 
> *There was a time when he was not,* 

signifying that the Son is less than the Father. Arius was the first to introduce this. <note>The central claim of Arianism, which argued that Jesus was a created being rather than co-eternal with God the Father.</note> Therefore, Christ could not have been in them. Without Christ—who alone is the Savior and the propitiation for the sins of the world—could there be a life-saving faith in them? Or will they have a life-saving faith in Christ when they hold views different from the Apostles and their succession? Christ cannot be split into discordant confessions. 

Therefore, when he said to the Apostles, *I am with you until the end of the age,* did the Apostles hear only "naked words" while the later fabricators of novelties received their actual power? Let us suppose they did receive it: but since they do not even agree among themselves, and Christ cannot be divided at all, a great quarrel will arise among them: which heresy of them all is the only one to claim Christ for itself based on these words? 

Again, if by the power of his promise Christ was not with the Apostles, and was only going to come to those later groups, then that saying *I am with you* would no longer fit; instead, it would be another phrase about the future: *I will be with you.* But was he then with the Apostles? Unless he remains thereafter in that succession, that other phrase *until the end of the age* will not fit; instead, it would be some substitute like: *until Manicheus,* or *until Arius,* or *until the Pighard,* or *until the Antichrist.* For even the Antichrist, to be thought true, will defame the Church of God as based on the error of a false faith—just as all heresies together defame the Church. From such great things—from prophetic prediction, from heavenly inspiration, from certain and witnessed beginnings from heaven—[they reduce] the matter of that Pighard into superstition...

He asserts that if Christ promised to be with His Church "always," then any sect appearing centuries later with different doctrines must be of the devil.</summary>

# THE WALDENSIANS: BOOK FOUR

...poured out this shameful and most damned heresy. It proceeded from no divine calling, but from a conspiratorial faction. Just as in the past, Montanus, along with the mad women Prisca and Maximilla, boasted with a most impudent lie—contrary to the very certain history of the *Acts of the Apostles*—that the mission of the Holy Spirit was fulfilled in them and not in the Apostles. In that history, among other things, the very words by which the false Montanus is refuted are written:

> *And eating together with them, he commanded them not to depart from Jerusalem, but to wait for the promise of the Father, "which you have heard," he said, "from my mouth; for John baptized with water, but you shall be baptized with the Holy Spirit, not many days from now."* <note>Acts 1:4-5. The author uses this to show that the Spirit was promised immediately to the Apostles, not centuries later to new leaders.</note>

Montanus cared nothing for these "not many days," but three hundred and thirty years later, he falsely claimed this promise was first fulfilled in himself. He was a madman, suggesting that Christ deceived the Apostles for the sake of his own opinion, that He did not fulfill what was promised to them, and finally, that the Apostles were not baptized by the Holy Spirit. If that were true, the great things they did were done without God as their author, and they would have ultimately transgressed Christ's command. They would have left Jerusalem before the permitted time and filled the world with the Gospel prematurely. Such most impure retreats—from which both the ear and a more chaste mind recoil—are characteristic of heretics who, being outside of Christ and the Church, are accustomed to claim divine illuminations for themselves.

After we have reviewed these things regarding the "Pighard" <note>A derogatory term for the Waldensians used by their opponents.</note> and his beginnings, let us now at last return with better faith to the words he recently spoke to us regarding the observance of his Synagogue. They propose that they keep those constitutions which are an aid to faith, love, hope, and justice, as much as can be known from faith. For that same reason, they admit they despise our institutions—not because they were humanly established, but for other reasons.

Nonetheless, lest a too-great novelty provoke too much hatred against them among the common people if they differed in everything, they profess to "play along" with us. They do this by observing many things which they know to be, for the most part, against justice, and which they would by no means do if left to their own free will. For instance, they observe feast days and fasts which they did not ordain themselves, interpreting them in the best sense they can. For they think there is no deception anywhere that cannot be clothed in a specialized appearance of piety. Thus, while they walk a middle path between their constitutions and ours, they think that in such great pretense <note>original: *simulatione*</note> they have maintained the best stewardship toward both God and man.

I have expressed this in a longer period <note>A complex grammatical sentence structure.</note> because on this point they are vehemently ambiguous with slippery words and meanings. Let us now discern these things. Let us begin from the last points and come to the first. They say that for the sake of both discord and bad example—lest they provoke the anger of the people against themselves—they preserve many of our customs, even contrary to their own opinion. 

If, therefore, our ways are "evil," and as evil as they have said—calling them "causes of idolatry, vain superstition, robbery, the overturning of faith, and the transgression of the commandments of God"—if they are so deadly to the conscience of the Pighard, he himself will never be right to observe such atrocious and impious things on the brink of ruin. Therefore, by pretending to observe them, his "simulation" will not be excused from the crime of sacrilege. 

That Pighard—that singular imitator of apostolic custom—did not seek out that hypocrisy from the primitive church. He claims to know the institutions of that church better than the reading of our ancestors, as if he can sniff them out, being more keen-scented than both a dog and a goose. The Apostle says:

> *I have become all things to all men: a Jew to the Jews, a Greek to the Greeks, that I might win them all.* <note>1 Corinthians 9:20-22.</note>

Does this mean he would recline at the statues of demons? It is a sin to say it, and further, most wicked to even think it. While he did not burden believers from the Gentiles with legalistic observances, he did not forbid those same things to the Jews for a certain time and in a certain manner. For the Synagogue, which had once been made holy by its laws, was not to be suddenly cast out as if [it were profane...]

# ON THE PRIESTHOOD AND THE WHOLE CHURCH AGAINST...
<meta>catchword: I think</meta>

...not as something impure, but having fulfilled its status, it was to be carried out to its burial dutifully and mercifully. Nonetheless, the Apostle always most constantly testified to both Jews and Gentiles that a man had fallen away from the grace of the Gospel whoever observed the sacraments of the Synagogue, its offerings, and its purifications as if they were necessary for salvation. Therefore, in this matter, you are prevented from rightly imitating the Apostle. As we have now shown from the Scriptures in more than one place, the Church cannot cease in the same way the Synagogue did, so that you might slip in from your own sacred rites. Furthermore, the purifications according to the ritual of the Law, which Paul completed upon coming to Jerusalem, were not impure from their very root; they were merely emptied of their power through the Cross of Christ. You, however, have condemned our rites from the very root, just as you condemn idolatry. Therefore, you cannot, according to your own conscience, ever simulate our rites—which you consider so impure—for any period of time (for instance, as long as you remain in these narrow straits of locations and accomplices) according to any example of the ancient Christians. Christians living among pagan religion, in order to purchase peace for themselves with their neighbors, surrendered nothing of the integrity of the Christian rite; they practiced nothing similar to a lying and wicked display. They did not think that any fairness was to be sought in pagan seduction, so that while remaining themselves in secret, they would have served public eyes externally as well—such as fasting at the death of Apis <note>The sacred bull of ancient Egypt.</note>, or celebrating the *Februa* <note>A Roman purification festival.</note>, the *Quinquatria* <note>A festival to Minerva.</note>, or the *Saturnalia* <note>A major Roman winter festival.</note> in like manner. 

The Pighard <note>A pejorative term for members of the Bohemian Brethren or Waldensians.</note> has pushed us away from the veneration of the saints and from the adoration of the Sacrament of the Altar, all the way into pagan superstition. Because he thinks us to be in such blasphemous seduction—and this pertains to the truth, for "what accord has Christ with Belial?" <note>A quote from 2 Corinthians 6:15, implying there can be no compromise between Christ and the devil.</note>—he himself cannot, in the midst of our great and intolerable error, gather anything good or fair, or anything holy, nor could he use his own simulation under the appearance of right. But let us grant the Pighard his simulation regarding our affairs, by whatever right he holds it. We lead festive days, and he leads them too. We go out again to work, and he goes out after us. We fast, and he fasts. We eat again, and he eats. We bow to the Crucified One—and he, though rebuked, bows too. Truly he does all these things against his own institutions; yet he does them before our eyes lest, by his will, he be the cause of discord and a bad example. 

Hey you, Pighard! You feel that discord is an evil. You feel that a bad example must not be given. "I judge you out of your own mouth, you wicked servant" <note>Luke 19:22.</note>. For if you did what you do in part for the sake of a good deed, how much more would you have done it for the sake of a full good deed if you did it in total? You take care to avoid causing discord or providing a bad example regarding a fast or a feast day, as you say. Why do you not take care, as a total Pighard, to avoid causing discord and providing a bad example? But you, contrary to your conscience, thus prevaricate between the two. Inconstant and fickle, you hide your hypocrisy and practice that "Sadducee" of yours—or rather our "Samaritan" <note>The author compares the opponent to the Samaritans, who were viewed as religious half-breeds or heretics by the Jews.</note>—toward us, so that you may walk more securely between us and your own treachery. 

You propose examples of fasts and feast days by which you might win our favor. I recognize those; they are mere trimmings upon your sacrileges regarding the veneration of the saints. I pray, let it be permitted there, by your judgment, for the Christian people to be afflicted over the martyrdoms of the saints by the same right that it was permitted for the ancients to be afflicted over the death of Aaron, Moses, the woman Judith, Judas Maccabaeus, and Stephen, the first martyr of Christ. 

Now I return to your constitutions. You do not say what nature or what number these are. Therefore, it is not so much what you *do*—which is difficult to track—but rather what has been tracked is even more difficult: to stand in open confession. What will I have to inspect regarding what you *do not* do? You do not perform all the ceremonies which you previously accused us of. These things, therefore, we have proved from the opposite side that we do by right, so that henceforth we may not know more of your affairs. Yet there, by one work, your own claims have in turn collapsed. For those things which we do by right, you certainly omit by injury. There are, however, a few of your things which I know are separate from ours, which will be the works to be examined individually at present. Before all other things, you have stripped off the Christian name, I think...

### WALDENSIANS BOOK FOUR

->Y<-

...since even that was an obstacle to the help of faith, as you say, and to love, hope, and justice. It did not assist, I believe, in the worship and veneration or the right prayer to God; it did not contain equity, virtue, honor, discipline, and unity. Therefore, you cast out the "Christian" name. Why that name? Was it lest you stir up the people’s anger against you and voluntarily become a cause of division and a bad example? Did you not retain it along with the feast day and the fast? But you found no appearance of equity in it, so that you could use the Christian name in some way for justice—as you say again—and for good sense. Behold, then: the **Pighard** <note>A derogatory term used by Catholic polemicists for the Bohemian Brethren, derived from "Picards."</note>.

But you are angry that you are "clothed in a certain name"—those are your own words—and so you are, in your own translated and splendid terms, "clothed in what is contemptible and false." You are unjustly angry; for if you wished to be addressed honorably, you should have remained a **Christian**. I ask you, Pighard, tell me: by what name will you confess Christ before a tribunal, if the case requires it? You will say, "I am a Pighard." You would no more have confessed Christ by an alien name than you would have confessed Jove <note>The Roman god Jupiter; the author implies the name "Pighard" is as pagan or "other" as a Roman deity.</note>.

But perhaps, as it now occurs to you, you will call yourself a **brother**. Read **Tertullian** <note>An early Christian author from Carthage (c. 155 – c. 220 AD).</note> in his *Apology to the Roman Judges*; you will find that even this name is not the symbol of a Christian confession. No martyr ever confessed for Christ by any name other than "Christian." No other name was capital <note>punishable by death</note> for those who confessed for Christ in times of persecution. For there is no strength in the name of "brother" beyond the custom of the Jewish people. The Jews, since they descended from the twelve brother Patriarchs, addressed themselves in this specific way to remember their origin. Thus **Paul** calls his accusers and those who laid snares for his safety—with whom he had nothing in common in Christ—"brothers." Indeed, in another place, in the catalog of his sufferings, he adds "perils among false brothers," following that same custom. Because it is a name of particular equality, is it not used in the church both then and today in daily, familiar speech? For such a common use, we could even admit it in a Pighard. But because he hides under it something that is not Apostolic, and because he makes a division under this token, it is displeasing and is not admitted without its own infamy.

So, will you give your confession of faith to a tribunal? Should you say, "I am a brother," you would no more have confessed Christ than the Synagogue. There were once **Photinians**, **Sabellians**, and **Arians** <note>Three groups declared heretical by the early Church for their differing views on the nature of the Trinity and Christ.</note> who followed your example. You have recently come forward as a "brother" by their example in turn. The Church never recognized those former groups; certainly, she will not recognize you as a "brother." For he is a traitor to his Lord who, when called to confess Him, confesses under a name alien to his Lord. Whoever, through hatred of the Christian name, fashions another name for himself, is a stranger to the Apostolic foundation.

Saint **Ignatius**, the most blessed martyr and a listener to the Apostles, is my witness. In his *Letter to the Magnesians*, he writes this regarding the Christian name: "Let us therefore be made worthy of the name we have received. For whoever is called by another name besides this one is not of God, for he does not receive the prophecy saying of us: 'Because he shall be called by a new name which the Lord called him, and it shall be a holy people.'" <note>original: *Efficiamur ergo digni cognomento quod accepimus...*</note> This was first fulfilled in **Antioch of Syria**, where the disciples acquired the name **Christian** through Paul and Peter founding the Church. Listen, Pighard, to the power of the Christian name. Hear your crime, that you have denied it. Hear that you have been made a stranger to the salvation which is in Christ Jesus.

Let us weigh the rest. The next institution of the Pighard is that in their synagogues <note>A dismissive term for the meeting houses of the Brethren.</note> they use profane <note>meaning "ordinary" or "common," rather than specially consecrated</note> clothes to perform their sacred rites. Did they perhaps catch a scent of this from the wind of Apostolic times? Certainly, their noses deceived them. **Polycrates**, the Bishop of the Ephesians, proves they are false when speaking of the celebration of Easter in these words: "We celebrate the day as immovable, neither adding anything nor diminishing anything." This opinion was followed by **Philip**, who died at Hierapolis, and **John**, who leaned upon the breast of the Lord...

He also attacks their use of ordinary clothing for religious services, citing early Church fathers to prove that sacred traditions should remain unchanged.</summary>

### ON THE PRIESTHOOD AND THE WHOLE CHURCH AGAINST

...rested, and his High Priest was there, bearing a golden plate upon his forehead. Behold, in the Church of God, there is a noble priesthood with a golden plate; but what golden plate? That which was on the priestly headband <note>Original: *infula*, a headband worn by priests as a sign of religious consecration.</note> of which we read in Exodus: "And they made the plate of sacred veneration of purest gold, and wrote upon it in the work of a jeweler 'Holy to the Lord,' and bound it to the miter with a hyacinth-colored ribbon." <note>Exodus 28:36–37 and 39:30–31.</note>

But regarding these things, we said more earlier when we were asserting our case against this **Pighard** <note>A derogatory term for the Bohemian Brethren.</note>. Let our Pighards have them, then; I say, let the "Apostolic" ones have them. If they perform sacred rites in profane clothing—garments that come from lawsuits and market-dealings, in which they have slandered, been injured, and lied to the judge—do they thus think they are helped toward worship, veneration, and right prayer to God? If they approach the performance of sacred rites in the same garment in which they lay down in their wives' bosoms? 

Let us take up another point: they prepare the Communion of the altar from leavened bread <note>Original: *de fermento*. The use of leavened bread was a point of contention; the Roman Church used unleavened bread, while the Eastern Church and some reform groups used leavened.</note>; they take it like a bone from a dish. Does this not also contain some measure of equity, virtue, and honor? Did they not take this from the Apostles, or the Lord’s Supper, or from some treatise of theirs concerning the chalice, upon which there would be invincible reasons? Not at all! Why then did they not revere those invincible reasons, but instead, with a hardened forehead <note>Original: *protrita fronte*, an idiom for being shameless or impudent.</note>, ignoring them, they accepted a foreign custom from some **Ruthenians** <note>Eastern Slavic Christians (Orthodox), who used leavened bread for the Eucharist.</note> and from **Judas Iscariot**? 

Judas, the betrayer of Christ, accepted the moistened morsel <note>Original: *buccellam*, the piece of bread dipped in wine.</note> lifted from the wine. I provide you with proof of this statement from the Gospel; there it is read: "And when he had dipped the bread, he gave it to Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, and after the morsel, Satan entered into him." When, therefore, he had accepted the morsel, he went out immediately. <note>John 13:26–30.</note> Thus do the Pighards receive the sacrament with Judas the betrayer, they whom it pains to receive it with the Apostle Peter. And so they immediately go out from the Church, just as he went out from the college of the Apostles. 

Furthermore, they say they observe such things as pertain to "right prayer to God," as if we were ignorant of right prayer! Thus they mention some other "right prayer" on their own part. And truly they say that they make their own prayers. How much more easily might they remain with the Psalms—which the Church, by the institution of the Apostles, uses in every divine office—and remain Pighards? Even in the most ancient and prophetic times, the Jews were compelled—these are the words of **Eusebius** <note>Early Church historian and Bishop of Caesarea (c. 260 – 339 AD).</note> from the twelfth book of the *Preparation for the Gospel*—to accept no other hymns and odes than those composed by the Holy Spirit through the prophets. Again: among the Jews, even in ancient times, the judgment of divine songs was not handed over to the multitude, but there were some—though very few—judging these things by the divine Spirit. To them alone was it permitted to consecrate, so to speak, and approve the books of the prophets; and those things which seemed foreign to the Holy Spirit, they were to disapprove and reject.

Most piously, therefore, would the Pighards also remain with the Psalter—unless the Psalms are not "right prayers"? Or unless the Pighards make more divine things than the Prophet **David**? Do they wish, therefore, to use "soliloquies" <note>Personal, private prayers.</note> other than the Psalms? Why then did they not adopt the *Meditations* and *Soliloquies* of Saint **Augustine**? And surely, if such a thing was to be done, every matter has its own mastery, and there will be a prepared discipline for this work, through which more faith is deferred to a Doctor of the Church than to an unlearned man <note>Original: *ydiote*, from the Greek *idiotes*, meaning a commoner or person lacking professional knowledge.</note>, and to a bishop than to the profane, and to Saint **Augustine** than to a **Pighard**, so that he might discern what and in what manner such a thing ought to be done toward God. For if these are the words of the great **Athanasius** <note>Bishop of Alexandria and defender of Orthodoxy (c. 296 – 373 AD).</note> regarding the Psalm: "Whoever says anything beyond what is right, let him fall into impiety." For an account must be given before the Judge not only for deeds, but for every idle word.

But those Pighards exercise a wicked rashness, showing contempt not only for the divine office which is spoken, but also for that which is sung at improper times. And they say in that writing of theirs concerning the veneration of the saints: "Nor is it true that we have no song concerning her, for we sing many enough songs about her." If, therefore, they receive song among sacred things, why not our divine office instead? Since they only accept what is taken from the places of the sacred canon, why do they fashion new things for themselves from whatever brain? Or by what faith do they reject what the leaders of our religion—and before others, **Ambrose** and **Gregory**, men of confessed holiness—instituted...?

# THE WALDENSIANS: BOOK FOUR
<center>Y ij</center>

Why should they not be condemned for human fictions, they who neglect [ancient traditions] for human inventions? The trivial songs of the **Pighards** <note>A derogatory term for the Bohemian Brethren, or Unitas Fratrum, whom the author links to the Waldensian heresy.</note>, unknown to ancient holiness, which have neither face nor body, neither juice nor nerve—should they not be condemned for these human figments? They hold up "human inventions" against us everywhere. Therefore, in this corruptible world, what does God *not* do through human beings? The Law was given through **Moses**, prophecy was written by men, and God performed miracles through men. He founded the Gospel through the man **Christ** and the **Apostles**, and spread it throughout the world; He governs the earth through **Kings**; and finally, what is there anywhere, since the world’s creation, that God does not establish through human agency?

I am not afraid to confess—and after such great examples, it is without danger—that the most ancient **Greeks**, the Bishops throughout **Jerusalem**, **Antioch**, **Alexandria**, and **Caesarea**, established ecclesiastical chant in the beginning. Later, the Roman Church, and those of **Milan**, **Carthage**, **Hippo**, and all of Africa and the West, adopted this chant. There were certain authors, and those who had the right to establish such things by their rank; and these were not common things, nor made according to anyone’s sudden whim, but they organized passages from both Testaments under the form of the Divine Office. 

The **Pighard**, who pretends to follow the most ancient traditions and to receive the canon of the Scriptures, fails on both counts. If he wanted to be faithful to the Word, he ought not to have rejected the ecclesiastical office from himself, whether it was spoken or sung. But he did reject it. Who, then, does not understand the iniquity of the Pighard? Since, as we have shown, it is necessary to follow human authority even from the institutions of the Church, by the truest right: the Theologian will stand above the one ignorant of letters, the Christian above the Pighard, **Ambrose** and **Gregory** <note>St. Ambrose and St. Gregory the Great, traditionally credited with organizing the chants of the Western Church (Ambrosian and Gregorian chant).</note> above those black and white concubinaries and eunuchs <note>Original: *concubinarijs & exectis*. A harsh polemical insult suggesting the Pighard leaders were morally corrupt or physically/spiritually deficient.</note>, and the entire most august order of Bishops will stand above every smelly tradesman <note>Original: *sellulario*, one who works a sedentary or manual craft, often used dismissively in this period for the "unlearned" classes.</note> for the sake of establishing authority. Therefore, they do not harm us even a point regarding "human inventions" where they do not first destroy themselves. But let them perceive that in this, as in all things, the Pighard differs from the Christian, and the heretic from the apostolic. 

Yet, it would not have been foreign to modesty—if they knew any—not to blame in our practices what was taken from the example of our ancestors. The songs which were written either in Moses or in the books of Judges and the Psalms were dedicated to God with measure, numbers, and rhythms, and with drums and musical instruments. And this was for a very great reason: for just as the body is dull without help, so the soul flags without rhythms and numbers. Indeed, these rhythms turned the soul around, transposed it, and caused it to pass into the contemplation of those things said in the songs. 

The wild agitation of **Saul**, whenever he was vexed by an evil spirit, was refreshed by **David** playing upon the lyre. **Elisha**, while following the camps of the three Kings against **Moab**, ordered a minstrel to be brought to him so that his spirit might be drawn forth into a prophetic trance. For this reason, the prophet wished to meditate upon the divine song—and that by which he might summon his soul above itself—not silently to himself, but to music. That is, he understood the power of harmony, which alone commands the souls of mortals. I say "alone," and do not catch me on the word, for even God—who truly alone commands souls—does not force His power upon you if you are discordant, unless you have composed yourself from a kindred symbol <note>An allusion to the "harmony of the spheres" or the idea that the human soul must be in tune (harmonized) to receive the divine.</note>. Therefore, even those masters of speech, the prophets <note>Original: *vates*, a term for poet-prophets.</note>, used oratory bound by numbers. Even those who speak in the forum and in court cases have especially wished to settle into the minds and ears of the judges by means of those things that touch upon musical composition and delivery. 

For these great reasons, chant was also received into the Divine Office. But if the Pighard—though we require nothing from him and gladly grant him his own ignorance—smelled less of "phlegm" <note>Original: *pituitā*, used here to mean dullness or stupidity.</note>, he ought to let be what he himself does not grasp, and not rashly or without investigation condemn the wisdom of the ancestors, but rather revere their judgment and authority. He should think that these men established nothing foolishly, rashly, or in a way not to be imitated. But they sin by a certain vice of their nation; we indulge ourselves more than is right, we are wise beyond our strength regarding God, heaven, faith, and obedience, even when a judgment must be made on a deep and profound matter...

# ON THE PRIESTHOOD AND AGAINST THE WHOLE CHURCH

Let no foreign advisor present himself here; let all things stand by our own judgment. We have already heard the institutes of a gentler custom; let no one be a nuisance to us after this. From that conscience, let them cease to act fiercely toward others by our merit. They do not know the same things we do; whoever, because of long usage, carries out all the better discipline equitably and modestly, feels deliberately about their own affairs and permits themselves to be guided by the judgment of others. They listen. This headlong presumption and contempt for the judgment of others have brought heresies and rebellions upon us. From this single knot, obedience could be stripped away, and the church could be trampled. For we disdain to admit into our senses anything that we ourselves did not conceive. Just as that **Pighard** <note>A derogatory term for the Bohemian Brethren, whom the author views as heretical.</note>, although he claims to revoke the institutes of the ancestors—where, then, is the faith, judgment, and authority of the ancients? Did they seem so great to him that reverence for them would cause his stubbornness to yield?

From the beginning up to this point, we have found him to be a disguiser of ancient holiness, a denier of Christian piety, and stubborn in his ways through all things. Now he detracts from the divine office and the chant, clearly out of a rustic brain. For that **Pighard**, returning from the dunging of the field and from every most base labor—from where would chant come to him? I speak of **Chant**, at whose artistry human music—which otherwise in our century has reached perfection and surpassed all antiquity—is stunned. Music confesses that this part of itself is above human faculty; it yields to itself and gives itself the palm <note>The "palm" signifies victory or excellence.</note> over itself. I am too small to be able to explain how great the power of that music is, based on **Arsis and Thesis** <note>original: "ab Arſi & theſi". These are technical terms for the rise and fall (upbeat and downbeat) of a musical or poetic rhythm.</note>, by which it surpasses all oratorical pronunciation. And it fits itself so perfectly to the virtue of the sentences, so preserves the decorum of the person, that it seems born and drawn out from the sense of what is being sung there, not imposed from elsewhere; it is perceived as a blood-relation to the words, not a stranger. If this **snotty-nosed Pighard** <note>original: "Mucoſus Pighardus". A harsh insult regarding the subject's lack of refinement or "low" physical state.</note> understood these things, he would never so rashly either detract from ecclesiastical chant or substitute his own adulterated versions.

But they say, "We act by your example; you also are accustomed to use vernacular songs <note>Hymns in the common language of the people rather than Latin.</note> during the sacred rites of the altar." Here they strike us in the face enough. But to defend the matter against them: not **Germany**, not **France** and **Spain**, nor the seat of religion, **Italy**—not even the principal cities of **Moravia**—is so bold and ignorant as to corrupt the divine office with vulgar fictions. They carry out this corruption through the countryside, marketplaces, and ignoble towns; namely, so that we may retain something to remind us of our present location, lest everything around us be found too "urban." I compel you Christians: you are corrupting the divine office! It was not established rashly, as you think, nor according to anyone's whim—as if whatever pleased someone was received into use. It is known to be a formal Institution. You think poorly of the Church. Whatever she does, she does by great and legitimate authors and reasons, the likes of which you have not yet reached. **Councils** and **Popes**, in whose hands is the right of sacred things, decreed these matters based on **Apostolic reception**. You are far too bold, making a matter of another’s power into your own right. Consider, however, what you would bear with indignation if someone made themselves powerful over your private family property, and abused your institutions there for their own rashness. 

Ah, you are too confident in yourselves! Even if you did not sin in many other things, yet you sin even here. You provide a downfall for the **Pighard**, who, while he refuses to follow you in other matters of your piety, nevertheless defends this error of his by your authority. But what are they, I ask, these songs that have such power among you? Surely they are like the "medicines of the common folk," gathered by filthy and most ignorant men! And if you were to greet them on a journey, you would disdain to return the greeting because of their filth. Consider, therefore, what should rightly make you ashamed: that you, who distinguish yourselves from others by your noble birth, here hold those most contemptible things in such high regard that you follow their fictions. You make yourselves inferior. Ah, open your eyes, unless you are blind because of your nobility! Think whether it becomes you more to follow a **Bishop** or someone who barely knows his letters. But it is worthwhile to call some of these songs into this present place, so that it may be understood what things we are currently indignant about.

# WALDENSIANS BOOK FOUR

->Hail, heavenly and pious hierarchy, divine monarchy of God, look upon us so that we, erring on the path, may be rescued. Blessed Mary, teach us the pleasing mandates of the new law. O noble and uncorrupted Virgin, make us keep what is decreed. Divine grace from the highest end, queen of virgins, offer us forgiveness; quickly incline your ear hither. Full of sweetness, bring loving gifts, the explanation <note>original: "glossa"</note> of our law. Be not hateful to those who seek you, gracious mother. The Lord formed Adam who sinned; He expiated that evil when He called you and blessed you in the womb. With you He redeemed us, the world which He set free. He who crushed the Devil <note>original: "Zabulon," a term occasionally used in medieval Latin to denote the devil or a poetic reference to the tribe of Zebulun interpreted as "dwelling of strength"</note> and came into the world, so that He might nourish us after He redeemed us. Blessed alone from the heavenly school, strain us from the dregs; purifier and millstone of our crime.<-

**Song.** In the beginning of the start of light, Mary was shown beforehand, signified by obscure figures. Let the people of the Orthodox churches commend her with heart and voice in joy, so that she does not stand in a cloud. This is the first law, the most celebrated law, introducing the sun, putting to flight foul errors. The heavenly bow and witness of the covenant, the strength of the fearful, Mary brings pardon to the shaggy <note>original: "crinosis," likely referring to those in mourning or the "hairy" sinners in need of cleansing</note>. A slender cloud ascends easily to the Lord Savior, bedewing with power, giving hope to the sinner. Naomi, Mara, sweet and bitter; feeding a sweet child, bitter while weeping under the altar of the cross. She is an exorcist, priest, and psalmist by restraining demons, by absolving those who pray after sinning. She is the throne of God my judge, pious for your protection, to appease the avenging judge. Such a hostess, none equal to her, special to the Lord, general to angels and us. A veil of hyacinth girt with the flesh of Christ, by which we ask to be covered from wrath, lest we be treated with violence. A bag of treasure <note>original: "Saccus thesauri"</note>, not of silver or gold but of our liberty, by which we are truly free for nothing. A horn of oil, the anointing of faith of the Christian order, having performed which we are made whole. A flask of wine of divine love, in which she obtains that we may be inebriated and commands that we be blessed.

These are two of the better ones and those they sing in Latin; first, because they lack all those things I discussed before regarding the dignity of the ecclesiastical office and chant; then, they are common in sense and worn out—shamefully so in words—with no rhythm in their structure. It begins everywhere, it ends everywhere; mere portents of things and words. Or is that not from the middle of the "Vault"? "A bag of treasure, not of silver or gold"—whoever that was, he was most filthy. He read Paul, the **vessel of election** <term>vessel of election: A traditional title for the Apostle Paul (from Acts 9:15), signifying a chosen instrument of God.</term>, and wanted to transform something similar himself; but there his narrow brain found nothing equally capable, and the slave <note>original: "Mancipiū"</note> found a "bag" from the middle of the mill. Look at that most dejected word as it is applied to the majesty of the Queen of Heaven! Strike out that dishonest word, review the rest; it will be equal in all of them. The sense itself has no weight, no honesty, no dignity; and as for the words and the form of composition—O God, what dregs, what husks!

Then there is the rhythm, which smells of the weaving-shop, and of the kind that can suddenly fall and be fashioned in the filth of a tavern; how inept, how bloodless and lifeless are their common songs! You make such abject men—recently leaving a three-month school and runaways turned to trades—the authors of your trifles <note>original: "nenijs," literally dirges or nonsensical songs</note> amidst the secrets of the divine office. You do this as easily as you recklessly hang all your well-spoken and well-advised household members by the nose; you are only persistent in your own senses, precocious wits, and always flaccid. But to be repelled when one warns well is an injustice; and no one gladly returns from their benevolence with this reward, so he withdraws, and each is permitted to feed his own chicks which he has brought to his own yard. 

While you sing such things, the song often finds no end. The priest, who thinks his service to the Lord is owed from the altar, stands suspended and idle in the middle of the **Secrets** <term>Secrets: The "Secreta" are prayers said by the priest in a low voice during the Mass, usually during the preparation of the offerings.</term>, or whatever else, as human thought is mobile and restless, turning to things other than the Secrets. Let them receive these things mildly from me regarding the songs which you—Christians as much as strangers—deemed worthy of yourselves so that you might "correct" and corrupt the divine office. You, however, being strangers, would even throw these things away; that such things are done among Christians, he is either ignorant...
