# CONCERNING THE PRIESTHOOD AND THE WHOLE CHURCH AGAINST [THE SECTS]

Whether it is the Bishop, or those who give good counsel—which is closer to the truth—you do not listen, and you set a very bad example. For you presume beyond your condition; you do not obey your leader and father in matters of religion. But if he, in turn, were to take a portion of your rashness into himself outside of his ordinary jurisdiction, and were to remove the ancient, sacred laws of provincial law as if they were superfluous, and substitute his own laws that were never requested, creating a new form of judgment, would that not stir up your indignation <note>original: "stomachum," literally 'stomach' but used here to mean 'bile' or 'anger'</note>? Therefore, consider it best in human affairs not to mix offices, but for each one to act according to his lot and to conduct himself without offense according to it. Finally, just as much authority as each man desires to have for his own magistracy, let him allow that much power to another in a foreign prefecture. Let him modestly abstain from that same prefecture, and thus public concord will stand for a long time. For indeed, if not all the seditions of kingdoms have arisen from this source, then certainly in this century, what other plague than the ignorance of one's own office has brought us these schismatics and Pighards <note>The "Pighards" or "Picards" was a derogatory term used for the Bohemian Brethren (Unitas Fratrum), a pre-Reformation Christian sect</note>?

After those things, we are challenged by the supreme claim that the Pighard holds. He thinks that if this is extorted from his hands, it would be as difficult for us as it is dangerous for him, since his salvation and honor openly depend upon it. I am speaking of that profane priesthood of theirs to which we are summoned. They say, therefore, that they have their own [priests]: but let us give words to the Pighard—for it is pleasing to laugh again at the barbarity from his mouth. The Pighard says: "These people certainly do not know that we have our own priests." Be silent, I pray! My ear cannot bear such barbarity. If you have a priesthood, it must also be legitimate; but it cannot be legitimate for you from any other source unless you have received it continuously from its author, Christ. But you were not there in the times of Christ, nor do you stand in the line of perpetual succession from Christ. In us—who reach back to Christ and the apostles, the founders of our faith, in a line from parents to grandfathers, from grandfathers to great-grandfathers, and from these to ancestors even unto the first—you did not remain.

We, the sincere posterity of Christ and the apostles, know no other author for our beliefs. No one, for the sake of a sect discovered by himself, has given us a foreign name or dogma separate from Christ. Just as in families, only he who descends according to the line carries back the legitimate lineage, so from religion, he will carry back a legitimate priesthood who has received it from continuous succession. You, however, have made yourself your own author by the confession of your faith. For when you were of us, you went out from us; where then does the authority of your priesthood stand? We have gone out from no one; we were here before you were, and we were here when you were made. We have likewise remained the same thereafter. Therefore, the true priesthood of Christ ought to be sought from this line, as if a Bishop of our side had consecrated your bishops. But you say that you have it by a hidden inspiration; we, however, have proved by many testimonies above that you are not inspired, so that you could boast of your suspicion or your priesthood as coming from a divine Author. And you make yourself a witness to our word: for when the Schismatics were contending with the Christians at a certain time, you were offended there; and since you disagreed with both, you followed your own separate path. This is easy for anyone to do according to the perversity of his own sense, so that he does not call upon a divine work.

But you say you are inspired. You say the priesthood was transfused into you divinely. It would have been necessary then for your Archimandrite <note>A title for the head of a monastery or a sect leader</note>, one or more, to have been made a priest without the mediation of a human hand. But this is a new example, unknown to both Testaments. For it is not possible, says Origen in his commentary on Leviticus <note>Origen of Alexandria (c. 184–253 AD), an early Christian scholar and theologian</note>, to be a priest whom the Law has not established. Therefore, by the hands of Moses, Aaron was made high priest; from the high priest, the lesser priests and the whole Levitical order were consecrated according to the established ceremonies. Nor thereafter, in all time, did it come from anywhere else than from this succession, by which the Synagogue perpetuated the priestly dignity for itself from the hands of priests. In the Acts of the Apostles, Saint Paul says: "Take heed to yourselves and to the whole flock, in which the Holy Spirit has placed you" <note>original: "Attendite vobis & vniuerso gregi in quo vos spiritus sanctus posuit," a reference to Acts 20:28</note>.

<summary>The author argues against the legitimacy of the "Pighard" (Bohemian Brethren) priesthood, asserting that true religious authority must come through unbroken apostolic succession rather than "hidden inspiration." He cites the biblical examples of Aaron and the teachings of Origen to prove that a priesthood must be physically transmitted through the laying on of hands.</summary>

...Bishops to rule the Church of God which he acquired with his own blood; <note>Acts 20:28</note> to Timothy, however, [he wrote]: do not lay hands hastily on anyone, nor share in the sins of others. For this reason I warn you to stir up the grace of God which is in you through the laying on of my hands. <note>1 Timothy 5:22 and 2 Timothy 1:6</note> Therefore the Apostles established Bishops, among whom was that Timothy at Ephesus, Dionysius <note>Dionysius the Areopagite, traditionally the first Bishop of Athens</note> at Athens, Titus in Crete, Polycarp at Smyrna, Ignatius at Antioch, and Mark at Alexandria. If, as the Pighard <note>Pighardus: A derogatory term for the Bohemian Brethren, suggesting they were similar to the "Picards," a heretical group from the Low Countries</note> boasts, bishops and priests are made immediately by the Holy Spirit without visible work, then those whom the Apostles established were not Bishops, and the Church sat without a pastor, without sacred rites, and without sacraments. But this delusion now falls back upon the Pighard himself. For if they truly were Bishops, then they are not made so divinely as to exclude the cooperation of human ministry and external signs. And indeed, if it had ever been believed that a sacred order consisted only of an internal calling, the Pighards would not have been the first to discover this; rather, in the primitive holiness of the Church, such priests of internal inspiration would have come forward long ago, and the Apostles would have received them and would not have had to wait for those whom they themselves would consecrate. Christ the Savior said:

> **He who does not enter through the door into the sheepfold, but climbs up another way, is a thief and a robber.** <note>John 10:1</note>

If a sacred order is now held only by invisible anointing without external signs, who, by this logic, could distinguish between a legitimate entry and a predatory one? Who could tell the difference between a pastor and a thief? Any profane person at all could present himself as a priest. Prophecy is a hidden gift of the Holy Spirit; therefore, so that sacrilegious men would not demand faith for their lies under such a name, God gave a sign from the outcome of predictions by which we might know a true Prophet from a false one. So it should have been the work of divine providence to have given a means of discernment between a true and a fake Priest. Let the Pighard show this place; I have not been able to find it. But let them show and assert that the priesthood is theirs by inspiration. Senseless men! For by those same arts of theirs, where they most condemn us, we are most absolved. We shall also say that whatever power of the priesthood you have snatched from us concerning the ancient anointing, we have received the same again, in your fashion, from internal inspiration. On what grounds will you exclude us from the priesthood then? Do you want your arts to be valid against us? Then ours will be valid against you in turn. Finally, whatever crime you charge us with for which we do not deserve to have the priesthood, we charge you with the same or a much more heavy crime regarding the things now witnessed—from your battle against God, against the saints, and against the attested truth with those lies of yours—whereby you yourself cannot have the priesthood. But the priesthood is most certainly from election and anointing, and so the Apostle writes to the Hebrews:

> **For every high priest taken from among men is appointed for all in those things which pertain to God, that he may offer gifts and sacrifices for sins; who can have compassion on those who are ignorant and erring, since he himself is also surrounded by infirmity. And because of this he must, just as for the people, so also for himself, offer for sins.** <note>Hebrews 5:1–3</note>

Nor does anyone take this honor for himself, but he who is called by God just as Aaron was. <note>Hebrews 5:4</note> In this way, like Aaron, the Pighards are certainly not called, but they take the honor for themselves so that they might steal away the Christian priesthood. If, therefore, the law were transferred from us to them, it would have to be transferred upon the death of someone; for the Apostle says again:

> **Where there is a testament, the death of the testator must intervene. For a testament is confirmed among the dead.** <note>Hebrews 9:16–17</note>

Either let them show their testator, or let them cease to thrust their insanities upon us. Or is this not the greatest insanity: that they claim for themselves a priesthood which is false for those who believe in it, lacking a just origin and a beginning sought from some specific time and place? And while no private person is permitted to establish any prefecture whatsoever without a superior or public power, those Pighards have established a priesthood from themselves, from beginnings conceived within themselves—a priesthood which even the Apostles could not have had except from an ordinary cause.

# ON THE PRIESTHOOD AND THE WHOLE CHURCH AGAINST THEM

...they were able to do; let the Pighards <note>A derogatory name for the Bohemian Brethren, linking them to the heretical "Picards" of Flanders.</note> hold that this was rashly seized today. So that the power of administering the virtue of the sacraments might be certain for the Apostles themselves, the founder of the Church and its sole master of the house, Christ, said, "Peace be with you. As the Father sent me, so I send you." <note>John 20:21</note> When he had said this, he breathed on them and said to them, "Receive the Holy Spirit. Whose sins you forgive, they are forgiven them. And whose sins you retain, they are retained." <note>John 20:22–23</note> In what way, then, was Christ sent, so that he might also send the Apostles in the same way? Specifically, he did not glorify himself; as the Apostle says to the Hebrews: "He was glorified so that he might become a high priest." <note>Hebrews 5:5</note> But it was He who spoke to him: "You are my son, today I have begotten you." From this fundamental power, Christ also sent the Apostles into the Church—not glorified of themselves—as dispensers of the remission of crimes (that is, of the priesthood) and as the performers of the sacraments. 

Into what secret gathering <note>original: "conciliabulum"; a mocking term for an unauthorized religious meeting.</note> of the Pighards did Christ come, just as he came into the assembly of the Apostles, in order to grant again new sacred rites outside the ancient order and new power to an emerging Pighard priesthood? The force and authority of the ecclesiastical priesthood has been clearly testified. Could Christ and the Divinity have performed something of such a divine and great work there among the Pighards alone—hidden from the world, stealthily, and not commanded by divine records? If this could have happened, then Christ did not confirm the priesthood once and for all in the Apostles so that its efficacy would be perpetually continued from this source alone to posterity; rather, he would have been destined to make other beginnings later on. Therefore, it would have been necessary in the intervening time, through the earlier ages of men, for Christ to send others and still others by his presence, just as he himself had been sent. Just as he once sent the Apostles, it would have been necessary for a new church, a new order, new sacred rites and dogmas—unfamiliar to their predecessors—to have come forth so many times in the previous century, contrary to that stability of the Church which Christ predicted would exist in Peter and his successors: "You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church." <note>Matthew 16:18</note>

Therefore, Pighards, are you not lying men? For just as robbers—who, besides the public laws they have betrayed, attack and violate others—make new decrees for themselves, so you, in the synagogue of the devil <note>A common medieval polemical term for a heretical sect, derived from Revelation 2:9.</note> through raw contention, invent new things against the Church and falsely claim divine inspiration as the author of your impurities. Or perhaps some other Samuel happened upon you there, who secretly anointed one or more of you, just as that man took a small flask of oil secretly for Saul, and anointed David as the future king? <note>Referring to the biblical accounts of the prophet Samuel anointing the first two kings of Israel (1 Samuel 10 and 16).</note> Although these matters fall into the aforementioned difficulties, I would still ask: who there made your leader <note><term>Archimandrita</term>: A Greek term for a high-ranking abbot; here used mockingly to describe the Pighard leadership.</note> powerful with the anointing by which he might anoint one or more of you outside the Apostolic order? We know of the holy Samuel; he was consecrated and the Lord was with him, and not one of his words fell to the ground. And all Israel from Dan even to Beersheba knew that Samuel was a faithful prophet of the Lord. <note>1 Samuel 3:19–20</note> But you and that leader of yours, who are you? 

But if he has sprinkled you from an obscure cloud, wherever it may be, hear again the example of Scripture: David, although he had been anointed, did not demand the kingdom by his own right until Saul had died. For he said: "The Lord be merciful to me, that I should not do this thing to my lord, the Lord’s anointed, <note>original: "Christo domini"; in this context, "Christ" is used in its literal sense of "anointed one." David refuses to kill King Saul because Saul had been validly anointed king by Samuel.</note> and stretch out my hand against him, for he is the Lord’s anointed. As the Lord lives, unless the Lord strikes him, or his day comes that he dies, or he perishes descending into battle, the Lord be merciful to me that I do not stretch out my hand against the Lord’s anointed." <note>1 Samuel 26:10–11</note> Therefore, Pighard, you should not hastily succeed our Church with your new sect. For she is certainly the Lord’s anointed; allow her first to cease to be. But because she will not cease before the age and the world are fulfilled, you shall at no time succeed the Apostolic Church and its anointing. Your priesthood is wicked at this time; your sacred rites are contaminated. In the manner of robbers and enemies against us, you have faked these things so that our rites might somehow be seen as impure in comparison to yours. But your Sacraments are stripped of all power; you are more profane than a Turk or a Saracen, and emptier than a Jew.

He uses the biblical examples of Samuel, Saul, and David to demonstrate that even a divinely chosen successor must respect the existing "anointed" order until it naturally ends.</summary>

### THE WALDENSIANS: BOOK FOUR

You have no baptism. No confirmation. No remission of sins. I say you do not practice the dignity of marriage, but rather meretricious unions <note>The author argues that because Pighard "priests" lack valid ordination, they cannot perform a legal Christian marriage, rendering the union equivalent to prostitution in his eyes.</note>; from this sacrilegious priesthood of yours—if it is even worthy of the name—you are all bastards. You are unclean; you were conceived as rashly as dogs. You are, in short, infamous in all things. You have silently birthed this infamy against us from our own cast-down priesthood; you have spoken it, you have cast it as an objection. But the side with the better cause has triumphed. 

Just as you have thrust this infamy upon your most Christian King Vladislaus <note>Vladislaus II (1456–1516), King of Bohemia and Hungary.</note>, that most choice prince, and upon the heir of his kingdoms, Louis <note>Louis II (1506–1526), who was a child at the time of this writing.</note>—who come as legitimate heirs only through our sacred rites—so you have thrust it upon all Christian people alike with your snares. And yet you still wish to appear simple and innocent? Not to paint words, not to cover up hypocrisy and heresy, not to deceive the King with diabolical deceits? Look at the faith you present with such a bold face; look how shamefully you fail it in your deeds! May the most pious King finally turn away this terrible plague, the Pighards, from all Christian people.

We have truly reported such things concerning the infamous and adulterine priesthood of the Pighard, which is more nonsensical than that of the pagans. Truly, the Indians, Chaldeans, Persians, Egyptians, Greeks, Latins, Gauls, and Germans never acted so foolishly as those Pighards do today. All nations felt more deeply about that which they worshipped as divine than to wish for their sacred rites to be exercised outside of an established law. There was a fixed origin of priesthoods, a fixed succession, and a decreed initiation known to those conceived for it. The Brahmins <note>original: "bragmahū"</note> of the Babylonians, the Magi, the Gymnosophists <note>Ancient Indian philosophers known for their asceticism and nudity.</note>, the Corybantes, the Phoebads <note>Priestesses of Apollo.</note>, the Samothracian pontiffs, the augurs, the Vestal Virgins, and the Druids—all were assumed, initiated, and substituted in certain ways according to their own ritual. 

Furthermore, in the age of the world's birth—that is, in the century of the holy Patriarchs—priesthoods were guarded within families. The priest was the same person who was the firstborn; this was his perpetual mark. This is what Esau sold of his birthright to his brother Jacob; hence those tears and تلك bellows of his. For Christ, who was to descend into the flesh from the Patriarchs through Jacob, willed that this nobility of the birthright and the prerogative of the priesthood be transferred into his own line. 

We too are the firstborn in Christ. At what price, then, or by what caution have we sold our mark to a Pighard, so that he might today claim the priesthood for himself while we are excluded? How much more modestly those "of the Cup" <note>The Utraquists or Hussites, who insisted on the laity receiving the wine (the cup) during the Eucharist, but who—unlike the Pighards—still sought valid apostolic ordination for their priests.</note> feel about these matters; for although they have cast off obedience, they nevertheless understand that the power of priestly anointing remains with the Apostolic Republic <note>The Roman Catholic Church.</note>. They submit their candidates to be ordained by our bishops by whatever means they can—by trickery or by theft. This is surely a divine judgment: that under such great dizziness as that which caused them to fall from obedience, they were not also able to fall away from our priesthood. Clearly, a perpetual rebuker of their disobedience had to be set against them, so that either, being convicted by this witness, they might return, or, by wickedly resisting, they might provoke a more manifest damnation for themselves. "So that you, O God, may be justified in your words, and prevail when you are judged." <note>Psalm 51:4</note>

For neither of these contributes to the piety of the faith: neither the fact that schismatics usurp the priesthood by theft or fraud, nor that the Pighards do so by violence. If it comes to this, they hold unjustly what they hold outside of legitimate possession, and they ignore the adjuration of Saint Paul as if it were ineffective: *I appeal to you, brothers, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you agree, and that there be no schisms among you, but that you be united in the same mind and the same judgment. For it has been reported to me about you, my brothers, that there are contentions among you. What I mean is that each one of you says, "I belong to Paul," or "I belong to Apollos," or "I belong to Cephas," or "I belong to Christ."* <note>1 Corinthians 1:10–12</note> 

The Apostle did not allow the Corinthians to glory over their masters, by whom they had been equally taught the way of salvation. If they had said, "I am a follower of Rokycana" <note>Jan Rokycana (c. 1396–1471), the leader of the Utraquists.</note> or "I am a Pighard," he would have heard it as if someone said, "I am a Nicolaitan" <note>A sect mentioned in the Book of Revelation, often used as a synonym for heretics.</note> or "I am a follower of Anti—"

### ON THE PRIESTHOOD AND THE WHOLE CHURCH AGAINST [THE HERETICS]

Therefore, is Christ divided? Was some schismatic crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of some Pighard? If we are "Apostolic," it is certainly not in the sense that we say one belongs to the Chalice <note>A reference to the Utraquists, a moderate Hussite faction that insisted on the laity receiving the wine (the chalice) during communion.</note> and another to a Pighard; we ought to say we are of Christ, as you also wish to be. Thus, by the name "Apostolic," we do not mean a human founder, but rather the line of succession. For we are Apostolic, which is of Peter, which is of Christ, which is of God. You have abandoned this Apostolic foundation; you have recently begun to believe from other origins. You are not Apostolic, and therefore not of Peter, who is of Christ, which is of God. If anyone is guilty of today's schism, it is not us. We have not deserted anyone; it is you who are guilty, you who have deserted—you, whom the Apostle adjures by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ that there be no schisms among you.

Bow your necks once more to such great majesty; return to your place in his mystical body, the Church, from which you have fallen away. For truly, as Moses says, "The Lord your God is testing you." The Lord your God has sent you false prophets like **Rokycana** <term>Jan Rokycana (c. 1396–1471), the influential Hussite Archbishop of Prague. Though he sought reform within the Church, the author views him as a "false prophet" leading the people into heresy.</term> and others, to make it clear whether you love the Lord or not with all your heart and all your soul. Beware, and restrain that most dangerous rashness regarding the priesthood. Let those who do not believe us be moved and urged forward; learn, indeed, from the example of all those who perished miserably because they wrongfully claimed for themselves the power over sacred things that was not theirs. 

The earth broke open under the feet of **Korah** and his assembly, and they went down alive into hell, covered by the soil. **Uzzah** stretched out his hand to the Ark of God and held it because the oxen were kicking and caused it to tilt. The Lord was angry and indignant against Uzzah and struck him for his rashness, so that he died there beside the Ark of the Lord. 

**Azariah** and **Uzziah**, the King of Judah, also provide a warning. When Uzziah had become strong, his heart was lifted up to his own destruction—these are the words of the book of **Chronicles** <term>original: *Paralipomenon*, the Greek title for the Books of Chronicles, meaning "things left out."</term>—and he neglected the Lord his God. He entered the temple of the Lord, intending to burn incense on the altar of incense. Immediately, Azariah the priest entered after him, and with him eighty priests of the Lord, most courageous men. They resisted the King and said, "It is not your office, Uzziah, to burn incense to the Lord, but the duty of the priests—that is, the sons of Aaron—who are consecrated for this kind of ministry. Leave the Sanctuary! Do not act with contempt, for this will not be accounted to your glory by the Lord God." 

Uzziah became angry, and while holding the censer in his hand to burn incense, he threatened the priests. Immediately, leprosy broke out on his forehead in the presence of the priests in the house of the Lord, right above the altar of incense. When Azariah the high priest and all the other priests looked at him, they saw the leprosy on his forehead and quickly drove him out. Indeed, he himself hurried to leave, terrified because he had felt the stroke of the Lord. Thus, King Uzziah was a leper until the day of his death. 

Concerning the men of Beth-shemesh: the Lord struck seventy men and fifty thousand of the common people because they had looked into the Ark of the Lord. For as the divine **Dionysius** <term>Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite, a highly influential mystical theologian. The author uses his authority to argue that sacred mysteries must be guarded from the "profane" or unordained.</term> says, "Let no profane person cry out; let no one who lacks celestial training proceed to try to see those things which are above us; it shall not be harmless." But he says darkly again to Timothy: "Take care more diligently not to bring forth the Holy of Holies, nor allow it to be violated by profane eyes, except by your equals, the most Reverend prelates to whom the handling of sacred things is ordained."

Saul said, "I have not appeased the face of the Lord; compelled by necessity, I offered a burnt offering to the Lord." But what did the Prophet Samuel answer him? "You have acted foolishly." And again: "Does the Lord desire burnt offerings and victims, and not rather that the voice of the Lord be obeyed? For obedience is better than victims, and to listen is better than to offer the fat of rams. Because to rebel is like the sin of divination, and to refuse to submit is like the crime of idolatry." Who could be thought to have acted more piously than Saul? He was in the camp; the enemies were insulting them and provoking them to battle...

# WALDENSES BOOK FOUR
## V. 6.

[His men] were slipping away in terror; Samuel, from whose hands the sacrifice ought to have been performed, was absent for seven days beyond the appointed time. [Saul] believed it irreligious to lead forth the battle line without having appeased the Lord, therefore, out of such great causes, he offered the sacrifice, both the burnt offerings and the peace offerings. And yet, because he had usurped the Priesthood in such great necessity, he was severely rebuked by the prophet. He was utterly rejected by God so that his kingdom—and not even his private posterity—should ever rise again. And you therefore, since divine judgments do not lie, you who commit the same sacrileges, shall no longer advance toward salvation; truly it is said to you: "Because you have cast away the word of the Lord, the Lord has also cast you away." Do not, therefore, "touch my anointed ones, and do no harm to my prophets" <note>Psalm 105:15.</note>. Observe diligently, says Moses, lest you incur the plague of leprosy, but do whatever the Priests of the Levite lineage shall teach you, according to what I commanded them, and fulfill it solicitously. Remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam <note>original: "Mariæ". In the Latin Vulgate, Miriam is often named Maria.</note> on the way when you went out of Egypt. She had spoken against Moses—this man established by God as a Prophet—for she and Aaron had said: "Has the Lord spoken only through Moses? Has he not spoken to us as well?" Certainly God had spoken to Aaron and Miriam, if indeed they were prophets, having spoken of how great a gift our rebels do not yet dare to boast of themselves. Nevertheless, the Lord was very angry, and in His anger He departed from them. The cloud also withdrew, which was over the tabernacle, and behold, Miriam appeared white with leprosy, like snow. 

Should not such great and capital examples terrify the rebels of the Church? At last, be terrified at the divine judgments. For a slight cause—otherwise, I do not say "cause" because there is none, but only through your own presumption—you take this burden upon yourselves and run into such horrifying examples. Namely, you accuse the vices of our [clergy] as a great cause for which you think the sacrament is impious, and you attribute a fault to Christian holiness because of the vice of some disapproved person, and so you turn away from the joined Church, as if you could not live holily unless you became deserters. It would have been holier if you had guarded your life among us in the same commonwealth, even amidst neighboring vices, following the example of the prophets who, in the midst of such great sins and the common corruption of the Synagogue, nevertheless lived holily within the Synagogue and the Mosaic laws. 

In Noah's ark, both the clean and unclean are called. If the "clean" person, because of the "unclean," deigns not to enter the ark, he perishes from his own cleanliness while the unclean are saved. Christ equally compels all to enter the wedding feast; strive also to enter with us into this house, walk there with us in agreement. Yet a great fear still looms over you, lest when the King enters and sees those reclining at the table, he sees you not dressed in a wedding garment and says to you: "Friend, how did you enter here not having a wedding garment?" And you would be speechless; but the King would say to the ministers: "Bind his hands and feet and cast him into the outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth." For many are called, but few are chosen. We hear that from the "called," sinners first become the "elect." What then shall those who are not "called" hope for? Namely, that he who does not believe is already judged. 

Finally, you think headlong that those who are now priests, though they ought not to sin, yet cannot sin at all; while certainly every high priest, as the divine Paul writes, "is taken from among men" and "he himself is surrounded by weakness," and therefore he must offer for sins, just as for the people, so also for himself. For certainly that "sinlessness," so to speak, does not come to man before we merit heaven. But you are like the boastful publican <note>The author appears to conflate the Pharisee and the Publican from Luke 18; it was the Pharisee who boasted of his own righteousness while the Publican was humble.</note> praying in the temple; you are like him who said with confidence: "All these I have done from my youth." You are resurrecting in yourselves **Pelagius** <term>Pelagius (c. 354–418 AD) taught that humans could achieve moral perfection through their own efforts without divine grace. His views were condemned as heresy.</term>, who felt that a man could reach such a peak that he could no longer sin. But what does the Apostle John reply to your arrogance? "If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us." If therefore we cannot refute the sentence of the Apostle—and he has concluded all things under sin so that he might have mercy on all—and finally "the heavens are not clean in his sight," but even in them he found something of perversity, then we surely, from our earthly dregs, have sin.

# ON THE PRIESTHOOD AND THE WHOLE CHURCH AGAINST [THE REBELS]

as also the Apostle James said: "For in many things we all stumble" <note>original: "in multis enim offendimus omnes"; James 3:2</note>. Furthermore, the same Apostle says again: "Whoever shall keep the whole law, yet stumble in one point, has become guilty of all" <note>James 2:10</note>. About which also the prophet said: "When the righteous man turns away from his righteousness and commits iniquity, he shall die in them; in the injustice that he has worked, he shall die" <note>Ezekiel 18:24</note>. Therefore, because you have sin, and moreover because you do not have legitimate **unction** <note><term>unction</term>: refers here to the sacred anointing during ordination, symbolizing the legal and spiritual transition into the priesthood.</note>, for both reasons you are unworthy of the priesthood. 

But to the sinner, God has said: "Why do you declare my justices and take my covenant into your mouth? For you have hated discipline and cast my words behind you" <note>Psalm 50:16-17</note>. And further: "Malice has abounded within your door, and your tongue fashioned deceits. Sitting, you spoke against your brother, and you laid a scandal against the son of your mother. These things you have done, and I was silent; you thought, you wicked one, that I would be like you. I will rebuke you and set [these things] before your face. Understand these things, you who forget God, lest he seize you and there be no one to rescue you" <note>Psalm 50:19-22</note>.

Understand with open ears, you who trample upon the **ordinary priesthood** <note>The "ordinary" priesthood refers to the established, regular succession of priests ordained by bishops within the Church hierarchy.</note> and profane it through your filth, and who wickedly break into the Holy of Holies of God! To you God says: "Why do you declare my justices and take my covenant into your mouth?" 

"For the lips of the priest keep knowledge," says the prophet Malachi, "and they seek the law from his mouth, because he is the **messenger** <note>original: "angelus"; while usually translated as "angel," in this context it refers to the priest as the herald or messenger of the Lord of Hosts.</note> of the Lord of hosts. But you have departed from the way and have caused many to stumble in the law; you have made void the covenant of Levi," says the Lord of hosts <note>Malachi 2:7-8</note>.

Truly, divine things are not intended to be performed out of order. For this reason, Christ also forbade the devil from preaching Him—not because it was an evil thing to confess God, but because it was not fitting for transgressors of the spirit, and those who have fallen from the order established under God, to usurp the mystery of the new grace. This grace was restoring the human fall back into divine order, and it was not appropriate for this Gospel of salvation to be preached by such a fugitive messenger. 

By this example alone, Christ the Savior vehemently strikes the schismatic **Pighards** <note><term>Pighards</term>: A derogatory term used for the Waldensians or the Bohemian Brethren, implying they were "Picards" or heretics from Flanders/France.</note> and all those plagues who cast obedience behind their backs, because they impiously practice the Gospel and the form of salvation. For Scripture says, "Let all things be done among you in order" <note>1 Corinthians 14:40</note>. Those transgressors who have gone outside of the order certainly put forward and perform outwardly those things which belong to the Church, just like the **exorcists** about whom we read in the Acts of the Apostles. They adjured demons by an authority that was not their own; for they said, "I adjure you by the Jesus whom Paul preaches." But their end shall be destruction. For finally, when the Lord reveals Himself in His day, the Spirit will also mock them just as He did those exorcists, saying: "Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are you?" <note>Acts 19:13-16</note>. He shall lord it over all of them there and prevail against them unto their ruin.

## HOW THE UNIVERSAL CHURCH DEPENDS UPON ONE VICARIOUS HEAD AS THE MASTER OF FAITH ON EARTH AND THE DISPENSER OF THE POWER OF THE KEYS. TO WHOM OBEDIENCE IS UNIQUELY NECESSARY FOR ATTAINING THE SALVATION OF SOULS.

This last point remains for us, which we took up against that Pighard to assert the authority of the ecclesiastical priesthood. Under this heading, we shall do nothing else but show that the Pighard—who formerly lived with us under common laws and Apostolic obedience—rejected that same obedience unjustly. For the **keys of the Church** <note>The "power of the keys" refers to the authority to forgive sins and govern the Church, given by Christ to St. Peter.</note> do not perish on account of the moral laxity of the clergy. Since those keys never perish, he can never draw the authority of the Church over to himself; since he follows a path different from ours by human faction and not by divine inspiration; and since he carries out a deadly priesthood. We have exposed how he deceives himself in external matters, and we have stripped him of the only supports which should have been the protection of his new faith.

### WALDENSIANS BOOK FOUR

...so that he may now understand that no salvation remains for him from his superstition and false persuasion, and that he should return to our commonwealth and common laws. However, these laws which we follow, Pighardus <note>A derogatory term used for the "Picards," a name often given to the Waldensians or the Bohemian Brethren.</note> mockingly insults from his own madness and attacks even more wickedly with invented calumny. Therefore, we are forced to give an account of our Apostolic obedience. 

Thus, Christ our redeemer, because he ascended into heaven after his passion and was not going to administer the church through visible work [in person], commended the dispensing of the heavenly sacraments to Peter, the Apostles, and the remaining pastors whom the Apostles were to ordain in the church as **vicars** <note><term>vicar</term>: from the Latin *vicarius*, meaning a substitute or deputy acting in the place of a superior.</note>. We read in the Gospels that he was going to do this; for when he set out abroad, he appointed servants over his household and sent laborers into the vineyard. He said of the disciples: "As you sent me into the world, so I also send them into the world" <note>original: "Sicut tu me miſiſti in mundum, ita & ego mitto eos in mundum"; John 17:18</note>. And in another place to the disciples: "Peace be with you; as the Father sent me, so I send you" <note>John 20:21</note>. 

For this reason, the Apostles also ordained elders and bishops throughout the churches, so that we might confess Christ as the head and author of the Christian church, but those others only as ministers and vicarious administrators of the Lord’s people. Pighardus, perverting this confession of ours out of blind malevolence, falsely claims that we make those same ecclesiastical leaders—or one supreme over all of them—not merely dispensers of Christ’s household, but the author and head of Christian salvation. 

If he were spreading such a blind calumny among foreigners who were ignorant of the Christian confession, it would still be an impudent and obvious lie. But now, since they dare to direct such a thing into Christian ears—which, by the conscience of their own experience, understand the lie to be so obvious it can be "felt with a finger"—these followers of Pighardus must certainly be most shameless. 

Therefore, let the perverse Pighardus grasp our true opinion, even against his will: the Christian people confess Christ as the head and author of the church. But the Church calls those priests, bishops, and supreme pontiffs only ministers and dispensers of His sacraments. Therefore—though I shall not add another word—we have already blown away all these "smokes" of Pighardus into vanishing clouds. And unless it were a pleasure to hear Pighardus’s fictions more closely and refute them step by step, I would have already finished responding to that insane chapter. 

Above all, the followers of Pighardus accuse the teacher Augustine <note>St. Augustine of Hippo (354–430 AD), a primary authority for Western Christian theology.</note>, claiming he corrupted their opinion regarding the priesthood. Therefore, Pighardus, surely you err now regarding the priesthood from the same opinion by which you testified then; you were erring then under a mask. If, therefore, teacher Augustine reported your present opinion to the **Royal Majesty** <note>original: "R.M." (Regiae Maiestati). This likely refers to a king to whom the Waldensians had submitted a confession of faith, which the author is now critiquing.</note>, what did he report that was foreign to your error, or what did he corrupt of your confession? 

You say afterward that the priestly office began not from the Pope, but from Christ. Therefore, Pighardus, what Christian says [otherwise]? But if we believe that the priesthood which began from Christ is thereafter dispensed through the ministers of the church, did it need to have begun from the Pope? Did not even the priesthood of the ancient Tabernacle seek its source from the high priests alone? Yet for that reason, it was believed to have its origin and sanctification not from the high priests, but from God. 

Furthermore, you say that only the Lord Christ and not the Pope is the High Priest; in this you trifle, and this is a worn-out point <note>original: "mostu⁹" (mos-tuus), suggesting a tired or dead argument.</note>, Pighardus; you do not speak of the matter according to our actual meaning. Therefore hear again, you blind wickedness: we never say the Roman Pontiff is the High Priest *instead of* Christ. 

But just as when some King has set out on a journey, the chief of the governors of the provinces is the highest of all—without injury to the King's majesty—since the King placed his royal decisions in that person's hands. In the same way, among the ministers through whom this Apostolic church is governed, the highest of all is the Apostolic vicar of Christ. As for the scriptures which you bring in here, we say those are introduced according to your false calumny. Because we do not believe according to your lying slander, those scriptures do not refute our true opinion. Nevertheless, to show that you have used those scriptures perversely and twisted them into an adulterous sense...

### ON THE PRIESTHOOD AND THE WHOLE CHURCH AGAINST...

...him. We wish for Paul to dispute among them; you recall, therefore, that passage from the Psalms: *You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek* <note>original: "Tu es sacerdos ĩ ét̃nũ secũdũ ordinẽ Melchisedech"; Psalm 110:4. Melchizedek was a mysterious king and priest from Genesis whom Christians see as a "type" or foreshadowing of Christ.</note>. Therefore, because it is not read with an addition like "You are the **supreme high priest**," but generally as "You are a priest," then, Pighardus, by the same Scripture you use to deny that there are other high priests besides Christ, you would have to deny all priests whatsoever from Christ. You would argue that neither the Apostles nor those whom the Apostles ordained as **presbyters** <note><term>presbyter</term>: from the Greek "presbyteros" meaning elder; the origin of the word "priest."</note> throughout the churches could be priests without insulting Christ. Yet even your own "Synagogue" <note>A dismissive term the author uses for the Waldensian or Bohemian congregations.</note> ought not to have its own little "priestlings" acting against Christ, the sole priest. And as for your butcherings and wool-workings <note>A mocking reference to the common trades (like weaving or tanning) held by Waldensian leaders, whom the author considers uneducated.</note>, why do you contend that we sin against our Supreme Pontiff? 

But as for your claim, Pighardus, that our men are made priests so that they might not die, you are lying. For mortality was taught long ago: it is necessary for all who are born to die. That **iron necessity** is unyielding and inevitable. In the next passage, you bring in the Apostle. Now, if the Bishop is not the **vicar** of Christ on earth because Christ is present, how do you argue? He is the "Bishop of the Christian confession." From this pivot, you must concede another point, because it is also read: *Consider the Apostle and High Priest of our confession, Jesus* <note>Hebrews 3:1</note>. Therefore, Pighardus, you should confess that there are no other Apostles in the Church besides Christ, and you would have to deny the Scripture of Saint Paul which says: *God has placed some in the church: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers* <note>1 Corinthians 12:28</note> and the many things that follow there. 

Answer me here, Pighardus: if those who acted as apostles, prophets, and teachers in the Christian commonwealth sinned, or not? Here, because you do not dare to accuse the deeds of the Apostles, you will therefore grant that there are apostles, prophets, and teachers in the Church, so as not to destroy the Scripture. And we, likewise, shall grant that there are **Bishops** as vicars after Christ, and we shall not destroy the Scripture. 

But what is this? Even Peter did not convert people to himself. Oh, blind perversity! Dare to treat this matter based on our actual deeds for once, rather than your lies, and see what is in your hand—what grounds for dispute are left to you against us? Or has any of the Supreme Pontiffs ever worshipped himself? I take up another point: you say we should grow in charity through Christ, not through the Roman Pontiff. Here I will put back to you something of your own fraud: if not only the Pope, but also the lower orders—the priests and bishops—are that ecclesiastical power by whose dispensation the present Church bears fruit for heaven, and if we only "grow in charity through Christ" as you say, then there will be no ecclesiastical order at all, which goes against the acts of the Apostles and the canon of the Scriptures. 

But this too is false, Pighardus: that because Christ alone is the head of the Church, there is therefore no **vicar** as head of the Church on earth. For we find the members of the Church described in Scripture as the hand, the foot, and the eye. Just as these are perpetually in the Church (without insulting the saints who were once those same members mystically), so He provides for **vicar members** and a **vicar head** on earth, without insulting the power of Christ as the Head. 

Why should there not be an Apostolic presidency just because "Christ is with us until the end of the age"? I bring in the Apostle: there would be no priestly order of God at all [if your logic held]. Under the holiness of the Synagogue, God was present above the **mercy seat** <note><term>mercy seat</term>: the gold cover of the Ark of the Covenant, where God's presence was said to dwell.</note>; yet even then, was there not a pontifical and priestly order to dispense the sacraments and sacrifices? Since there was, your tricks, Pighardus, did not make it so then, but the testimony of the Scriptures made it so. Therefore, the tricks you babble here are most vain. 

Furthermore, if because Christ is present in the Church, there is therefore no visible dispensation of ministers in the Church, then it must be that these ministers have not existed since the time of the Apostles. But has Christ, from the very beginning of the rising Church, governed all things alone and through immediate works by His presence? This is against the faith of the Scriptures. 

Finally, you say that no bishop at all is the head of faith, and no one offered his body and blood for us. We grant you this, and this is the Christian confession. But we do not grant you this: that under Him, there is no vicar head of Christ on earth. For the one does not invalidate the other. No; it is not because some Supreme Pontiff suffered for us that he is, according to our faith, the vicar of Christ. Rather, it is because Christ said to Peter, the president of that seat: *To you I will give the keys of the kingdom of heaven* <note>original: "tibi dabo claues regni Celorum"; Matthew 16:19</note> and *Feed my sheep* <note>original: "pasce oues meas"; John 21:17</note>. You, Pighardus, have wickedly removed these Gospel passages from the middle of the dispute, as if they were not the very pivot of the present argument; and...

# THE WALDENSIANS, BOOK FOUR

Others of a contrary opinion are brought in who do nothing for the case except to fill the eyes and the page. Why did you not bring in those who are most closely related to the present discourse? If they favored your cause, you would better confirm your position; or if they did not, but rather opposed you, you would holily yield to the Gospel. But you do not yield to the Gospel, Pighard <note>original: "Pigharde"; likely referring to a leader of the Bohemian Brethren or a generalized name for a Waldensian opponent.</note>. For you think it is enough for the Roman Pontiff that he be a faithful servant of Jesus. In this, you agree with Korah and his accomplices <note>original: "Chore"; referring to the biblical rebellion of Korah against Moses and Aaron in Numbers 16.</note>, who said to Moses and Aaron: 
> "It is enough for you, for all the multitude is of holy ones, and the Lord is among them; why do you lift yourselves up above the people of the Lord?"

Therefore, because you agree in opinion with those who rebelled against God, what better can you hope for, Pighard, than to one day share their punishment? Yet Moses and Aaron were faithful servants in the house of God, and nevertheless they presided. Peter and Paul were faithful servants of Jesus, yet they presided over the churches. Thus, you should not deny one or the other in the Roman Bishop: the Roman Pontiff is the "servant of the servants of God"—as the Apostolic diplomas <note>official papal documents or charters</note> testify—but in the Christian world, he is the supreme pastor of visible presidency, just as he received this from God:
> "To you I will give the keys of the kingdom of heaven," <note>Matthew 16:19; the traditional biblical basis for papal authority.</note>

and "Feed my sheep." After these things, you say: "Look, we ask you, who desires these bishops of the present age?" I answer you here, Pighard: Who denies obedience to the King's ministers by whom the punishments of the King and the Kingdom are administered, except a traitor and a deserter? Likewise, no one rejects these bishops of the present age except the schismatic, the heretic, and the Heathen, who have cast the Gospel and heavenly piety behind their backs. For if you think that the successors of the Apostolic mission and power seek their own interests and not those of God, look again, Pighard, for Judas, Caiaphas, the Pharisees, and the Scribes were worse. Yet Judas was placed among the Apostles, Caiaphas among the high priests and prophets, and the Pharisees and Scribes among the teachers of the divine law by Christ and the Holy Spirit. Prick up your ears here, Pighard, and from this testimony of the Scriptures, tell me: regarding the Apostolic leaders, look, we ask you, who desires these bishops? I say: Christ and the Holy Spirit are the first who desire them, and they do not wish for you to cast out their bishops. 

You add that in this time, that "adversity which stands in the holy place" is Apostolic <note>A reference to the "Abomination of Desolation" mentioned in Daniel and Matthew, which reformers often identified with the Papacy.</note>. I perceive your unhealthy brain, Pighard; you allude again to the Harlot of the Apocalypse <note>The "Whore of Babylon" from the Book of Revelation, a common anti-Catholic trope used by dissenting groups.</note>, and you wish to say that the word of the Apostle is fulfilled: "that he sits in the temple of God, showing himself as if he were God." <note>2 Thessalonians 2:4; the description of the Antichrist.</note> Regarding such a pestilential infamy, I tell you freely to your face: you lie in every point of that passage. We greet the Pope by the kissing of his feet; we give this to the honor of Christ, whose power he represents on earth. But the Apostle speaks of one man, the Antichrist; however, the supreme pontiffs have been many, and they do not sit in the temple of God wishing to be confessed as gods, but as Apostolic Vicars. Furthermore, the Roman See is not in "falling away" <note>original: "discessione"; a reference to the "apostasy" or "falling away" mentioned in 2 Thessalonians 2:3.</note> but in the perpetual succession of Peter. That "man of sin," however, who will sit in the temple as if he were God, shall be born from falling away and rebellion. Finally, the Jews do not receive our Apostolic leaders as their long-awaited Messiah. Thus, Pighard, you lie most wickedly when you imagine that the "Idol of Perdition," the Antichrist, has today made a pact in the Church of God and the See of Peter.

After this, you turn to the wealth and power of the Roman Pontiff, and you think that today, just as in the past, he has no right to the city of Rome. I say: today there are other kingdoms also, established in parts from the collapsed body of the Roman Empire—Spain, England, France, Hungary, Dalmatia—which formerly did not exist. Tell those most powerful kings: "What did you have then throughout Europe?" They ought not to be considered unjust possessors today simply because they were not there formerly. By this right, Pighard, you must allow the Pope to hold whatever he possesses without force or fraud. The Imperial Majesty formerly abandoned Rome <note>Referring to the move of the capital to Constantinople or the subsequent fall of the Western Empire.</note>; was it therefore necessary for the Father of Religion, the Supreme Pontiff, to depart as well? The city of Rome, in its vast ruins...

->### CONCERNING THE PRIESTHOOD AND THE WHOLE CHURCH AGAINST...<-

...obligations to religion and the supreme pontiff, which is not long dead, but remains. Rome, therefore, which has been cast out from its own boundaries so many times by a hostile hand—would the Roman Pontiff not finally consider it his own, since it has lived again through him and exists today? You subject it to your judgment; from this, anyone can know whose successor the Roman Pontiff is and whom he serves. He is the successor of Peter and his successors; he serves the Church by the public authority which was entrusted to him from the See of Peter. However, whether in his private life he is a sinner and serves sin, or is innocent and serves virtue, is not for me to decide. For "Who am I to judge another's servant? To his own master he stands or falls" <note>A quotation from Romans 14:4. The author argues that God, not man, is the judge of a Pope's soul.</note>. 

But you, Pighard <note>original: "Pigharde"; the author's name for his opponent, likely a member of the Bohemian Brethren.</note>, say all these things as if the Supreme Pontiff serves sin entirely and is the successor—to use your word—of the **Anti-god** <note>original: "Antithei"; a term implying one who is against God, similar to "Antichrist."</note>. If, therefore, those who serve the world are of the world or the devil, as you say, Pighard, then by the contrary argument, whoever among those Supreme Pontiffs served God as martyrs and confessors are of God. Thus, let us no longer dispute about the power of the office, but about the merit of each private person. Therefore, just as much as you labor to weaken Roman authority because of the evil lives of some, so much do we confirm that pontifical authority because of the most holy lives of many pontiffs. This is even more true because power coming from God depends on no man's merit or demerit, but rests solely on its author, God, whose examples we have repeated to you so often: Judas, Caiaphas, the Pharisees, and the scribes <note>The author cites Judas Iscariot and the High Priest Caiaphas to show that God can work through wicked men who hold legitimate office.</note>. 

Finally, let the nobility of lineage be an example to you. Once this is established by the virtue of ancestors, the legitimate pedigree remains in all descendants, not only in the good but also in the evil and the Tyrants. Thus, all things should be viewed from their first origins and not by the merits of each immediate private person. But you, persisting in your evil opinion, call upon **Francis Petrarch** <note>The famous 14th-century Italian poet and scholar who was often critical of the corruption in the Papal court at Avignon.</note> in this same matter, from whom we might learn—according to your stomach—to lose Apostolic obedience. We also pursue the evil habits of individuals, but not so as to cast out their power. Even tyrant kings do many unjust things, yet they do not lose their scepter through violence. If the Pharisees and scribes sit upon the **Chair of Moses** <note>original: "cathedrā Moſi"; a reference to Matthew 23:2, meaning the seat of teaching authority.</note> and the Gospel, and they say many things to us from divine law but do not do them themselves, let us do whatever they say according to the Savior’s precept; let us simply not do according to their works. 

Therefore, Pighard, with whatever scraps or whatever foreign author you cover yourself, you still feel against the Gospel. You have snatched up the poet and orator Francis Petrarch in place of the Gospel. Yet, when you once refused to trust Doctor Augustine, the King's secretary <note>original: "Doctori Auguſtino Regio ſecretario"</note>, because he was a poet or orator—claiming such people either praise or disparage things beyond moderation—now you go against your own opinion. Because Petrarch, a poet and orator, is seen to have said something through your malevolence in a case of deciding the faith, you approve of him so greatly against the Gospel, granting him as much as you everywhere ignore in the Gospel and the Apostle. Thus, you are not found following the authority of anyone, but are seen seeking burrows from which you might protect your perverse sense with whatever veil. Petrarch spoke against "Gallic ambition" <note>A reference to the Papacy's move to Avignon, France, which Petrarch called the "Babylonian Captivity."</note>; yet the Roman Church's universal power is everywhere faithfully confessed and venerated. Why do you not also venerate the Roman Church by his example? Why do you suppress all the better things Petrarch said? Even if he had known nothing better regarding the Roman Pontiff, you still ought to yield to the Gospel, the Apostle, Ignatius, Cyprian, Jerome, and Augustine—who all command pontifical obedience—rather than to a poet and orator.

In the final place, you ask whether many of them were from the noble, the powerful, the wise, or the learned, and what livelihood they had; and that [the Roman Church] ought to compress its lips [in shame]. If we may therefore look at the matter by comparison, I permit you to look, Pighard: if in the primitive Church, slaves, shoemakers, cooks, butchers, wool-workers, tanners, and cobblers—the vilest dregs of the people—were chosen as bishops by the apostles; if they were heralded from the Vandal countryside <note>original: "vandalica rura"; likely referring to rural or "barbarian" regions.</note>, from weaving shops and workshops of trade; yet they were not seen to have lived in their sees most splendidly and honorably in the eyes of the philosopher-schools and princes...

# THE WALDENSIANS, BOOK FOUR #

...they established bishoprics. If they themselves had not been famous, powerful, wise, and learned men from among their ancestors, then surely authority, nobility, learning, and the knowledge of affairs would never have been lacking in the leaders of the early Church. Eusebius, Jerome, and Gennadius <note>Eusebius of Caesarea, St. Jerome, and Gennadius of Massalia were early Christian historians who wrote "catalogs" or biographies of famous Church writers and leaders.</note> are my witnesses, for they recorded those ecclesiastical bishops in their catalogs. Certainly, these were men of such stature that a clumsy, rustic Pighard <note>A derogatory name for the Bohemian Brethren, used by their opponents to link them to the Beghards or Waldensians.</note> would not even deserve to be a footman to them—he who now, inflated by his own foolishness, inserts himself at their side and ambitiously boasts that he administers an apostolic office as an equal. 

Was not even the chosen Apostle Paul <note>original: "vas electionis"; literally "vessel of election," a traditional title for St. Paul from Acts 9:15.</note> high-born and of the first nobility? Was he not a Roman citizen? Was he not wise and learned? He was all these things, and was liberally educated at the feet of Gamaliel <note>A famous Jewish teacher mentioned in the New Testament; the author emphasizes Paul’s high-level education.</note>, whose profound erudition was so well-known that the governor of Judea exclaimed, "Your great learning is driving you mad, Paul!" <note>original: "Multe te littere ad insaniam Paule ducunt"; see Acts 26:24.</note> Therefore, look closely, Pighard: were many of the bishops and leaders of the Church—following the example of your own lowliness—butchers and slaughterers? Did they live from the cobbler’s trade <note>original: "de Sutrina"; a jab at the common trades of lay preachers in the dissenting sects.</note>, as your filthy example suggests? Since, by the testimony of Eusebius of Caesarea and Ambrose, the churches were always generously endowed. Even when the Apostle [Paul] wished for those who were considered "contemptible" in the church to be judges, he meant under the authority of the law, not that the master of the altar should be a common peddler. This fact should compress your lips, you wicked Pighard, so that you might finally blush at those workshop-priestlings <note>original: "sellularijs sacer-dastris"; a contemptuous term for priests who work at manual trades.</note> of yours.

We have replied to the Pighard in this pointed way, setting down almost word for word what was said, and we did this because we wished to treat the matter of Roman obedience in a continuous discourse. Therefore, the Pighards say: [**And seeing the custom, they afterwards confirmed it for the sake of obedience to the Roman Pontiff.**] 

Thus, the Pighards think we are insane, following the Pope like raving Maenads <note>In Greek mythology, Maenads were female followers of Dionysus known for their wild, ecstatic frenzies.</note> following Bacchus. These Pighards thrust such gross ignorance of affairs upon Kings, Princes, and all Christian nobility! They judge their faith and deeds so abjectly, as if these rulers were people who would allow themselves to be mocked by every kind of insult, or as if they suffered from such deep lethargy that they could neither recognize those "frauds" of apostolic veneration nor allow them to be re-examined and brought to open judgment once they were discredited. I say, they attribute such dullness of sense to kings and princes—as if they followed the Pope by reckless and unconsulted obedience rather than by any higher counsel—that these vilest slaves, the Pighards, should be judged guilty of treason <note>original: "temerare maiestatis"; violating the majesty of the state.</note>. 

If even a Pighard slave were to disparage his own private master so foully, accusing him of such supine stupidity, his servile insolence would be checked by the lash. Yet we see that in this time, it is granted only to those wild Pighards—like cattle without a shepherd—to mock ignominiously all princely majesty, all sublimity, and the entire Christian Republic. They suggest that the Christian conscience follows a single man out of servile patience, as if by a horse’s reins, or merely out of naked veneration. We see the world today—and this goes unpunished, which we find most grievous—being accused of being stunned, captured in its senses, and void of reason. 

Therefore, before the other things that must be said to this Pighard regarding this knotty issue, I will excuse the Christian world of this "stupidity." For we follow one head on earth as the Vicar of the Christian cause. If we follow it blindly, as the Pighards quibble—if we follow it without judgment and not according to defined laws—what other supreme judgment ought the Church to have instituted, to which even the Pope, like every Christian, is equally compelled to stand? That common saying, "as I will, so I command; let my will be the law for you" <note>A reference to the Roman poet Juvenal, often used to describe tyranny or arbitrary power.</note>, was not enough for the Church to expect from the Pope. But we understand that we must observe veneration in the Pope, not for his person, but for the power that comes upon him from above, which is higher than man. Therefore, we preserve that power as inviolable, unshaken, untainted, and most holy from the very beginning of the Christian religion, even while we observe it in the leaders of such great power...

-># CONCERNING THE PRIESTHOOD AND THE WHOLE CHURCH AGAINST...<-

The Church has established many things regarding the High Pontiffs <note>The "High Pontiffs" refers to the Popes.</note>; indeed, the Church has often conducted inquiries into the status of the High Pontiffs whenever they were convicted of the crimes of heresy or schism. The Christian people have never wished to follow a Pope who was not Catholic, nor would they have followed one if—as the wickedness of the Pighard <note>A derogatory term for the Bohemian Brethren, a proto-Protestant group.</note> falsely charges against us—they venerated this Seat <term>The Holy See: the jurisdiction of the Pope.</term> out of some sort of suspended stupidity. Therefore, we receive a legitimate power, established under a legitimate presiding officer, and a just authority—one certainly not from man, but from God—in a chaste and holy manner. For so we read in the Law:

*If you perceive that a judgment is difficult and ambiguous for you—between blood and blood, case and case, leprosy and non-leprosy—and you see that the words of the judges within your gates vary: rise up and go up to the place which the Lord your God has chosen. You shall come to the priests of the Levitical race and to the judge who is there at that time; you shall seek from them, and they shall declare to you the truth of the judgment. You shall do whatever those who preside over the place the Lord has chosen shall say; and they shall teach you according to His law, and you shall follow their sentence. You shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left. But he who acts proudly, refusing to obey the command of the priest who ministers at that time to the Lord your God by the decree of the judge, that man shall die, and you shall take away the evil from Israel. And all the people, hearing this, shall fear, so that no one henceforth shall swell with pride.* <note>The author is quoting Deuteronomy 17:8–13 to argue that God established a central religious authority to settle disputes.</note>

By this oracle of the divine voice, we follow one head in the Church as the guardian of our faith and salvation, just as God handed down this same mastery to the leaders of the Church through His Son, saying: **"You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church."** <note>original: "Tu es Petrus et sup hāc petrā edificabo ecclesiam meā"; Matthew 16:18.</note> And again: **"Simon, son of John, do you love me more than these? Feed my sheep."** <note>original: "Simon Ioannis diligis me plus his, Pasce oues meas"; John 21:15–17.</note> Truly, as the divine Paul says: *Let every soul be subject to the higher powers; for there is no power except from God, and those that exist are ordained by God. Therefore, he who resists the power resists the ordinance of God; and those who resist acquire damnation for themselves.* <note>A reference to Romans 13:1–2.</note>

If, therefore, the Church itself is from God, and the things that are from God are ordered, then the Church is also ordered. He who dissolves this order and makes himself a stranger to it resists God and acquires damnation for himself. Let the Pighard congratulate himself on his rebellion; let him return to us from that "hinge" <note>The author likely plays on the word "cardinal" (from *cardo*, meaning hinge).</note> upon which he turns. Let him laugh at and condemn the "simplicity" of the Christian people because of the obedience they hold toward the Apostolic See. 

But let us recall our discourse to its beginning. So, Pighard, you accuse Christian obedience? You would not accuse it unless you yourself held no obedience against the precepts of Scripture: **"Obey those who are set over you and be subject to them, for they keep watch as if to give an account for your souls, so that they may do this with joy and not with sighing."** <note>Hebrews 13:17.</note> Therefore, you do all things without order and clearly testify that you are on the side of the devil, who is himself the deserter of divine order, around whom no order but everlasting horror dwells. 

But tell me, Pighard, with what sense do you deny ecclesiastical obedience? Do you believe there is no legitimate power at all in the world, but only pure tyrannies? Truly, you do not dare to say this so clearly out of fear of kings. Thus, under the subject of "Apostolic obedience," you say what you feel about authority in general. Certainly, whatever you can bring against the Church in this matter—for instance, that its head is the invisible Christ in heaven, and therefore no other "Vicar" <term>Vicar: an earthly representative or deputy acting in the name of Christ.</term> or head or arbiter of religion should be received on earth—in saying such things, you have, with one stroke, attacked all other powers. 

For Christ was no closer to the Church when He established it than the Trinity was to the world when It created it. Nor is Christ more the head of the Church than God the Lord is the head of the world. If it is an insult to Christ to name a "Vicar Head" on earth, it would also be an insult to God to recognize any "Vicar Lord" in the world. For just as we read that Christ is the head of the Church, so we read: **"One Lord, one faith, one baptism; one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in us all."** <note>Ephesians 4:5–6.</note> Therefore, if God, the Lord of all, had reserved the governance of the world to Himself without the intermediary ministry of men—just as you, rebellious Pighard, claim Christ carried the administration of the Church away with Him into heaven—[then all earthly government would be void].

# WALDENSIANS BOOK FOUR #

Z iv

...so that you might charge these kingdoms and even these powers as nothing but usurped tyrannies. Therefore, shall we be purified by that opinion of yours? Shall we dissolve obedience in the world? Shall we dissolve power—which is the very bond of society? Shall we cast off our possessions? Shall we discard those pledges of worldly concord: the ready arbiters of what is just and right, the judges, the praetors <note>original: *propretores*; Roman judicial officials</note>, the consuls, the proconsuls, the military leaders, the kings, and even the Emperors <note>original: *augustos*</note> themselves? 

Should we first weaken every private household? Let the father—the source of authority—put his power from his hands into the common pool. Let him open the storehouse and the larder; let him unlock the inner chamber and the stable. Let the father himself descend to the rank of a servant. We will soon see everything among his own people fall into ruinous waste. Servants and maids will go about promiscuously; boys and girls will grow fat on their own whims; they will eat, play, snore, snatch, and squander. There, one will be idle; here, another will brawl. 

Let us leave this mob and go out into public. There, robbery will break out and rebellion will rise; servitude will vanish, and taxes will be denied. Men will lie in ambush and commit murder; the law will be torn down; lust will exercise its violence. From here, this chaos will pass into the neighborhood; cities and peoples will be troubled; by these forces, kingdoms will be shaken. Consequently, East and West will be mixed in turmoil; they will destroy, plunder, and lay waste. They will provoke the very elements to vengeance. Mortality itself will not provide enough bodies to satisfy the sword's desire to rest. From the legion down to the individual soldier, blood and madness will spread. Finally, the end of these furies will sit upon an overturned world.

To these evils, add the crime of this abandoned power and, furthermore, the madness of religions. Let discord spread from man to village, from village to cities, and from cities to peoples and kingdoms. Here they may deny the faith; elsewhere they may confess it. There will be such confusion as will only be seen at the end of the world, when the elements and the faces of all things will be mixed within themselves. Such will be the face of the world once you have released it from authority. No reason, no providence, no care for benefits or for avoiding harms toward one's neighbor will prevail; instead, those inextricable errors arising from uncertain chances will drive the human race headlong into itself. 

At this point, if anyone thinks the world can remain safe and orderly without authority, the world would have to stand by no other way than the necessity of fate or by continuous miracles. For if neither my own strength nor the laws and princes who defend human peace could stop you when you wished to do harm—if the creeds of Christian unity, the priests, the bishops, and the patriarchs could not restrain you when you wished to be faithless—then some force of fate or the judgment of God alone would necessarily have to intervene to make you less harmful or less treacherous. 

But for God to govern the world in this way—without the intermediate ministry of men—is contrary to the examples of the Scriptures. For once God Himself established His works, He thereafter committed them to the governance of men. According to Scripture, the Lord God sent Adam out of the paradise of pleasure to work the earth from which he was taken. This follows the parable of that man traveling abroad who called his servants and handed over his goods to them so they might work with them; and according to another parable where a certain nobleman went into a distant region to receive a kingdom for himself and return, and having called his ten servants, he gave them ten minas <term>Mina: An ancient unit of currency equal to about 100 drachmas.</term> and said to them, "Trade until I come." 

Finally, this follows what we read in the Acts of the Apostles: "Take heed to yourselves and to the whole flock, in which the Holy Spirit has placed you as bishops to rule the Church of God which He acquired with His own blood." Therefore, the Law was given through Moses; therefore, prophecy was sent through men; therefore, Cornelius <note>The Roman Centurion who was the first Gentile convert.</note> was taught the faith not by an angel, but by Peter the Apostle. From these examples, we see that the rich man Epulo <note>original: *Epulo*; a common medieval name for the "Rich Man" (Dives) in the parable of Lazarus, derived from the Latin word for "feaster."</note> did not deserve to have Father Abraham send Lazarus back to his five brothers. For they had despised the ordinary authority from which, by God's decree, they were meant to be taught salvation on earth, and instead they sought the amazement of some miracle and the continuous operation of God by which even the unwilling might be compelled. 

At three other times, God visited and established religion—that is, the path that runs toward the salvation of men in this corruptible age—through His own presence and through witnessed miracles. But as soon as it was established, He thereafter entrusted the mystery to the patriarchs of the old tabernacle, the high priests, the prophets, the apostles, and their successors. Do you, then, demand miracles at this time? Noah, a just man, preached to sinners and the unbelieving while building the ark; they did not listen and perished in the flood. Pharaoh resisted God’s warning and was submerged in the Red Sea.
