They add that they did not show reverence to this Sacrament because, as I say, they fashion that idea for themselves outside of Scripture. Yet they believe that after the consecration, the bread is—as they write—the present body of Christ, and the wine is the present blood: the whole Christ just as He was handed over to death for the redemption of sins? What then is the Pighard <note>A term used by the author for the Bohemian Brethren, whom he considers heretics.</note> going to do here regarding the presence of Christ? Will he not bow? Even the crucifiers of Christ did not bow. But the Kings <note>The Magi or Three Wise Men.</note> surely bowed to adore the child. The man born blind, Mary Magdalene, and other pious minds also bowed. If they sinned in this, then a portion of that sin would also fall upon Christ, who allowed such things to be done to Him. To say such a thing is an impiety! Therefore, let the Pighard see whose examples he follows more piously.

They further add as an argument for their error: "**Sitting, they immediately received.**" It disturbs me what they mean by that most necessary word "immediately." Perhaps it is because the Church first performs the purifications of souls, the divine office, and the sacred prayers—through which she prepares herself to contemplate the works of God and the benefits granted to the human race, and transforms herself into a divine state—whereas these men do not do the same. They are like men occupied only in making a profit; just as they hurry to their workshop, they "immediately" release themselves from the divine rite, which they do not truly perform anyway. Thus, they are weary of the delays caused by our ceremonies, and they accuse the Church because she herself does not "immediately" complete the same sacred rites. 

Or perhaps they contend that the Apostles approached not having been previously purified, but with unwashed and unbathed souls and bodies, just as they themselves are accustomed to come suddenly from their work. When Christ gave communion to the disciples, did He not first wash their feet? Or did He not say, **"If I do not wash you, you will have no part with me"**? Or did He not give witness to them, saying, **"And you are clean, but not all"**? Did He not first do all these things and then admit the disciples to the participation of the Sacrament? Do these facts not conflict with their claim that "sitting, they immediately received"? 

As for the fact that the Apostles sat at that same time: they did not do so with the mind or intent for which the Pighards plead. For though we nowhere read that they adored Christ [at the table], if they neglected to adore Him because they thought—as the Pighards do—that such an act was a wickedness, then they did not fully believe in the divinity of Christ. They would have had to rebuke others who adored Christ in the flesh, and Christ's own action in allowing Himself to be adored would have displeased them. It is a wickedness even to think this! Therefore, they sat without any dishonor to Christ; indeed, they sat with a holiness, a religious devotion, and a greater veneration for Christ than we show when we adore Him. 

For just as not everyone is required to speak with God face-to-face as Moses did, and not all who are called to the faith can have Christ as the inseparable companion of their daily life as the Apostles did, they should never use this action of the Apostles to argue that what we know (or suspect) was not done at a specific time or by a specific person ought not to be done at all. 

The Pighards add: "**They retained nothing, nor did they carry it out of the house,**" and they say they have this from the "Chronicles of the times." I was expecting that, since they usually call us back to the words of the Lord alone, they themselves would not receive or believe anything attested from any other source. Yet now they actually put forward annals and believe and receive something other than what they found in the Gospel! 

But we admit and also give credit to the chronicles if they are suitable. However, they provide no names for these chronicles, and in this matter they often offend us: they call themselves "above the ancients" and yet they produce no ancient writers. If there were any ancients as strongly against us as they want people to believe, they would have produced them; they would have presented them most readily to confirm their own case and to overturn ours. Therefore, because they do not allow such great witnesses into open judgment, what they boast is not far from a lie. They say truly: [ **Sitting, they immediately received; they retained nothing, nor...** ]

...they carried it outside the house. These are frivolous things and mere trifles, since they have denied the power and truth of the Sacrament, trampled upon the Gospel, and profaned the Apostle <note>Refers to St. Paul</note>, as if these things were not impious and sacrilegious, or as if we had either not noticed them or forgotten them. Thus, regarding the act of sitting and similar things—as if they alone are the ones who maintain the purity of confession, and which they say they preserve while we violate them—they labor to commend the innocence of their faith to those who are unskilled in these matters. Behold the Pighards <note>A derogatory term for the Bohemian Brethren.</note>! Now, if they interpret the Gospel only as far as the sitting down, they truly subject it to a fable or a theater performance. Therefore, those who represent that Supper so precisely and point-by-point: why do they not also do it just once in their life, and specifically in Jerusalem, in the evening before the feast day of Passover, after first removing the supper of the lamb? They bring the sacrament onto a second table; or they do this, and in that one place they eat and drink to excess. Therefore the Apostle rebuked the Corinthians for their behavior:
> Do you not have houses for eating and drinking, or do you despise the church of God, and put to shame those who have nothing? <note>original: "Nunquid domos non habetis..." quoting 1 Corinthians 11:22</note>

Moreover, why did the apostles retain nothing of this? Truly, because there was not yet a reason to retain it; there was not yet a Christian populace that would demand the reception of the sacrament in the final and uncertain moment of life. Finally, they cast these things over us in such a way that, even if we otherwise believe rightly concerning the nature of the Sacrament, they claim this is nothing like Apostolic imitation, and that if we retain our practice, we have overturned the entire faith there. You ethnic! <note>Used here as "pagan" or "outsider."</note> Thus you strain out a gnat and swallow a camel. 

They add because—
> They did not carry it out of the house,

I do not understand why they say this. Perhaps it displeases our heretics because we walk around and purify cities, towns, and marketplaces with this most divine Sacrament <note>Refers to Eucharistic processions like Corpus Christi.</note>. Therefore they think we are overly superstitious. On the contrary, it is they themselves who are excessively insulting toward such a venerable sacrament. Could the high priests and kings carry the Ark of the Old Testament with the highest veneration, and we cannot make Christ's presence in the Sacrament worthy of the same honor? Because the Ark stayed in Kiriath-Jearim, God multiplied their days; will God not bless the cities that have consecrated themselves to the present Sacrament? Indeed, we know that the most serious fires have sometimes been halted because they were met with this most august Sacrament. Now those Pighards mock this faith of ours in God—and they do not believe anything divine is there, but truly our "grassy and wheaten" thing. The senses shudder, and the tongue recoils from conceiving and speaking that most atrocious blasphemy of theirs; they openly attack our "wheaten God" <note>original: "siligineumq̃ deum nostrum." The Pighards mocked the Host as being merely made of fine wheat flour (siligo) rather than being the body of Christ.</note> within those most filthy brothels of the devil. O religion! O care for asserting the celestial majesty! And yet no one has been found among the princes who would cut down those cursed pack-horses of the devil and mockers of divinity. 

But perhaps they also refer to this: "They did not carry it out of the house," and they consider it unjust that we carry this consummating Host <note>term: "hostia" - The consecrated bread of the Eucharist, literally meaning 'sacrificial victim.'</note> out to the sick. In truth, at that time, whoever was baptized also received the communion of the Sacrament of the altar immediately after the font. Therefore, since it is outside the realm of belief to think that no one newly instructed in the faith fell ill or lay dying—and wished to be baptized at the end of life—therefore, because such people were found, the body of Christ, the sacrament, was carried out to them along with the baptismal font and the holy oil. Furthermore, the saintly Jerome, at his passing just before nightfall—as Eusebius of Cremona <note>A disciple of St. Jerome.</note> who was present at these events testifies—received the sacrament of the body of Christ. Therefore, the host was preserved there from the time of the morning sacrifice until the evening, and it would have remained for the next day if it had not been taken that very night. Since that same host was also carried out from the sanctuary and the altar to the sick man, and since it was also adored by Jerome, then...

the primitive saints <note>The early Christians of the first centuries.</note>, who received it immediately while sitting. They claim those saints retained nothing of the sacrament for sudden cases of mortality, nor did they carry it outside the house. Regarding all of this, the Pighards <note>A term used by Catholic polemicists for the Bohemian Brethren, or Unitas Fratrum.</note> are lying with their fictitious Chronicles. They mention that Origen, as he writes on the third book of Moses <note>Leviticus is the third book of the Pentateuch.</note>—as they call it—says that if anyone spoke about their rural affairs in anything other than the usual words, they would be seen as ignorant of farming. Therefore, let us not have Pighards who cite "the third book of Moses" for the unlearned. I do not know if any among the educated would wish to speak this way; for while they are accustomed to dividing works into numbers where the name and subject of the work is one (yet it receives sections because of the size of the volume—such as the first, second, or third Book of Kings, or the first and second of Chronicles <note>original: "paralipomenon," the Greek-derived name for the Books of Chronicles.</note>, or the Books of the Maccabees), translators of the Holy Scriptures are not accustomed to saying the "first, second, third, fourth, or fifth book of Moses" instead of **Genesis**, **Exodus**, **Leviticus**, **Numbers**, and **Deuteronomy**. Similarly, they do not usually cite the "first, second, and third books of Solomon" for **Proverbs**, **Ecclesiastes**, and the **Song of Songs**. This is a minor matter, yet I wished to note that Pighard’s lack of familiarity with the Sacred Scriptures.

But let us come to Origen. These Pighard men are childish, as they hold onto no authority of the Scriptures but build their treachery out of pure malevolence. Previously, when they ought to have sought the Gospel to believe fully in the power and truth of the sacrament of the body of Christ—as if the Gospel existed nowhere—they never mentioned it. Now, after that point has been passed, and we have come to the matter of sitting, the reservation of the sacrament, and its exportation—as if the whole strength <note>original: "neruus," literally "nerve" or "sinew," meaning the core strength of an argument.</note> of the faith regarding the sacrament rested on these things—some of them have found certain abstruse homilies <note>Sermons intended for a congregation, often interpreting scripture allegorically.</note> of Origen. It seems to me that I have read those homilies quite diligently, yet I did not find the passage they cite in the way they cite it, except in the *Fifth Homily*, where Origen left this written:
> For the Lord also, giving the bread which he gave to the disciples, said to them: "Take and eat." He did not delay, nor did he command it to be saved for the next day. Perhaps this also contains a mystery in that he does not command bread to be carried on the way, so that you may always bring forth fresh breads of the word of God <note>original: "verbi dei panes"</note> which you carry within you. Finally, those Gibeonites <note>A group in the Book of Joshua who tricked the Israelites by bringing dry, moldy bread to pretend they had traveled from a great distance.</note> were condemned for that reason, and became hewers of wood or drawers of water, because they brought old bread to the Israelites, whom the spiritual law commanded always to use what was fresh and new.

Now, when these words of Origen and those of the Pighard are compared, they are so foreign to one another that we can rightly deny that the things the Pighard cited were actually Origen’s, even though he cited them as his. But who would he not corrupt next, after he conceals the truth about the Gospel and leads the Apostle’s captured meanings into his own error? If Origen truly wrote for the Pighards and against us, why did they corrupt him by adding verses? For if he were intact, he would have provided the same point better or with the fullest faith. If he did not write it, why did they corrupt him again and translate the primary teacher of the church against his will into their lies?

Now let us refute the wickedness of the Pighard from that very passage. They say: "Whoever takes this bread of the supper of Christ on the second or third day will not bless their soul but will pollute it." We, however, have previously shown by the example of Saint Jerome <note>A 4th-century scholar and Father of the Church.</note> that because of the sudden necessities of the Christian people, they retained the sacrament from the time of the sacrifice in ancient times. But the Pighards are lying, and Origen did not say that. They add: "For God does not want us to have old breads, but new." This is not in Origen either, but the Pighards added it by their own license. If they did not wish to speak their own words, why did they provoke an innocent writer into another's treachery? Therefore, if they truly felt as the ancients did, we would not call the Pighards heretics like the ancients. Now let us look at our Origen: "He did not delay," he says, "nor did he command it to be saved for the next day." He said only this, and concerning this...

# THE WALDENSIANS: BOOK FIVE

now, by a brief point, they have made a whole victory for themselves, and they think that they have struck us down thoroughly with it. Truly, regarding why Christ did not delay, nor command that it be saved for the next day, we do not need to look far for the cause, nor should we seek it out from our own suspicions. Origen himself says, from the present word <note>Referring to the biblical text at hand.</note>, that it is so that you might bring forth the bread of the Word of God which you carry within you while it is fresh. He intended it, therefore, to be a figure <note>A symbolic representation or type.</note> of a moral institution which we should fulfill in imitation, according to the sense which the Apostle <note>St. Paul.</note> also spoke: **Cleanse out the old leaven, that you may be a new lump, as you are unleavened. For Christ our Passover has been sacrificed. Therefore let us feast, not in the old leaven, nor in the leaven of malice and wickedness, but in the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.** <note>original: "Expurgate vetus fermentum... in azimis sinceritatis & veritatis." Quoting 1 Corinthians 5:7-8.</note> 

The Pighard <note>The author uses "Pighardus" as a singular representative of the Bohemian Brethren.</note>, erasing this proper cause and this moral sense, substituted another that serves his own desire and treachery: namely, that just as Christ commanded nothing to be saved for the next day, so we should retain nothing of His sacrament. Here, if the Church—out of necessity for the faithful <note>Usually referring to the need to have the Host ready for the sick and dying.</note>—preserves this most divine Sacrament, let it by no means be believed, based on the Pighard’s slander, that she acts irreligiously. If the Pighard thinks this must be kept according to the letter, then let him also keep this according to history: that today you should not carry bread for yourself on the road, for Christ also prohibited this from being done.

But let us put an end to this discourse. In the next place, they say that Christ did not give this sacrament for **veneration**. I wonder where they get this from the words of the Lord. For it is not so cautioned in the Gospels that what they object to us is forbidden simply because we venerate it. Truly, I said before that they believe nothing true or pure concerning this sacrament; for if they believed Christ to be there, true and whole according to His nature, it would follow even without the scriptures that they should venerate the present God, prostrate <note>original: "cernui," meaning bowing or falling on one's face.</note>. In the same way, Moses adored God above the propitiatory <note>The "mercy seat" or cover of the Ark of the Covenant.</note>, and finally, he adored before the bush; yet God had not appeared in the bush specifically so that He might be adored, but so that He might appoint Moses as a prophet who would deliver the people of Israel from Egypt. 

Next, they make mention of **both species** <note>original: "utriusque speciei." This refers to the Utraquist controversy—whether laypeople should receive both the bread and the wine (the Cup).</note> under which this sacrament ought to be received. Whether the use of this was formerly the practice in the primitive church, we discussed in the fourth book: that it was neither a commandment of the Gospel that it be done so, nor does the salvation of the believers depend upon it. It could, therefore, later be changed—for other most just causes—into the present use of one species <note>Receiving only the bread, the standard Catholic practice of the time.</note>. Or, if such a use was not in the primitive church, then just as she did not use both species of the sacrament then, we shall not use them today. 

So be it, and let us leave the Pighard to his own suspicion. Yet, he most strongly overturns himself regarding this opinion. For earlier, when he held a discourse on the **breaking of bread**, he remembered the testimony from the Acts of the Apostles: **"They were persevering in the doctrine of the apostles, and in the communication of the breaking of bread and in prayers."** And again: **"Daily continuing with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread from house to house, they took their food with gladness."** <note>Quoting Acts 2:42 and 2:46.</note> The Pighard then explained these passages as referring to the communion of the sacrament. Let us grant them this sense for as long as we are discussing this. Therefore, the general church was not communicated under both species, but only by the "breaking of bread." Thus, I marvel at the blind malevolence of the Pighard, who followed this passage to prove the "breaking of bread," but did not wish to follow the same passage for the use of one species of the sacrament. So, for him, the very same passage must necessarily be seen as suitable for one point but unsuitable for the other; true for one, but a fable for the other. 

Therefore, having been convicted of such great dishonesty, let him cease to object "treachery" and "rebellion" against the innocent. He is the one who resists the Holy Scriptures and heavenly piety; he is the one who, in order to establish heresy, first kicks away, corrupts, and tramples underfoot the Gospel, the apostles, and Christian consensus.

### ON THE SACRAMENT OF THE EUCHARIST AGAINST THE PIGHARDS

We wish to respond to his second writing in this manner and keep to the rule, as in the previous response, that we leave aside his insults and oppressions, and so on, until that place where he asks: "If he is that one, why do they not worship this one as that one?" <note>The author is ignoring personal attacks to focus on the theological question of why the Pighards do not offer the same worship to the consecrated Host that they would offer to Christ in person.</note>

At last, we come to that long-awaited place where the Pighards reveal their open treachery regarding the sacrament of the altar, having set aside the pretense of a better faith. They have departed a little from that usual and painted innocence with which they decorated all the entrances and exits of their work—with which they even weave their present trifles, professing some kind of truth and simplicity in their response. As for the nature of their "truth"—so that I do not call forth as witnesses whatever they might write hereafter—I only call forth those things they have written until now. Those things were certainly found to be related to nothing less than truth, and to nothing more than the most impudent lies. But so it happens while they carry forth their sacrileges according to the spiritual fornication <note>A common biblical metaphor for heresy or unfaithfulness to God.</note> of their own senses. Yet they wish to be thought well of in Christ; but they would boast of that simplicity much more sparingly if they realized it was a fraud stolen from the devil. If their "rustic filth" knows nothing beyond dung and smoke, we do not interpret that as simplicity, but as stupidity and ignorance.

But at last, we are tired of their persistence, and we can by no means refute all those honeyed poisons as often as they put them forward without involving ourselves directly with Pighard himself and the matter at hand. It will now be our purpose that, while they labor to give us an account of their faith, we shall report nothing of a deeper Christian confession there to be refuted in turn. Rather, from the scriptures which they have corrupted against us, and from their own contradictions, we will press the Pighards so that they cannot show those things to be true which they have constructed from nothing but lies. We will bring forward our own matters at the opportune time, after they have begun either to mock or to question us regarding our faith.

Immediately, then, from the beginning they hold this: **"We believe that the bread is the natural and spiritual blessed body of Jesus Christ."** But he [the Pighard author] writes that under that substance of bread and wine the true body and true blood are present, and he claims this has "changed" our faith founded upon the word of Christ.

Hey you, Pighard! If this is now the difference between you and Doctor Augustine <note>Augustin of Olomouc (1467–1513), a fierce opponent of the Bohemian Brethren.</note>, and you are debating over the single word "true" <note>original: "verum"</note>: if you therefore deny this *true* body of Christ and this *true* blood, you who confess another body of Christ and another blood besides the "true" one cannot be true yourself—and in reality, you hold a view that is not founded upon the words of the Lord. We did not previously understand your great frauds—namely, that you believed the body of Christ to be one thing, and the *true* body of Christ to be another. Now, at last, after you accuse Doctor Augustine of "changing" the word "true" in your confession, we have looked into those hiding places where you have hidden your treachery until now. I ask you, Pighard: what kind of body of Christ is this, which you distinguish against His *true* body? Also, what is this great madness of yours, that you complain about the "injury" of a changed word to Doctor Augustine, when you were the first to openly write that word? 

Or does it not read in your Latin confession in these, your own words: **"When indeed a priest, rightly ordained, has expressed the words of Christ’s testimony, immediately the bread is the true, natural body of Christ, taken from the most chaste Virgin, which was to be delivered <term>traditurum</term> [about to deliver], just as the living bread testifies: 'This is,' He says, 'my body, which will be delivered for you'; similarly the wine is the blood of His natural body, which was poured out for the remission of sins, for many."** 

It is pleasing rather to note the foul barbarism <note>The author is mocking the Pighard writer’s poor Latin grammar.</note> in this Pighard; he says: "which was to be delivered" <note>original: "quod erat traditurum"</note>. Words of this mode and nature signify that someone will act in the future, not suffer. But Christ was not "about to deliver" [as an active agent of the betrayal] but was Himself "to be delivered" <note>original: "tradendus"</note>. We gladly note faults of that kind...

...whereby he who speaks barbarously <note>original: "barbare loquitur"; a critique of the linguistic skills and perceived lack of education of the Bohemian Brethren</note> believes more poorly; but let the Pighard stop boasting to us that he holds whatever all the most esteemed ecclesiastical writers have written as Catholic. For since these men are Latin—or indeed, most fluent in Latin—it could not be that by reading them, the Pighard would not also become more Latinate. But let us return to the matter. Do you not then say that the bread is immediately the true body of Christ? Finally, in that *Apologia* of yours, you write:

┌ **Immediately the present bread is the body of Christ offered for us unto death; likewise the present wine is his blood poured out for the remission of sins.** ┘

Was any other body than the true body of Christ offered unto death? Was any other blood than the true blood of Christ poured out from the scourges, the nails, and the spear? What madness is this then, Pighard, that after these words you should contend against us over a single word—"true"—and that you should shift your ground and say you are excluded from your own confession? How openly malevolent you are, and how lyingly entangled! Next, the Pighard complains with the same pen that Doctor Augustine <note>Augustin of Olomouc (1467–1513), a prominent Moravian humanist and fierce opponent of the Bohemian Brethren</note> did not fear to change even their own confessions and to arrogantly claim that the Pighard preaches that no honor ought to be shown to the body and blood of Christ in the sacrament. 

Do they not, therefore, preach this very thing? I do not wish to call them to witness because they previously contended against us that the primitive church did not practice the veneration of the sacrament; which they finally said as their own opinion:

┌ **This Sacrament of the body and blood of Christ was not given for veneration, so that it should be adored there; he who sits at the right hand of God in the higher places ought to be adored with the Father and the Holy Spirit.** ┘

I do not wish to cite those things which we have struck out from their proper place; rather, I will produce their own confessions. There, they certainly left it written:

┌ **To worship the sacramental subsistence of the body and blood is no command delivered to the believers. For Christ gave it to the disciples as they reclined to be used; obeying him, they ate and drank without such worship of the sacrament. And again in the *Apologia*: It is one thing to worship him as we greatly fear him alone residing at the right hand with the Father and the Holy Spirit.** ┘

Let us consider here, I beseech you, the impudent face of the Pighard, how he has wiped away every blush of shame from it. He makes Doctor Augustine guilty of a "changed confession," though Augustine did not depart by a single point from their own writing. No one who did not compare the last things with the first would believe that they would dare to lie so openly against their own conscience, and to say that what their predecessors wrote was fabricated by another. I also wanted to note down every single lie of the Pighard by number, but their frequency has shaken my memory; and I see that I must labor enough just to receive these things, however undigested they have placed them in my hands. Someone else will hereafter find an assessment who will gather everything into one, place it before our eyes, and judge how their treachery—which has fashioned, equipped, and composed itself with nothing but the most impure lies—can stand according to the Evangelical faith, simplicity, and innocence.

Regarding the fact that communion should be received under both kinds <term>sub utraque specie: the practice of the laity receiving both the consecrated bread and the wine, a central demand of the Bohemian Reformation</term>, as the Pighard says: in what way have they dared this, unless out of malevolent contention? For why does the Pighard not take the species separately according to the form of Apostolic communion—namely, the body of Christ separately and his blood separately—but instead takes a morsel of bread soaked in the wine? <note>original: "intinctum panem de offa"; the author critiques the Pighards for using intinction (dipping the bread) while claiming to follow Apostolic "purity."</note> But such is the custom of a heretic: after he holds views most alienated from the truth of the sacrament, he finally desires to be held as "Apostolic" in its use. 

We say, therefore, as is possible: It is not necessary for the Christian people to communicate under both kinds. For Christ spoke of both: "Amen, amen, I say to you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you shall not have life in you; he who eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life." # ON THE SACRAMENT OF THE EUCHARIST AGAINST [THE PIGHARDS]

"If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever" <note>original: "Si quis manducat ex hoc pane vivet in eternum"; John 6:51</note>. These most wicked heretics, although they ought to have bound us to the command of the Gospel regarding the use of the Sacrament, nevertheless remained silent, as if such clear testimony existed nowhere. Truly, they feared that if they cited the Gospel by name for their own cause, we might be reminded of that very place. And so we would cite from the same text against them that Christ, regarding the reception of the Sacrament, had left it to be understood as being under one species <note>The author is defending the Catholic practice of "Communion in one kind" (bread only for the laity) against the Hussite/Pighard demand for the chalice (wine).</note>. But of this we spoke more extensively in the fourth book. 

After those things, those "truth-telling" <term>Pighards<gloss>A derogatory name for the Bohemian Brethren (Unitas Fratrum), a group following the teachings of Jan Hus.</gloss></term> ask whether we might penetrate into their hearts and make them more wicked through their treachery. Certainly, neither Saint Augustine nor we, through this work of ours, penetrate into their hearts, nor do we speak anything against them based on presumed suspicion; rather, we confute their own treachery from their manifest words and deeds. They themselves, from their soul to the point of the pen, and from the pen to the writing, are all full of the blood of impiety. Therefore, let them cease imploring the simple common folk to believe and think that the Pighards are made harmful only by the accusations of others and not by their own wicked deeds. They also mention their own priests; but as for those priests of theirs, we have long since cast them out to Calvary in our fourth book. 

Moreover, they confess in that *Apologia* <note>A reference to the "Apologia" or confession of faith published by the Bohemian Brethren to defend their beliefs to King Wladislaus II.</note> of theirs that they have made a departure from the Roman Church. Yet this most divine Sacrament is the sacrament of the union of the members of the Church with Christ the head, according to what the Apostle wrote: "The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the participation in the blood of Christ? And the bread which we break, is it not the participation in the body of the Lord?" <note>original: "calix benedictionis cui benedicimus... panis quem frangimus..."; 1 Corinthians 10:16</note>. Therefore, schismatics, heretics, and whoever exists in a state of departure do not communicate in the body and blood of Christ. 

However, they think they do not dare go to priests who are opposed to them—certainly no one opposes them, but rather they themselves, while they were among us, began to stand in opposition against us. Nevertheless, they accuse the priests of things contrary to the faith. To that accusation we responded in the fourth book, yet we say even now: if, on account of the "iniquitous faith" of our people, they do not receive the ecclesiastical sacraments under Apostolic obedience, then they should not receive the sacraments under schismatic priests either. Therefore, the sin of those men and of our own would be the same, since—these are the words of the Pighard—they minister the sacraments "for a purpose other than what Christ intended." 

Where then do those "Old Bohemians" remain now, whom the Pighard in another place calls good and holy men? If he was not here scratching another’s itch, and if they were truly good and holy according to his opinion—and holiness does not deceive—let him follow the faith of the saints. But if he does not follow them just as he does not follow us, then he does not dare go to them just as he does not go to those opposed to him, and he believes their faith is not true. For to believe and yet still stand apart does not befit a good conscience. True piety does not permit schismatics to follow those whom they do not believe. Finally, what he wrote in that epilogue he has confessed: 

<insert>┌</insert> **From which it is easily understood,** says the Pighard, **that those who are always closer to the equity of faith and to that narrow way which leads to life are those who suffer for the sake of equity, rather than those who, for the sake of it, disturb others according to their own opinion.** ┘

If, therefore, Apostolic obedience made Bohemia flourishing, blessed, and tranquil; if the Bohemian Christians remained tranquil until, through the crime of another, they could no longer remain so and disturbed no one; if for the sake of the heavenly faith they suffered all extremes under the robbery of others; if, however, there was rebellion and a betrayed sacrament; if Hus <note>Jan Hus (c. 1369–1415), the Czech reformer whose execution sparked the Hussite Wars.</note>, Jacobellus <note>Jacobellus of Mies (1372–1429), a colleague of Hus who advocated for communion in both kinds (bread and wine).</note>, Rokycana <note>Jan Rokycana (c. 1396–1471), the Hussite Archbishop of Prague.</note>, Žižka <note>Jan Žižka (c. 1360–1424), the famous one-eyed (later blind) general of the Hussite armies.</note>, the two Procopiuses <note>Procopius the Great and Procopius the Lesser, Hussite generals who led the "Warriors of God" after Žižka's death.</note>, the schismatics, the Orphans, the Orebites, the Adamites <note>Radical sects and military factions of the Hussite movement; the Adamites were an extremist group famously suppressed by Žižka himself.</note>, and the Pighards—men who are deserters and treacherous regarding the profaned honor of God and the saints; if they themselves are sacrilegious, having violated the reverence of their ancestors in the sacred King and the tombs; if they are robbers and executioners who corrupted the fortunes of citizens and shed blood; if those men, cruel barbarians in all things, desolated, fouled, and impoverished their own fatherland of Bohemia—once remarkable and happy for its density of citizens and cities, its splendor, and its abundance—with plundering, fires, devastation, and the capital persecution of Christian blood: 

Then they are the ones, by their own decree, O Pighard, who depart from Heavenly Piety and the way which leads to life! Let him therefore cease to earn the goodwill of others through lying titles; let him instead at some point stand before his conscience and remain by one certain decree on who the saints are.

# WALDENSIANS: BOOK FIVE

<note>original: "VALDENSES LIBER QVINTVS"</note>

...calls those holy forever who are not holy, and those he does not call holy. They boast then that they do whatever is commanded by the Son of God. Certainly, the Pighards <gloss>A derogatory term for the Bohemian Brethren, or "Unitas Fratrum," a pre-Reformation Christian group.</gloss> lie there, who so often dissemble regarding the Gospel. But it does not immediately follow that if something is not specifically commanded, it must not be done. In the Gospel, the Lord calls those "useless servants" who have done only what they were obliged to do <note>original: "servos inutiles dicit, qui quod debuerunt facere id tantū fecerūt"; Luke 17:10</note>. Therefore, other things remain to be done beyond what we have a command for—things toward which Paul extended himself, forgetting those which were behind <note>referencing Philippians 3:13</note>. 

Finally, many things are taught by implication: Moses above the mercy seat; Abraham and Lot meeting the angels; the man born blind adoring Christ in the flesh. These were done outside of any specific command, yet because they confessed a present divinity, they offered adoration. And if the Pighards truly believed, according to the truth of the Gospel, that Christ—both God and man—is present in the **sacrament of the altar**, they would adore Christ as God and man without any hesitation. 

Furthermore, when they claim that the apostles "passed through houses and broke bread"—interpreting this as the **Sacrament**, as the Pighards do—they err, and it is outside all historical truth. Regarding what they wish to argue to us from the *Acts of the Apostles*—that they were "breaking bread from house to house"—they certainly misunderstand this passage, as well as the following: "And the first Christians took their food with gladness" <note>original: "Et summebant cibum cum exultatione"; Acts 2:46</note>. Rather, these were converts from the Jews; just as they had given their possessions in common, so they lived in common. And since there were many thousands of believers, they necessarily lived together in many groups, rather than in one single place or monastery. Through these fellowships, just as they shared every other necessity, they shared the communal living of the table; and thus they "broke bread from house to house." 

As we explained in the next section, it happened that the Hebrew widows, out of national partiality, were cared for more diligently than the Greek ones. The Greeks complained of this to the council, and the apostles replied that it was not right for them to leave the Word of God to "serve tables." Thus, they appointed seven deacons for that domestic distribution <note>This refers to the origin of the diaconate in Acts 6</note>. Such is the true sense of history. For the idea that the apostles withdrew themselves from the celebration of the Mystery <note>The Eucharist</note>, or that they allowed the deacons to do it (which is against sacred law), or that they shared communion more zealously with Hebrew women than Greek, or that they celebrated the **sacrifice of the altar** in any profane place whatsoever as the Pighards do—this is beyond the belief of any history.

Consequently, they say: "And they [the apostles] did not show reverence." Perhaps the Pighards know what the apostles did at the **Lord’s Supper**; but after the mission of the Holy Spirit and the establishment of ecclesiastical ceremonies, they know nothing at all of what the apostles and Christians did in veneration of this Sacrament, and they make things up of their own. 

For if, because the apostles did not adore the Sacrament [at that moment], Christians today shall not adore the Sacrament, then—by the same Pighard sophism <note>A "sophism" is a clever but false argument.</note>—because the apostles did not adore Christ while He was present in the flesh and living with them, we Christians today shall not adore our Savior Jesus Christ. Again, if because the apostles did not venerate the Sacrament, does it mean Christ is not in the Sacrament according to His true nature? By the same Pighard sophism: because the apostles did not adore Christ at that same Supper, Christ as God and man would not have been there in His own nature. If they had believed Him to be God and man, they would have been ready to adore Him. 

Do you finally understand, O Christian people, the deceits and frauds of the diabolical Pighard, by which he lays snares for you regarding the truth of the sacrament we must confess? Therefore, we proceed against the Pighard, the enemy of God and Christ. Although the apostles, by their own temporary privilege, might not have adored Him at some time, nevertheless we truly adore Christ as God and man wherever we truly confess Him. 

But let us hear next the horrible blasphemies which the Pighards use in their fight against God. "It is commanded," he says, "that they honor Jesus Christ, true God and man, not in the very subsistence of the blessing in the sacrament, but in His own natural and corporal substance of God." Now, therefore, as I hear, they distinguish the sacrament from Christ...

# ON THE SACRAMENT OF THE EUCHARIST AGAINST THE HERETICS

"If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever." <note>original: "Si quis manducat ex hoc pane vivet in aeternum"; John 6:51</note> The worst heretics, though they ought to have bound us to the sacrament by the precept of the Gospel, nevertheless kept silent about this most present testimony as if it existed nowhere. Namely, they were afraid that where they cited the Gospel by name on their own behalf, we would be reminded of the passage and cite it back against them from nearby—that Christ, regarding the sacrament under one species <gloss>The practice of receiving only the bread (Host), rather than both bread and wine</gloss>, had left us moved by suspicion. However, we have said more about this in the fourth book.

Those truth-telling Pighards <gloss>A derogatory term for the Bohemian Brethren, a pre-Reformation Christian group</gloss> ask that we penetrate into their hearts and make them even more criminal through their perfidy. But neither Doctor Augustine nor we, by this work of ours, penetrate into their hearts, nor do we speak anything about them based on presumed suspicion. Rather, we refute their own perfidy from their manifest words and deeds. They themselves, from their soul to their articles of faith, from their pen to their writing, are all full of the blood of impiety. Why do they not stop imploring the simple common people to believe and think these things? 

The Pighards record that they are not made harmful by another's accusation, but by their own crime, even though they have their own priests. We, however, have long ago cast those priests of theirs into Calvary <note>An allusion to execution or condemnation</note> in our fourth book. But also, because in that apology of theirs, they confess they have made a departure from the Roman Church—and this most divine sacrament is the **sacrament of the union** of the members of the Church with the head, Christ, according to what the Apostle <gloss>St. Paul</gloss> wrote: "The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communication of the blood of Christ? And the bread which we break, is it not the participation in the body of the Lord?" <note>1 Corinthians 10:16</note>. Therefore, schismatics, heretics, and whoever is in a state of separation do not communicate in the body and blood of Christ. 

They think, however, that they dare not go to the priests who are opposed to them—certainly no one opposes them; rather, while they were among us, they began to stand against us from the opposite side. Nevertheless, they accuse the priests of things contrary to the faith. We answered that accusation in the fourth book, yet we say now: if they do not receive the ecclesiastical sacraments under apostolic obedience because of the "unjust faith" of our priests, why then do they receive sacraments under schismatic priests? Their sin and ours would then be the same, since—these are the words of the Pighards—the words are administered for something other than Christ’s intention. 

Where then do those old Bohemians <term>Bohemians: In this context, the followers of the martyred reformer Jan Hus</term> remain, whom the Pighard calls good and holy men in another place? If he was not scratching another's itch here, and if they were good and holy in his opinion—and holiness does not deceive—let him follow the faith of the holy. But if he does not follow them as he does not follow us, then he does not dare go to them as if they were opposed to him, and he does not believe their faith to be true. For it does not befit a good conscience to believe and yet stand apart. Truly, piety should have been followed, but certainly, true piety does not permit schismatics to not follow those in matters of belief. 

Finally, what he wrote in that epilogue he has confessed <insert>^</insert> from which it is easily understood, says the Pighard, that they are always closer to the equity of faith and to that narrow way which leads to life, because they suffer for equity's sake, rather than those who, because of it, disturb others according to their opinion. 

If, therefore, apostolic obedience made Bohemia flourishing, blessed, and tranquil; if the Christian Bohemians could remain tranquil through another's crime and disturbed no one; if they suffered all extremes under the robbery of others for the sake of the heavenly faith... but if rebellion and the betrayed sacrament... if **Hus**, **Jakoubek**, **Rokycana**, **Žižka**, the two **Procopiuses**, the **Orphans**, the **Orebites**, the **Adamites**, the **Pighards** <note>These are names of various leaders and factions within the Hussite movement in 15th-century Bohemia who fought in the Hussite Wars (1419–1434).</note>—men who are deserters and faithless from the profaned honor of God and the saints; from the reverence of their elders in the sacred kingdom; and, with tombs violated, impious and sacrilegious; from the corrupted fortunes of citizens and the shedding of blood, robbers and executioners; if those cruel barbarians in all things desolated, defiled, and impoverished their own Bohemia—once spectacular and happy for the frequency, splendor, and abundance of its citizens, cities, and all things—by robberies, fires, devastations, and the capital persecution of Christian blood: then they are the ones, by decree, Pighards, who fall away from Christian Heavenly Piety and the way that leads to life. 

Let him cease, therefore, to earn the goodwill of others with false titles, but let him at last be with his conscience and remain by one certain decree, and those whom [he calls] holy...

-># THE WALDENSIANS: BOOK FIVE<-

...continually calls those people holy whom God does not call holy, nor does he call them unholy. They then boast that they do whatever has been commanded by the Son of God; certainly, those Pighards <note>A derogatory term used for the Bohemian Brethren, a pre-Reformation group that influenced the later Reformation</note> lie there, who so often practice deception regarding the Gospel. But even if something is not explicitly commanded, it does not immediately follow that it should not be done. The Lord in the Gospel calls them "useless servants" <note>original: "servos inutiles"; Luke 17:10</note> who have only done that which they were required to do. Therefore, other things remain to be done beyond what we have a command for, toward which Paul extended himself, "forgetting those things which were behind." <note>Philippians 3:13</note> Finally, many things are commanded by implication: Moses adored God above the mercy seat; Abraham and Lot adored the angels who met them; the man born blind adored Christ in the flesh—all outside of any explicit command, but they adored because they confessed a present divinity. And if the Pighards believed that Christ, God and man, was present in the Sacrament of the Altar according to the rite and the truth of the Gospel, they would adore Christ, God and man, without hesitation.

But as for why the Apostles went through houses and "broke bread"—which is how the Pighards interpret the Sacrament—they err, and it is outside all historical truth. When they try to use that passage from the Acts of the Apostles against us—"breaking bread in their houses" <note>original: "frangentes circa domos panem"; Acts 2:46</note>—they certainly understand this passage poorly, as well as the one following: "And they took their food with gladness." The first Christians, and even more so the converts from the Jews, lived in common just as they had given up their possessions to the community. And since there were many thousands of believers, they lived together in many groups by necessity, not in just any one single place or monastery. Through these shared living quarters, just as they shared every other necessity, they shared their meals in common; and so they "broke bread throughout the houses." Here, as we explained in the very next section, it happened that the widows of the Hebrews, because of national affection, were cared for more diligently than those of the Greeks. The Greeks complained about this to the council, to which the Apostles responded that it was not right for them to leave the word of God to "serve tables." <note>Acts 6:2</note> Then they appointed seven deacons to that domestic distribution. 

Such is the true sense of history. For it is outside the faith of all history to suggest that the Apostles withdrew themselves from the celebration of the Mystery <gloss>The Eucharist</gloss>; or that they permitted that task to the deacons contrary to the law of sacred rites; or that they gave communion to the Hebrews more studiously than the Greeks; or that they celebrated the sacrifice of the altar in any profane places whatsoever, just as the Pighards do. 

Consequently, they say: "And they did not show reverence," referring to what the Apostles did at the Lord's Supper. Perhaps the Pighards know this secret. But truly, after the mission of the Holy Spirit, after the ecclesiastical ceremonies were established, they are entirely ignorant of what the Apostles and the Christians did in veneration of this Sacrament, and they make things up of their own accord. For if the Pighards use the sophistry <note>A clever but false argument</note> that because the Apostles did not adore the Sacrament, Christians today should not adore the Sacrament, then by the same sophistry, because the Apostles did not adore Christ while he was present in the flesh and living with them, we Christians today should not adore our Savior Jesus Christ. Again, if the fact that the Apostles did not venerate the Sacrament means that Christ is not in the Sacrament according to his true nature, then by that same sophistry, because the Apostles did not adore Christ at that same Supper, Christ—God and man—was not there in his own nature. For the Apostles, being men, would have adored him as God and man if they had believed it so. 

Finally, do you understand, O Christian people, the snares and frauds of the diabolical Pighard, by which he lays traps for you regarding the truth of the Sacrament to be confessed? We walk, therefore, through the Pighard, an enemy to God and Christ. Even though the Apostles, out of their own temporary privilege, did not adore him at one time, we nevertheless truly confess and truly adore Christ, God and man, wherever he is. But let us hear next the horrible blasphemies which the Pighards use in their fight against God. "It is commanded," he says, "that they honor Jesus Christ, true God and man, not in the very <term>subsistence</term> <gloss>The state of being or underlying reality of a thing</gloss> of the blessing in the Sacrament, but in his natural and corporal substance of God." Now, therefore, as I hear it, they distinguish the Sacrament from Christ...

-># ON THE SACRAMENT OF THE EUCHARIST AGAINST<-
->## THE PIGHARDS<-

Why, then, have they so often previously confessed that after the words of consecration <note>original: "consecrationis"</note>, Christ is present under the sacrament according to His entire nature, just as He came forth from the Virgin, suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified and died? Or did they not lie then? And yet they now complain so severely that their confession has been changed regarding a single word, so that we are now forced to believe that to confess all these truths in this sacrament is more wicked than to confess what is untrue. Therefore, let them correct one confession to match the meaning of the other; however, they must have lied in one of them. They should not be angry if we accuse them so many times of an impudent lie. They say, moreover, that there is no command that we should honor Him in the Sacrament. I demand Scripture from these Pighards <note>A derogatory term for the Bohemian Brethren, used here by the author to paint them as stubborn heretics</note>—those Pighards who wish to feel and say nothing outside the words of the Lord. But since they bring forward nothing, just as they say there is no command outside of Scripture, I say the opposite: because it is not forbidden for us to honor Christ in the Sacrament. 

Yet they play around with a few verses of Scripture, and lying about their own impiety under a different color, they say: "You shall adore the Lord your God, and Him only shall you serve." <note>Matthew 4:10</note> Most wicked heretics! Since they now strike at us with this testimony regarding the veneration of the Sacrament, they must also today cast out the adoration of Christ—as they once did with the saints and the Virgin Mary—as "idolatry." And will Christ be in the Sacrament (other than what they have confessed), and not at all our Lord and God? But why do I say "other than what they have confessed," when they confess nothing at all? For Christ will not be in the Sacrament according to the truth of His nature, despite His own words: *This is my body.* I had intended to say more here concerning the adoration of the sacrament, but since they put forward even more wicked things, I shall defer these points of ours to those.

They say, however: "That all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father." <note>John 5:23</note> These malicious Pighards use a certain sophism <term>sophism: a clever but false argument intended to deceive</term> based on the single word "as" <note>original: "sicut"</note>. They contend that just as the Father is not adored except in heaven, so also the Son ought not to be adored except in heaven. Now, if this comparison is not according to the nature of adoration—whereby we receive the command concerning the Son just as we do concerning the Father: "You shall adore the Lord your God and Him only shall you serve"—but is instead understood as referring to local or similar incidental circumstances, I say that by the same fraud of the Pighard, just as no one honored the Father in the person of a human nature, so no one will honor the Son in the person of a human nature. This is a witnessed impiety! Therefore, Pighard, you must necessarily either take back this lie which you have constructed for yourself from this Scripture, or you must cast Christ, the power of God the Father, out from divine honor. 

You see your tunnels <note>original: "cuniculos"; here referring to "shifty schemes" or "hidden paths" of argument</note>, you wicked Pighard! But let us pursue the rest. You say: "No one honored the Father in a creature" <note>A "creature" in this context refers to any created thing or physical manifestation</note>. You lie entirely in this assumption, since divinity *has* been adored in a creature. For when the angels came to Abraham as he sat at the door of the tent, and when they also came to Lot in Sodom—whether they were the Trinity of God in an assumed figure, or angels representing the person of God—certainly divinity was adored there in a creature. For it is written: "And he adored upon the ground and said: Lord, if I have found grace in your eyes..." <note>Genesis 18:2-3</note> And again, when he had seen them, "he rose and went to meet them and adored prone on the ground." <note>Genesis 19:1</note> Let us not think that this was merely a human greeting of respect; they certainly either recognized the divine presence and adored, or, as Lot says afterward: "I pray, my Lord, because your servant has found grace before you, and you have magnified your glory and shown mercy to me to save my soul." Finally, Abraham much more aptly confesses the present God, of whom it is written: "But Abraham still stood before the Lord and, drawing near, said: Will you destroy the just with the wicked? It is not yours, you who judge all the earth, by no means should you perform this judgment." Where does the Pighard stay now? Let him now return to us and say: "No one here honored the Father in a creature," if he can from this word...

...if he is true, why does he not produce scriptures? But if he is false, why does he bring forth false things beyond scripture and conscience? Finally, those Pighards <note>A derogatory name for the Bohemian Brethren</note>, the deniers of divine veneration, contend that Christ did not compel men to adore Him. If the Pighards think that only that which Christ compels them to do should be done, then I no longer wonder why they believe nothing at all; truly, they are continually tossed about by the dizziness of their own senses like a ball from one opinion to another. 

But let the Pighards say: for what does God ever compel men? He certainly wished His Gospel to be received by the world, yet He compelled no one to receive it. For God from the beginning established man and "left him in the hand of his own counsel." <note>A reference to Ecclesiasticus 15:14 regarding free will</note> He added His mandates and precepts. If you wish to keep the commandments, they shall preserve you. Before man is life and death, good and evil. Therefore, He allowed all nations in past generations to walk in their own ways. So, why do they lie in wait for us regarding whether Christ compels us? Let them rather show if He forbade those who adored Him. But if He did not forbid it, it is not a sin, for Christ did not disapprove of it among pious minds. And if we here in the sacrament adore Christ, we sin against no example of scripture or the saints, nor do we adore anyone other than Him who is in heaven. For just as we worship the Divinity—which is not contained by any place, but is truly existing everywhere and filling all things—yet we adore that Divinity in heaven (that is, remaining in His most inward places, neither departing nor divided from Himself). So, wherever Christ may exist by His omnipotence, we adore Him as He sits at the right hand of the Father in His greater goods; from which He neither withdraws, being once blessed, nor is He spread thin, whether He is adored in any one place or in many different places at once. 

They mention that passage: "Thou shalt not make for thyself a graven image" <note>Exodus 20:4; original: "non facies tibi sculptile"</note>. Are we therefore criminals for the veneration of our Redeemer? And shall the Pighards—who cast this most divine Sacrament away from being a "graven image" <note>The author is mocking the Pighards' claim that the consecrated host is an idol</note> into execrable idolatry—not be criminals? Indeed, they are most wicked, and the weight of this most atrocious blasphemy escapes the narrowness of human understanding; for here the Pighards turn against the majesty of Christ, defiled by every diabolical filth. Truly, I would not have expected that after that "graven image" (which they formerly claimed as an insult to the saints and the glorious Virgin Mary), they would return to such a horrendous blasphemy even against Christ. But their madness did not stop at the first impiety; rather, they return, and with that same scripture by which the Holy Spirit through the Prophets strikes and condemns the worship of demons, they also pursue Christ, true God and man, forever blessed. They labor to seize Him and cast Him out of legitimate adoration. 

Furthermore, they dare to lie about the primitive saints, claiming that they also acted this way and did not err. In this, the primitive saints truly did not err, for they neither felt nor did things similar to the Pighard. Therefore, if that impure man maintains a faith that is different and unknown to the newborn Church, he should not be indignant if he is held to be a heretic, standing alone without example. But let us approach Moses; let us see if this most divine sacrament is a "graven image," so that afterwards, regarding its veneration, the prophet

### ON THE SACRAMENT OF THE EUCHARIST AGAINST [THE PIGHARDS]

God is nothing if not truth; therefore, all things are true again in the sacrament, whatever he said they were. For he said, **This is my body** <note>original: "Hoc est corpus meũ"</note>; this, therefore, concerns natural existence. We believe it is present there because he spoke and it was done. But Pighardus escapes from us under that one brief word, "body." Since that word also signifies the unity of the church with Christ as the head, according to the sense which the Apostle also spoke: **because we, being many, are one bread and one body, all of us who partake of one bread and one chalice.** <note>A reference to 1 Corinthians 10:17, used by the Pighards to argue the bread is merely a symbol of the community.</note> However, Pighardus contends that only this mystical Body of Christ—and nothing else—lies beneath the sacramental species <note>The term "species" refers to the outward appearances of bread and wine that remain after the substance has changed.</note>. In this, he errs blindly, for the Savior also said, **This is my blood of the new testament, which will be shed for many.** <note>Mark 14:24</note> This unity of the church in Christ the head is not spoken of as "blood" in a mystical sense. Unless, therefore, Christ is present in his true nature under the species of wine, there will be nothing else that we can confess as Christ's blood there, and the church would be pushed back from the Lord's words into that previous fiction. Therefore, just as we confess the natural blood, so we confess that the natural body of Christ is contained under the species of the sacrament.

Furthermore, in another place, he called this body of his "flesh." **My flesh is truly food and my blood is truly drink.** <note>John 6:55</note> Now, "flesh" is not used metaphorically to signify the mystical body of the church, but signifies only the nature of Christ, by which he is God and man in personal existence, according to the sense the Evangelist spoke: **And the Word was made flesh.** <note>John 1:14</note> Therefore, just as the flesh of Christ is true in the Sacrament, and his blood is true, so his body is true there, for the flesh and blood of Christ *is* that body. Again, just as the body of Christ is true there, so his divinity is true there, regarding which he said: **I am the living bread who descended from heaven.** <note>John 6:51</note> For the body of Christ did not descend from heaven, but his divinity did. If, therefore, he who said, **He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life,** also said, **This is my body**—and if he who said, "This is my body," also said, "I am the living bread who descended from heaven"—it follows that the whole Christ, true God and man, is in the sacrament of the altar. And we adore him, just as it was commanded: **You shall adore the Lord your God, and him only shall you serve.** <note>Matthew 4:10</note> Truly, our Christ in the Sacrament is not an idol; truly Moses does not strike us with the command, **you shall not make for yourself a graven image.** <note>Exodus 20:4. The author is arguing that adoring the Host is not idolatry because Christ is truly there.</note> It is only Pighardus—an enemy of divinity and a betrayer of Christ's majesty, following his master the devil—who rejects Christ in the Sacrament as if he were a graven image, and assigns him to the idols of demons.

Pighardus, a portion of the Antichrist, what has he left for himself now from this supreme battle against God? He holds and calls Christ in the sacrament an idol and a graven image, alien to all holiness. Just as the Antichrist will one day try to push Christ out of his majesty, so in other places Pighardus falsely claims a certain "heavenly ray" is spread through him across every page—just as the Antichrist will one day arrogantly claim the name of God for himself. He prepares everything with lies, just as the Antichrist will appear **according to the working of Satan, in all power and signs and lying wonders, and in all seduction of iniquity.** <note>2 Thessalonians 2:9-10</note> Behold now, into what desperate straits Pighardus has fallen because of this "graven image": since he previously confessed that after the words of consecration <note>original: "consecraciõis"</note> the true body and blood of Christ are present under the species of bread and wine—just as he was born of the Virgin, suffered, was crucified, and died—it is now easier for him to retract such a confessed truth of the Sacrament and think that God deals with us in this Sacrament with fictions and statues and things that do not exist at all, than to remain in that sense, confessing the presence of Christ in his true nature in the Sacrament, and yet casting him out as an idol and a portion of demons. Neither...

<meta>This page continues the author's polemic against the "Pighards" (Bohemian Brethren), moving from a defense of the literal nature of the Eucharist to an accusation that the Pighards are distorting the Gospel by applying Christ's warnings about false messiahs to the Sacrament itself.</meta>

# THE WALDENSIANS: BOOK FIVE

They are not even content to have provoked Christ's majesty over a carved image <note>original: "sculptili"; likely referring to the use of icons or the physical nature of the host</note>. But they also, for his sake, corrupt the Gospel into a perverse sense. That which was predicted by the Truth <note>Christ</note> himself regarding the Antichrist—the head of all evils—namely: **"Then if anyone says to you, 'Behold, here is Christ,' or 'there,' do not believe it,"** <note>Matthew 24:23</note> these most filthy Pighards have now twisted to deny the majesty of Christ. They suggest that Christ must have necessarily divided himself from himself, or that he warned believers to beware of himself as if he were the Antichrist.

O pestilential tongue! O tongue that should be burned out by the fires of hell! O **faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you**—says Christ—**and endure you?** <note>Matthew 17:17</note> They extort a false meaning from the words of the Eternal Gospel. They corrupt the Scriptures following the example of their master, the devil. Satan said to Christ: **"Throw yourself down, for it is written: He has given his angels charge over you, and in their hands they shall bear you up, lest you dash your foot against a stone."** <note>Matthew 4:6</note> Satan said this to Christ only because he believed it would lead to seduction; however, he remained silent about the part that followed regarding his own trampling: **"You shall walk upon the asp and the basilisk, and you shall trample the lion and the dragon."** <note>Psalm 91:13</note>

In the same way, the Pighards bring forward only that which they can isolate for a contrary meaning. They have suppressed the immediate context which would have kept the quoted verse within its legitimate sense. For in the immediate context it is read: **"There shall be then great tribulation, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, nor ever shall be; and unless those days had been shortened, no flesh would be saved."** <note>Matthew 24:21-22</note> Certainly, there is no tribulation today so remarkable or so atrocious in the world that even more grievous examples have not preceded it, and worse things could happen in the future.

Nor is this time—under which it is said, **"This is my body, this is the blood of the new testament,"** which is the same as saying, "Here is Christ in the sacrament"—as "short" as the Savior predicted that future tribulation would be. For this confession has endured in the Church from the time it was said: **"Unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you shall not have life in you."** <note>John 6:53</note> Therefore, the Pighards have most wickedly corrupted the words of the Gospel into their own distorted sense. It would follow that the prophecy of Christ would be false, both regarding that most grave tribulation (the likes of which has certainly not yet happened to the world) and regarding the time (which he said would be very short, yet has lasted over fifteen hundred years).

But the truth of the Prophecy remains unshaken. Therefore, when the Pighards translate what was said above regarding the Sacrament of the Altar—which they now blasphemously call a "false Christ"—they necessarily lie. Therefore, let the cursed Pighards finally hear a better judgment: If anyone says to you, "Christ is with Sabellius," <note>A 3rd-century heretic who taught that the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit were not distinct persons</note> or "He is with Arius," <note>A 4th-century priest who denied the full divinity of Christ</note> or "He is with the Pighard," or "with the schismatics," or "with all the masters of lies"—**do not go out and do not believe them.**

If, in the final time of the world, someone speaks of the Antichrist, the head of all evils, saying: **"Behold, here is Christ,"** or **"there,"** or **"behold, he is in the desert,"** do not go out; **"behold, he is in the inner rooms,"** do not believe it. **For false Christs and false prophets shall arise.** <note>Matthew 24:24-26</note> However, there is nothing false in the flesh, nor the blood, nor the body, nor the soul and divinity of Christ. Thus, they can never rightfully or piously cast this Body of Christ—which is in the sacrament—into the category of a "false Christ."

When they conceived such headlong blasphemies and committed them to writing, it is a wonder if their senses did not shudder, if a great darkness did not flicker before their eyes, or if their hands and pens did not tremble. Or perhaps all these things did happen, but the demon was more powerful in their possessed minds and overcame their senses, even as they recoiled. I am moved to pity here by the supine negligence of those who, having this most deadly Pighard plague in their power, listen so calmly to those intolerable blasphemies against Christ and his divinity, while they would not suffer their own personal reputation to be diminished by a hand's breadth or by laws. But I pray, let them wake up! For they cannot be ignorant of these things...

-># ON THE SACRAMENT OF THE EUCHARIST: AGAINST<-

The letters sent by this Pighard <note>A derogatory term for the Bohemian Brethren or Waldensians</note> to these people were concerning these matters. Therefore, I pray, if there is any strength <note>original: "nervus"</note> left in those who wish to be called Christians and who have been redeemed by the blood of Christ: let them rise up against such great blasphemies! Let them, out of reverence for Christ, prohibit and avenge them. Let them avenge them as faithfully as they wish God to be merciful to them in death, rather than sending them to Gehenna <note>Hell</note> and perpetual torments. Just as they wish God to be present and merciful to them then, let them now faithfully defend the Divine Majesty against those horrible blasphemies.

Nevertheless, those wicked despisers of the Divine Majesty—acting as if they had handled the Divine Scriptures with faith rather than with fraud and deceit—add the rest of their faithlessness as if it were now a proven assertion: **"He shall not descend with his body before the day of judgment,"** and again, **"according to his command, we do not believe him to be personally on earth."** Therefore, they argue that if he ascended into heaven as he did and left the world, we must not confess that he descends again into the Sacrament according to his true nature. They claim he will not descend under any other condition—a condition known only to him through his omnipotence, but unthinkable and ineffable to us.

Put aside your insane presumption, Pighard! For Christ is not limited to descending only in the single way you define for him. Rather, just as the Divinity was present when Adam heard the voice of the Lord God walking in paradise in the afternoon breeze; or when He descended to see the tower and confound the languages; or when He was received as a guest by the righteous <note>likely referring to Abraham at Mamre</note>; or when He inspected the cry of Sodom; or when He appeared in the burning bush; or when He dwelt above the Mercy Seat of the Ark <note>original: "propiciatorum arche"; referring to the golden lid of the Ark of the Covenant</note>—at those times, though He descended to perform unusual works, He nevertheless remained always within His own hidden essence. In every moment, it was truly said: **"Our Father, who art in heaven."**

In a similar way, we truly say at all times, according to the Apostolic decree: **"He ascended into heaven, sits at the right hand of God the Father Almighty, from thence he shall come to judge the living and the dead."** Yet we believe that Christ descends no less daily into the Sacrament in a way incomprehensible to us, just as he said so that he might be present: **"This is my body; do this in remembrance of me."** Furthermore, we believe that Christ descends to earth whenever he witnesses to his presence through miracles and works beyond the course and power of nature.

This is just as it will be when—as the Apostle wrote—**"then that wicked one shall be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus shall kill with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming."** <note>2 Thessalonians 2:8</note> This refers to the one whose coming is according to the working of Satan. Truly, since the Jews will first cling to the false messiah, the Antichrist, before they begin to confess Christ as the true liberator, a time will intervene between the Antichrist and the Final Day so that all Israel may enter the Church after their final error. And since Christ will kill and destroy that Antichrist "by the brightness of his coming," we therefore—according to the Apostolic word—confess another "coming" of Christ distinct from that final, most illustrious and terrible one. In that final coming, the hinges of heaven and the foundations of the earth shall be torn from their places, and all things shall melt like wax before the face of God, and all flesh shall run to God to receive a sentence according to their merits and demerits.

But the Apostles' Creed <note>original: "Symbolum apostolorum"</note> does not bind us as strictly as the decree of the Pighards. The Creed says truly: **"He sits at the right hand of God the Father Almighty; from thence he shall come to judge the living and the dead."** While it certainly confesses that Christ will come on the Last Day, it does not deny his coming at another time. After this, they rail against the Teacher Augustine <note>St. Augustine of Hippo</note> as if he had not correctly understood their scripture. If, therefore, he said nothing foreign to their confession but spoke what they truly feel—and what we have perceived them to feel—it is not out of anger but by a manifest judgment that we expose the frauds and heresies of the faithless.
