# THE FIFTH BOOK ON THE WALDENSIANS
<note>The header indicates this is the fifth volume of a larger work refuting the Waldensian or "Picard" heresy.</note>

Ee iij
<note>This is a signature mark used by early printers to help binders assemble the book in the correct order.</note>

...to follow and refute our very footsteps and current arguments. But it is enough for the **Picards** <note>original: "Pighardis"; a derogatory term for the Bohemian Brethren or Waldensians</note> that, whether by right or by wrong, our "beehives" <note>original: "aluearia"; a metaphor for the Church and its organized doctrines where the "honey" of divine truth is stored</note> are displeasing to them. But what beehives? Primarily the Canon of the scriptures, the Gospel, the Apostles, and all that holiness which has earned heaven from the vineyard of the Lord. For that lazy **drone** <note>original: "fucus"; in the 16th century, the drone bee was a common metaphor for someone who consumes the labor of others without contributing</note>, the Picard, to exhaust these beehives is a task of great difficulty, since previously all the power of demons has fought in vain with heresy and the sword against these Apostolic beehives, and the truth of the Church conquers above all things. 

But if he thinks entirely from his own arrogant head that the Christian confession is unjust—though his own sect is more full of holes than **rotten wood**—yet the Gospel, the Apostles, and all holiness (whose faith has stood with us on earth through these little works) seem to him more burdensome when he experiences them. Behold our own works, which have only this: that they are **Catholic**; for the rest, according to the poverty of our own talent, they do not approach the beehives, the Church Fathers, or the magnitude of their learning even by a single point. Therefore, let the Picard call our works into judgment. I say, you **asps** <note>original: "Aspides"; referring to the "deaf adder" or "asp" of the Psalms, a common metaphor for stubborn heretics who refuse to hear the truth</note>, conspire and strike the stone, you Picards, so that you might wear away this present dispute.

Finally, they say, "Surely the Lord Jesus will not deceive us." Far be such a great crime from God, who wants the whole human race to be saved. For God is not a tempter of evils, but each one is tempted by being drawn away and enticed by his own **concupiscence** <term>concupiscence: the human inclination toward sin or worldly desires</term>. In this way, the Picards also seduce themselves; for conceiving an untimely hatred against us, they could not walk in the house of God with consensus. But since they could do nothing with power or weapons, they attacked us with faithlessness and perfidy. This hatred has rendered them so blind that, to satisfy it, there is nothing in heaven or earth they do not violate. Therefore, it was not Christ who deceived them, but their own bad mind and evil spirit. Because of this, they neither follow the scriptures nor value the faith of the saints, which they have often abandoned at the slightest offense. Therefore, that curse follows the Picards: *let their table become a snare before them, and a retribution, and a stumbling block; let their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and keep their backs forever bent.* <note>The author is quoting Psalm 69:22-23, which was traditionally interpreted by theologians as a curse upon those who reject the truth.</note> Because of this vice of theirs, **Isaiah** also rebukes the Picards: *Walk in the light of your own fire, and in the flames which you have kindled; this has been done to you by my hand; you shall sleep in sorrows.* <note>Isaiah 50:11</note>

->**THE PICARD**,<-

And those standing by said to Saint Peter: *Truly you also are one of them, for even your speech makes you manifest.* <note>Matthew 26:73</note> The same could be said to this "Doctor" according to his own writing, and so on until that place to which the one God leads us—in the essence of divinity and in person a Trinity: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever blessed—with all those who love the truth and His law. Amen.

Since the Picards are preparing an end to their affairs, they return again to their accustomed frivolous games and put on for a second time that lying mask of innocence which they had briefly set aside during their work. They thrust themselves into examples, making it seem as if they suffer the same things from **Doctor Augustine** as Christ suffered from the Jews. But because they compose themselves for such a simulation out of a contested impiety, from the crime of perfidy and contempt for divine things—so as not to examine the works of others—they betray themselves and commit an **imposture** upon the most holy examples of Christ. Finally, they say that theirs is the "true faith." I would believe it, if everything the Picards have brought forth to us everywhere were not found to be lies, circumventions, and the most noxious poisons. Therefore, since Christ never expressed such impure things, nor has the Church ever observed them, however much they may adorn themselves, they are nonetheless treacherous and must be considered as such.

# ON THE SACRAMENT OF THE EUCHARIST AGAINST THE PICARDS

...they condemn, just as the Law commands us to do, namely: "But that prophet or dreamer of dreams shall be put to death" <note>A reference to Deuteronomy 13:5, which was historically used by polemicists to justify the punishment of heretics</note>. He should certainly not be dragged before judges, but rather be killed by the people for his crime. In this way, the **Picards** <note>original: "Pighardi"; a derogatory term for the Bohemian Brethren or Waldensians</note> are guilty of their own treachery. And they are not only accused by the holy teacher **Augustine**, but condemned as surely as **Phinehas**, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, rose from the midst of the multitude and, seizing a dagger, followed the Israelite man into the chamber and pierced them both through—the man and the woman—in their private parts, moved by a zeal for God against them <note>This refers to the biblical story in Numbers 25 where Phinehas kills an Israelite and a Midianite woman to stop a plague caused by their idolatry; the author uses it here as a metaphor for "holy" intolerance of heresy</note>. The Picards are also accused by that word of God: "If there arises in your midst a prophet or one who says he has seen a dream, and he predicts a sign or a wonder, and what he spoke comes to pass, and he says to you: 'Let us go and follow alien gods whom you do not know and serve them,' you shall not listen to the words of that prophet." <note>Deuteronomy 13:1-3</note>. Truly, by what word of God do the Picards defend their heresy? By what word of God do they pass judgment on the Church and its law, and kill its cause without a hearing? 

Finally, they accuse the teacher **Augustine** of the very things he himself accuses, testifies to, and judges. They are deceived; rather, it is their own treachery, set against the Scripture, that testifies against them. The Gospel, the Apostles, the Law, and the Prophets judge and condemn them. For if they call the teacher Augustine into account here, they simultaneously make a criminal of all ancient holiness that was ever deployed against heresies.

After these things, they mention **communion**. Just as if the whole of faith depended on communion alone, they cannot forget it; they appeal to it everywhere. Yet the Picards do not even preserve the form of **Christ's Supper**, and they are uniquely treacherous regarding the faith of the Sacrament. But whether that form of communion was ever in the Church or not, we have abundantly shown in the fourth book and in this fifth book that the present custom <note>Referring to the practice of "communion under one kind," where the laity received only the bread, not the wine</note> is kept entirely holy by the Church. But even those who in this century revived that **communion under both kinds** <note>original: "vtriusq; speciei communionem"; the practice of giving both bread and wine to the laity, a central demand of the Hussite and Protestant movements</note> were previously driven by the agitation of another crime. In order to interpret their actions as a religious deed, and to feel less shame before men, they threw out "communion" as a religion—like a veil—to cover it. Nevertheless, we do not contend with those who are certain of this; we do not consider them our enemies. And would that Christians had not suffered such hostilities from them—slaughter, plundering, and destruction—as they themselves have not suffered! 

We trade and exchange in turn; we sell and buy; we export and import fruits and merchandise, both theirs and our own, and we cause them no shame for their defection. Yet they have defected; if they are now deserters, the name they bear comes from their own fault. Finally, we do not insult them, but rather pity their unhappiness. For just as a plucked flower, a broken twig, or a severed limb is no longer animated but dies away, so **disobedience** does not grow toward heaven. Let them consider this themselves: if they cast off civil obedience to a city, surely the laws and liberties of the fatherland will not support those who desert it. Nor will the rights of a registered citizen be given to those who are cast out and proscribed. Finally, it is entirely impossible for an outlaw to be considered at the same time a citizen under the law. By this domestic example, I think they will eventually be warned to feel more toward their own salvation. 

You hear, wicked Picard, the Christian equity and clemency which hastens to no man’s injury. But you, who now glue yourself to them—what views do you hold? I do not want that; but what kind of Christians are you making? Exiles from Heaven and earth! What is the cause of your bitter decree? Our faith? Then except for the one matter of **communion under both kinds**, upon what other thing have you cut us off, such that you have not also cut yourselves off from it? The intercession of the **Saints**, the memory of the dead, priestly ordination <note>original: "iniciacio sacerdotalis"; the Sacrament of Holy Orders</note>, the faith and adoration of the **Sacrament of the Altar**—all these things are equally common to us. Therefore, whatever...

# WALDENSIANS BOOK FIVE
Ee iiij

...you have spoken the most foul things against the faith and against us. Now, appearing as nothing less than a clandestine traitor and a domestic enemy, you insert yourself into our midst, composing your countenance not for faith but for convenience. You turn your back as long as you remain safe, then turn around instantly when you suspect destruction for yourself, and now, in your fear, you make others tremble as well. You deck out images of great slaughters <note>original: "magnarum cedium imagines"; likely referring to the rhetoric of the reformers regarding martyrdom or the violence of the wars</note>, so that you may be rendered safe by another’s fury. Finally, you mutter that nothing stops us from rushing to the sword except the adverse will of God. Yet one can observe how vehemently we meditate on, prepare for, and attempt war, and how vehemently we are restrained by God in that attempt. If it is permitted in this way to make people criminals by conjecture, and to accuse a deed not yet done as if it were a fact, you will be much more harmful to us, **Picard** <note>original: "Pigharde"; a derogatory name for the Bohemian Brethren or Waldensians</note>. 

And we suspect with much more credibility: that God stands in the way so that no standard-bearer happens upon you to satisfy your spirit with our blood, which you have so often and so clearly shown is so ulcerated against us that we plainly sense that your vow, mind, zeal, and everything is ready for slaughter, except for the power to carry it out. As for the other things by which they here accuse the Christian state, we have examined all of these in the fourth book; therefore, we now rightfully indulge ourselves by not repeating them. 

After all this, however, they congratulate themselves on the Christian calamity which then happened during that famous Bohemian excursion under the leadership of **Žižka** <note>Jan Žižka (c. 1360–1424), the famous blind general of the Hussite armies</note>, when all the priesthoods, monasteries, and churches of God and the saints were most insolently despoiled, burned, and torn down. Even today, the memorable and astonishing ruins of these places, scattered throughout **Bohemia** and **Moravia**, move those who look upon them to pity and tears, as the memory of our ancestors' piety returns. It comes to mind how the honor of God was profaned, the relics of the saints burned, and the remains of the dead in their holy rest were turned into stables for brutes. 

Upon this lethal calamity the Picards now leap, and they think that the increase of their perfidy would not have occurred if Žižka had not crushed the Christian state. On the contrary, what is far more true is that if Christ had not crushed from heaven the Greek communion "under both kinds" <note>original: "sub utraque specie"; the practice of giving both bread and wine to the laity, a central demand of the Hussites</note>, all schismatics and heretics would today still defend their obstinacy by the Constantinopolitan faction. Now, however, since God has rebuked the Greek Church with the sword and destruction <note>A reference to the Fall of Constantinople in 1453, which Catholic polemicists often interpreted as divine punishment for the Greek Orthodox "schism"</note>, with what face do our rebels persist in their purpose? 

That **Žižka**—from a courtier a deserter; from a deserter a thief; from a thief a standard-bearer of thieves; who knew nothing of justice; who sought right and wrong through arms; a deserter of his lord and of the Kingdom; a burglar of everything sacred and public; who, not for love of piety but for love of plunder and hatred of the religious <note>i.e., the monks and clergy</note>, mixed divine and human law and equally overturned both. This Žižka is not so great that he could make schismatics and Picards righteous against God. 

But what is this, that they congratulate themselves that Žižka was the author of communion under both kinds for them? Do they not therefore confess that their faith was obtained by arms? Therefore, how great is the forgetfulness of the Picard! Or did he not say in that *Apology* of his that no one should be compelled to the faith? Certainly! Therefore, when the business was in such a state that they themselves were doing the compelling, that opinion was valid to them. Now that it comes to us compelling them, they suddenly consider it void. 

Those who plainly believe it is right to be compelled to the faith by arms—as the truly perfidious Picards are now regarding contested matters—if they had fallen into a more vigilant age, they would by their own opinion and deed be rightly compelled to the apostolic faith. Instead, they now remain safe through no merit of their own before God or man, but through the laziness and greed of this time. This is to the damage not only of their own salvation, which they gamble with, but also of the neighborhood, which they never cease to corrupt with their perfidy at every moment. 

Why did Žižka please the Picards so much? By what good deed do they so notably approve of Žižka, whom they now congratulate as a vindicator of religion? Was Žižka not "of the Chalice"? <note>The "Utraquists" or Calixtines were Hussites who focused on the chalice for the laity, whereas the "Picards" or Brethren were often more radical in their theology</note>. Are they not Picards? Do not the schismatics and Picards disagree in all things to be believed, with the sole exception of their disobedience? But I understand: it is not for faith, but for plunder and for slaughters [that they agree].

He compares the destruction of Bohemian churches to the fall of Constantinople as evidence of divine judgment against schismatics.</summary>

# ON THE SACRAMENT OF THE EUCHARIST AGAINST THE PICARDS

...but by the trampling of things profane and sacred, Žižka <note>Jan Žižka (c. 1360–1424), the famous blind general of the Hussites, known for his tactical genius and his destructive campaigns against Catholic churches and monasteries.</note> earned such a notable longing for himself among the **Picards** <note>original: "Pighardos"; a derogatory term for the Bohemian Brethren, who were often grouped with Waldensians by their opponents.</note>. Therefore, Picard, if the opportunity were now available to you, what would you do regarding this vow of yours? Or would you not have the opinion—to use your own words—and the will to answer the power of the world with arms? Entirely so! For both that you are prohibited and that you voluntarily cease from answering the word of the powers of the world with less, your present writing, which we have now examined, is witness. Witness also is that infamous pamphlet, the *Apology of Theology* <note>The *Apologia confessionis*, a defense of the Brethren's faith sent to King Vladislaus in 1508.</note>, which this summer you snatched from a most famous city of the German name <note>likely referring to a printing center like Nuremberg or Augsburg</note> through lies and an obtained printer, and scattered into the world. And so, that you may triumph, you seek not the equity of faith, nor truth at all—from which you have wandered—but the violence of arms. For in this way did Žižka also promote his rebellion. 

If you were truly of the truth, you would as easily allow us to rescue you from your perfidy and sustain us, as easily as Christians, from the conscience of their confession, both receive and sustain you. Now, you sigh only for this: that a leader be made for you. I say to you, for whom it is as pleasing that apostolic obedience be in part undermined as it is displeasing that even this seedbed of apostolic obedience remains surviving through **Bohemia** and **Moravia**. It is because your vow is not to be satisfied by the misfortunes of Christians until you see even this remnant of the same utterly uprooted. I say you long for a leader to come to you who would take up the spirit of Žižka, under whom that which you have long imagined might happen for you:

> Who will give the salvation of Israel out of Zion? When the Lord turns away the captivity of his people, Jacob shall exult and Israel shall be glad. <note>original: "Quis dabit ex Syon salutare Israel..."; Psalm 14:7/53:6. The author suggests the Brethren misuse this scripture to pray for a violent "liberation."</note>

Therefore, your headlong hatred forces Christian safety there; this bloodthirsty will of yours compels the apostolic people to suppliantly call upon the most Christian Prince **Vladislaus** <note>King Vladislaus II of Bohemia and Hungary (reigned 1471–1516).</note> into the common danger. Where you demand a Žižka as the avenger of your traitorous faction and of this perfidy against God and the saints, we, under the favorable auspices of Royal and Christian Majesty, shall successfully run to meet this brigand. 

Therefore, deign, Most Christian and most powerful King Vladislaus, for the sake of the common Christian cause, to come into a part of our labor. Nor should your Majesty be indignant if you are implored now, when the business is nearly finished. For this also was given by the Royal Majesty out of veneration. Thus it is in military matters, whether it be a battle or a siege: first the camp commanders apply their effort, but they permit the highest glory of the completed affair to their Emperor. So **Joab**—to use our own examples—when he was in the camp and the siege of the city, wrote to his King, **David**:

> I have fought against Rabbah, and the City of Waters is to be taken. Now therefore, gather the rest of the people, besiege the city and take it, lest when the city has been destroyed by me, the victory be ascribed to my name. <note>original: "Dimicaui aduersum Rabba..."; 2 Samuel 12:27-28.</note>

David therefore gathered all the people and set out against Rabbah, and when he had fought, he took it. Most powerful and most Christian King, we also have fought against this Picard; we have tested the protection of the most wicked enemy, from which he was wickedly launched into an attack against God, against the saints, and against the Christian faith (which is your own Majesty’s faith). We have broken the most deadly enemy of the Gospel, of the Apostles, and of all holiness by virtue and by hand. The impious Picard lies open for the final assault and his supreme downfall. Only let your Majesty lay the final hand upon it, so that this glory of defending the Christian religion may be added to your Royal innocence and virtue. 

Otherwise, a deadly danger threatens the Christian cause and the safety of the kingdom if you neglect the public enemy—if the wicked Picards escape the Royal hands. I know you have shuddered at the heights of crimes and sacrileges against God and the saints; I know you have shuddered at those most deadly breathings of the greatest hatreds of the Picard against the Christian state. From these things, they indicate they intend nothing moderate, but destruction, slaughter, and the overturning of our most holy religion, whenever another Žižka should happen upon them. And I am minded to turn over and meditate: against such nefarious plans as they conceive against us, I have called the nobility to our aid. I have said—whether you are in that faction or whether you tolerate them—since you indeed consider your blood pure and worthy of your lineage, consider that your ancestors were not such as these. Emulate both their piety and their prudence, among whom that filth and internal evil could neither take root, nor be retained, nor be known at all. Most religious Prince, I could not fail to warn the nobility. Thus let it stop, and let it await the pious command of your Royal Majesty. Therefore, descend into the cause...

# VALDENSIANS BOOK FIVE

Act as a Christian prince, most powerful King, against the confessed enemies of heavenly piety, the **Picards** <note>original: "Pighardos"; a derogatory name for the Bohemian Brethren.</note>, since they wander from the truth both knowingly and willingly. This is the greatest part of the damnation pressing upon them, both for the sake of averting public evil and for establishing the public health of the kingdom—which you, most illustrious Prince, desire to remain unshaken and firm under God for the blood of your House <note>The author is likely referring to the Jagiellonian dynasty and its claim to the Hungarian and Bohemian thrones.</note>. Your Majesty should remember how a harmonious religion can establish kingdoms, and how a discordant one is powerful enough to overturn them.

Thus, when Jeroboam had withdrawn the ten tribes of Israel from the house of David, he took precautions through a different religion so that the province might never return to the legitimate kingdom. Regarding his counsel, the Scripture says: *And Jeroboam said in his heart: "Now the kingdom will return to the house of David, if this people goes up to offer sacrifices in the house of the Lord in Jerusalem; and the heart of this people will turn to their lord Rehoboam, King of Judah; and they will kill me and return to him."* Having devised a plan, he made two golden calves and said to them: *"Do not go up to Jerusalem anymore; behold your gods, O Israel, who led you out of the land of Egypt."* And he placed one in Bethel and the other in Dan. And this thing became a sin, for the people went to worship the calf as far as Dan. Thus, Jeroboam established the perpetual kingdom of Israel through religion, until God transferred the people of Samaria to the Assyrians.

Furthermore, when the Romans had snatched away the liberty and empire of Greece, and for some time the Greeks stood at a foreign tribunal and bore the tribute of servitude—a confession of their killing indignity—they finally regained their seat and liberty under the Constantines <note>The emperors following Constantine the Great who established Constantinople as the "New Rome."</note>. From their own body, they sent judges throughout the world. Fearing that at some time they might again be forced to a foreign tribunal, they applied themselves most obstinately to any means by which they might retain the empire now offered again. Since there was no way for this counsel through either wisdom or arms—because the good fortune of others produces envy in those who lack it, and a lack of confidence in those who have it breeds a desire to seek the same from others (for which reason kingdoms perpetually come and go)—Greece took precautions for itself and its empire through a different religion. 

For religion—that is, the fear of heavenly things and the desire for one's own salvation—is sought from others with less envy. Indeed, it is the nature of empire that it wishes for things to be remote and foreign. Whatever is established, in whatever place and by whatever author, if its authority is once obtained and received in the minds of mortals—even if it be false and plainly impious—it is thereafter retained so tenaciously that no one desires to be against God, from whom everyone expects the fruit of their salvation. So too do men turn away from a different religion, judging those of it to be injurious to God, despisers of their own salvation, and perpetually miserable. 

Therefore, from this counsel, Greece produced from within itself **Arius**, **Macedonius**, **Nestorius**, **Eutyches**, and other masters of novelties <note>These are leaders of famous early Christian heresies: Arianism (denying the full divinity of Christ), Macedonianism (denying the divinity of the Holy Spirit), Nestorianism (emphasizing the distinction between Christ’s human and divine natures), and Eutychianism (the opposite of Nestorianism).</note>, whom it made authors for itself in matters of belief. Through religion—which mortals by their own nature most tremble at and venerate—Greece attempted to ensure that Asia, Egypt, and Africa would expect no right or law from Old Rome. It succeeded so powerfully that Rome was cast out of veneration, to the point that for a long time it was believed that anything a Latin priest touched was contaminated; the altars on which they performed the divine mysteries were considered unclean, and they would rebaptize anyone whom a Latin priest had baptized. Thus, for the sake of imperial greed, Greek impiety went wild until God himself restrained it from heaven.

Then there is **Muhammad** <note>original: "Maumettes"</note>, that false prophet of the Saracens and Turks, about whose superstition the Divinity predicted: *This man will be wild; his hand against all and the hands of all against him, and he will pitch his tents over against all his brothers.* <note>A reference to the biblical prophecy regarding Ishmael in Genesis 16:12, traditionally applied to the rise of Islam in medieval polemics.</note> When he sensed that the Arabs were meditating on defection because of a perceived disgrace, he used a timely army of Arabs, and with himself as a timely leader through Syria, Egypt, and Africa, he established a great power for himself. Since Muhammad wanted this to be lasting, he sought a firmament for his rising empire from a new religion. Nor was he deceived in his opinion. For while the Emperor **Heraclius** <note>Heraclius (r. 610–641 AD), the Byzantine Emperor who fought the Persians but saw the initial rapid expansion of the Islamic Caliphate.</note> neglected the rising superstition, and after recovering the East from the Persians, triumphed as if he had subdued the Persians with Greek delights—as if that one work were enough for his glory and the benefit of his empire—he gave himself over to feasts and baths. He forgot the losses of his empire and treated deserters in the same way as citizens, granting lands and homes throughout his province of Syria to the Arabs and Saracens with a misplaced clemency...

Ee iiij

# ON THE SACRAMENT OF THE EUCHARIST AGAINST

...lest I say anything more grave against the Emperor of the East. The abuses of **Heraclius** <note>Heraclius (r. 610–641 AD) was a Byzantine Emperor. The author blames his religious policies for the loss of territories to the early Islamic conquests.</note>, through his favor of a new religion, raged with an insatiable fury against the confessors of the Christian faith, as if they were fresh enemies of either God or the prophet. In doing so, he cut off the most extensive empires, the most blessed provinces, the most populous cities—and in one stroke, Asia and Africa—from the Christian confession, along with the splendor and glory of all Europe: Greece itself. Indeed, Prince Heraclius cast from his more secret delights a name to be showed in the face of the Christian and the impious, which in this time has grown to such magnitude that it has been made fatter by the very organs by which it ought to have been digested. Now, unless it is dissolved from heaven by a manifest miracle, the internal parts of the Christian republic will burst before they can reject it. He who sustains a diverse religion certainly nourishes a **serpent in his bosom**. A contrary religion creates contrary minds.

Look even at the one Jewish nation that has lived for so many centuries in Christian provinces; yet neither in sound, nor in clothing, nor in food, nor in the habit of the body, nor in any manners does it agree with us. Rather, within our midst, they retain their own foreign and pagan-like habit. A diverse religion closes the circle of the earth to mortals. It is **suspicion** <note>The author argues that religious difference breeds the mutual distrust that makes travel and diplomacy difficult.</note> of the Turk—not the scepter he aims—that makes the approach to Greece difficult; it is **superstition** that makes Palestine so remote to us at such great expense. And the treachery of the **Picards** <note>The Bohemian Brethren, whom the author views as a domestic threat equivalent to the foreign threat of the Ottoman Turks.</note> gives birth to these same detriments for the Christian state, whatever they may eventually produce. These people now yearn to hasten so greatly, and they are only prevented from doing so by their current number and lack of means—a wish they betray on every page of their writings. They harass not only the Christian common folk, but also the entire Royal Majesty. In that **Confession** <note>Referring to the "Confessio Waldensium" presented to King Vladislaus II in 1508.</note> given to your Royal Majesty, they say:

> [ But in truth, because we now perceive that your gentleness has now departed from the law of human kindness and mercy. Therefore, we vehemently pity your highness, since you have preferred to embrace a matter adverse to your governance. ] <note>original: "At vero quia vestram mansuetudinem... amplecti"</note>

Do they not in this place accuse your Royal Majesty of **tyranny**? And which of the Kings is more innocent after his holiness? Who else refrains more from oppression and blood? Only one or two Picards were condemned to prison and fire for blasphemies against God and the saints; the rest of the accomplices of that most impure and foul flock were sent away safe. These are the enemies of divinity, the domestic accusers of your Royal Majesty, among whom a more stubborn vengeance for the condemnation of a few resides, because you left the entire **Synagogue of the Picards** <term>Synagogue of the Picards (Synagoga Pighardi): A derogatory term used by Catholic polemicists to describe the gathering or church of the Bohemian Brethren, implying they are non-Christian.</term> untouched.

That hatred is also retained in another place, where **Doctor Augustinus** <note>Augustin Olomucensis (1467–1513), the King’s secretary and a fierce opponent of the Brethren.</note>, your Royal Majesty's secretary, is likewise insulted. They betray this most clearly with these words: *“Who therefore insinuated themselves to the princes, and confirmed the impious hands of the princes.”* Hey there, you Picard! Whose spirit was the persecutor of the saints? The spirit of the accuser, the devil! Since such people acted from this spirit, they resisted the saints and the prophets, and they confirmed the impious hands of princes in slaughter. Whose spirit do you accuse Doctor Augustinus of possessing? The devil's? Whom do you make him out to be? The same one who resists the Picards for the sake of the just and the good, away from their treachery—and I doubt not he resists even their "prophets." He [Augustinus] confirms the "impure hands" of Prince **Vladislaus** <note>Vladislaus II (r. 1471–1516), King of Bohemia and Hungary.</note> in slaughter? Therefore, by your judgment, this most indulgent Prince has impious hands, especially since he [Augustinus] approached as an advisor. 

But hear this, most treacherous Picard: if indeed you were called wicked, impious, sacrilegious, and blasphemous by our blind judgment before your treachery was shaken off, it would be a matter of which of us was thrusting a crime upon the other. But because we have endured all those things, we have struck out these claims of yours. We find these things to be against the Scriptures and the faith of the ancestors, and that you respect nothing anywhere, which is why you refuse to be called a "Picard." Rather, you have suppressed these things, corrupted those, and erased others so that you might defend yourself more wickedly. Finally, you have constructed everything with lies that can be felt with the finger. Since we find you to be such a person, witnessed by present realities, Doctor Augustinus has now brought this crime of yours to the knowledge of the Royal Majesty. If the Royal Majesty, with him as advisor, should avenge heavenly piety, they would not be the two people you make them out to be; but truly another...

# WALDENSES BOOK FIVE

Whoever he was, by whose intervention you are safe, he will be held guilty before God and the Christian state. He prepares a seat for himself in **Gehenna** <note>original: "gehenna"; a biblical term for hell or eternal punishment</note> among you **Pighards** <note>A term of abuse used for the Bohemian Brethren or Waldensians, likely derived from "Picards."</note>. He is no more upright for himself, nor more beneficial for **Your Royal Majesty**, nor more faithful to the safety of the kingdom than was once **Eusebius the Eunuch** <note>Eusebius (died 361 AD) was a powerful court official under Constantius II who favored the Arian heresy.</note>, the Prefect of the Bedchamber to **Constantius**, son of the Great Constantine and successor to the impious Emperor. That man, the most powerful of all courtiers and a wicked pursuer of his lord's legacy, was a plotter. Under a pretense of duty, he had "bought" the ears, eyes, and every sense of his lord, so that the Emperor perceived nothing for himself, seeing and hearing only what that man wished. When such power and will were redeemed by the **Arian heretics** who were then rising, he brought it about before Constantius that **Arius**—who had been cast into exile by Constantine the Great because of his heresy—should be brought back. Thus the Arian heresy grew, protected by the Emperor as its guardian. 

But what followed? Namely, that the **Goths, Vandals, and Lombards**, when they had poured themselves into the impious empire and sought the apostolic faith, were instead intercepted by Arian treachery. The Arians then used the arms of these peoples; finally, those nations, stirred up by a zeal for that treachery, raged against the apostolic confession with plundering, fires, and slaughter. They polluted the impious empire through **Illyricum, Pannonia, Italy, Gaul, Spain, and all of Africa** with impiety, and overturned it with arms. In the same way, by the favor of a few, the Pighards grow stronger by the day. And even in this weak time of theirs, they look wickedly upon your Royal Majesty, most pious **Prince Vladislaus** <note>Vladislaus II (1456–1516), King of Bohemia and Hungary.</note>. They have most wickedly alluded to dogs and pigs—terms they have long revealed in their most burning hatred for us and for the entire Christian state. 

But hey, you most impure Pighard, to whom among all Christians did you address this confession and your **Apology** <note>A formal written defense of their faith.</note> to be examined? To **Your Royal Majesty**. Tell me, you most impure Pighard: surely you did not betray all your "holiness"—for that is how you want us to describe your blasphemies—and all your "heavenly mystery" to the King? I say, with you as my witness, you did not betray it. For you say that you used that "evangelical prudence": *Beware of men, for they will deliver you up* <note>Matthew 10:17</note> and *Do not give what is holy to dogs, nor cast your pearls before swine* <note>Matthew 7:6</note>. You say you used that apostolic counsel: *Walk prudently toward those who are outside* <note>Colossians 4:5</note>. Therefore, you deem the King’s Majesty unworthy of your secrets. You turn away from him as if he were impure. You accuse him as one who has held many of you in chains or killed you, contrary to divine and human law. From this Royal Majesty, you withhold all the more hidden parts of your treachery, *lest you give your "holy thing" and your pearls to the unclean.* You regard the King's Majesty as an outsider because of his worship of "idols"; you have cast him into pure idolatry because of his use of **sculpted images**, the **intercession of saints**, and the **adoration of the Sacrament of the Altar**. 

Consider, most pious King, the vow and the mind of those robbers. Let your Majesty estimate their "holiness"—is it not the **face of a scorpion**, which at first sight feigns innocence, but threatens a sting from its tail? Who is a greater pretender than this Pighard? He secretly mixes the most atrocious poisons. His writing is more slippery and indirect because it is adorned with the color of simplicity and innocence to avoid suspicion, yet in secret, it festers with every atrocious and lethal venom. Nor does it stop there, most pious King; your Majesty is insulted by these crimes of the Pighard. Truly, like a boiling cauldron casting off its heated froth, so the Pighard overflows with one thing after another from his stomach, which seethes with hatred for us. With these things, he covers and suffocates the Christian state in the foulest mud of infamy. 

Such is their claim: *They did not call upon the Lord; there they trembled with fear where there was no fear* <note>Psalm 13:5 (Vulgate numbering), often used by reformers to criticize Catholic rituals as superstitious "fear."</note>, just as they currently do regarding the male and female saints. Most pious King, do you not, after God, worship the saints and the **Virgin Mary**? Most certainly and most religiously. Hear then, most pious Prince, what this wicked Pighard retorts against your Royal Majesty for this Christian piety: *You have not called upon the Lord; you have trembled with fear before the saints and the Virgin Mary where there had been no fear.* Finally, it is for this purpose that these pestiferous Pighards make your Majesty guilty of a single impiety—that of not worshipping the Godhead—nay, rather of every most atrocious crime mentioned in that same **Psalm 13** from which they copied this little verse. They condemn all who do these things to this punishment: that they should *tremble where there is no fear.* Into all this impiety, from this one verse...

e. b. 6.

# ON THE SACRAMENT OF THE EUCHARIST AGAINST

The pestilent **Pighards** <note>A derogatory term for the Bohemian Brethren, or "Unitas Fratrum," a pre-Reformation Christian movement in Bohemia.</note> exclude your majesty. Your majesty itself is that "fool" <note>original: "insipiens"; the author is quoting Psalm 14:1, accusing the dissenters of viewing the King as the biblical 'fool' who denies God.</note> who has said in his heart: "there is no God." It is itself corrupt and made abominable in its pursuits; it has turned aside and become useless. Its throat is an open sepulcher; your tongue has acted deceitfully; the venom of asps is under your lips. The feet of your majesty are swift to shed blood; destruction and unhappiness are in your ways. You have not known the way of peace. There is no fear of God before the eyes of your majesty. You devour the helpless Pighard like a morsel of bread. You have adored the most divine **Sacrament of the altar**, the undefiled **Virgin Mary**, and all the saints, but you have not called upon the Lord. For such great offenses against God, you trembled with fear where there had been no fear. They thrust such crimes, horrific to speak of, upon you, the **Most Christian King**, and equally upon all Christian people. But they tremble at such a horrible and deadly accusation against the **Royal Majesty**, and they shuffle about, wishing it to remain unnoticed. 

Therefore, **Most Christian King**, if they do not wish you to be held for punishment by your Christian piety, it is because they do not think your majesty agrees with us in the faith. But you are the most Christian of all. Therefore, from what graven image, from what idolatry of the saints and the **Sacrament**, from what "abominations" taken from this present Psalm <note>The author refers to Psalm 14 (or Psalm 53 in some numbering), which describes the corruption of the godless.</note> have they defamed the Christian faith? By all these things they have insulted your **Royal Majesty**, so that your majesty might receive this judgment from God: let him tremble with fear of the saints and the Virgin Mary, "where there had been no fear." I know your majesty is astounded how this servile cattle, the Pighard, dares and is able so atrociously to insult you, the lord of his life and death.

But this is not their supreme crime which they commit against your majesty; rather, by casting out and profaning our Christian priesthood, they deny the legitimate union of your majesty's parents, your majesty's own legitimate birth, and the birth of the **Most Illustrious Prince Louis** <note>Louis II (1506–1526), son of Vladislaus II. The author argues that if the Brethren reject Catholic marriage and baptism, they effectively declare the royal family illegitimate.</note>, the sole heir to the kingdom. They deny whatever birthright belongs to you by right of divine baptism. The mind shudders at the atrocity of such an accusation with which the Pighard dissects your majesty and every other royal majesty and the whole Christian state. These are the things the Pighards are now bringing forth from their differing religion against Christian piety; unless you withstand them, **Most Religious Prince**, they will soon give birth to them. They will desire to intercept the provinces of the Christian confession—which they consider the most impure of all—by their treachery. And what their most trifling impiety cannot achieve by itself, it will demand by force of arms. In these plans, only a leader is missing, not the will; for they boast that once a leader of rebellions, **Zizka** <note>Jan Žižka (c. 1360–1424), the famous Hussite general who never lost a battle.</note>, befell this kingdom. 

Even at this time, unless **Your Royal Majesty** tempers your edicts (as they say in their confession), they long for such a liberator and supreme defender of their impiety to be raised up against the royal power. Meanwhile, however, they conclude that they must endure this necessity, saying that their souls are held by Christ's command to the virtues of patience and pretense. Such are the Pighards; their own writing witnesses that they will one day be fatal to the Christian cause. Therefore, **Most Powerful Prince**, stand against them and turn away this most atrocious plague while it still remains within their wishes and minds. Otherwise, no mediocre evil hangs over us. A most dangerous kind of rebellion is being attempted; for while it spreads under the appearance of a better life, and while no one prevents men from "becoming better" through a religious institution, the mass of another power grows. A conspiracy thickens under the favor of religion and ends up where it was not feared—it ends up where kingdoms are finally undermined. Therefore, let your majesty stand against it while the enemy’s affairs are still weak. Assert God's honor, which alone your majesty desires to serve in this life. Restore the veneration of the saints and the **Virgin Mary**, whom you look to as your only helpers before God for your offenses. Confirm this kingdom for your **Most Illustrious blood**, for our most expected **Prince Louis**, whom your fatherly and royal affection desires to reign most happily. Persist in the work, **Most Religious Prince**, nor...

He cautions that their outward "patience" hides a desire for a new militant leader like Jan Žižka to overthrow the social order.</summary>

# WALDIANS BOOK FIVE

Let your Majesty not be moved by the Pighards, even if they threaten much regarding the divine wrath that is not to be provoked. Let your Majesty consider there that our religion is Christian, while their superstition is a persuasion of the devil. But why would they think this is a great thing? If they themselves believe, or wish others to believe about them, that they are pure in religion, did not the Jews flatter themselves with the same example when they adored the calf? "These are your gods, Israel, who led you out of the land of Egypt." <note>Exodus 32:4</note> Does not the Saracen <note>A common term for Muslims in this period.</note> grant an apotheosis <note>Divine status</note> to his Muhammad with the same madness? Is whatever anyone believes from a naked opinion to be received? Rather, the origins from which every opinion is taken must be inspected. And the superstition with which the Pighard now flatters you has proceeded from figments; it has no kinship with God, with the Gospel, or with the Apostles. Therefore, if they are afflicted, no sin of the deed comes to God. For if they display the adversities of their lives or their constancy in torments or in death itself as a sign of innocence; if they threaten divine wrath upon you, the **Most Christian Prince**, as the avenger of injuries against God, his saints, and the apostolic faith: let your Majesty consider there that not all who suffer persecution for whatever cause are immediately saints. For by this reasoning, no one would have been more just, no one closer to God, than the Egyptians and Canaanites whom Moses and Joshua afflicted with such calamities and final destruction; no one would have been more just at that time than those unbelievers whose bodies God prostrated in the desert. But if those men, in their most bitter slaughters, were the most damned of all, then by that example, let all the pestiferous malice of heretics also be judged, even if they are terrified from their quiet by dispute, so that they might be struck with the sword. Although they have the name of God in their mouths, although they stuff their little works with the memory of sacred things, they are nonetheless criminal against God and the saints, and harmful to heavenly piety. For Peter said: "let none of you suffer as a murderer, or a thief, or a slanderer, or a craver of others' goods," <note>1 Peter 4:15</note> but neither the disobedient, nor the slanderer, the schismatic, the heretic, and likewise the sacrilegious and the blasphemer shall possess the kingdom of God. For only those are blessed, says Christ, who suffer persecution for the sake of justice. For if the Pighards now boast of their adversities, whatever they may be, and think them a mark of heavenly kinship, does this world not go according to the wish of the Pighard alone? Or is there not that public complaint running through the course of every age, sex, and condition of men: infirmity of the body, the deaths of loved ones, the flooding of fields, fires, by which both the hope of our old age and of our children are consumed; profound poverty at home, virgin daughters, naked, of marriageable age and unmarriageable; the oppressions of the powerful, and among these, the corrupt judge? In these evils, if the Pighard offers public hatred for his perfidy, so that he may boast of being received into the lot of the martyrs, that he might be a friend to God, that he might be believed holy for his perfidy—it is so far from the truth! For adverse things do not grant that every man is rendered a Christian closer to God. Nor does all persistence testify to a good conscience. For even the little sorceresses, the poisoners, and the hags <note>original: "Mulierculæ Sagæ. veneficæ, lamiæq;" — terms for witches and practitioners of folk magic.</note> have often wished to die for their poisonings; and the guilty could sometimes be driven by no torment so grave as to name their accomplices. Therefore, let us imagine that the Pighard, suffering all things more atrocious, should so endure in his purpose: it is not a holier conscience of his perfidy, but a deranged mind and a sense numbed by perpetual blasphemies against God and the saints that denies the Pighard pain and makes him obstinate toward punishment. Therefore, insults, animadversions, and deaths—just as for the Manichaean, the Sabellian, or the Arian <note>Reference to the Great Heresies of the early Church: Manichaeism (dualism), Sabellianism (modalism), and Arianism (denial of Christ's divinity).</note>—just as for all enemies of God and the saints, so for the Pighard: they build no merit in heaven for the crime of perfidy, but only guilt in Gehenna. Therefore you say, **Most Christian Prince**: "Let those enemies of God, contemners of the saints, and the most present pestilence of the safety of the kingdom, the Pighards, be slain." I say, **Most Christian Prince**: "Let the deniers of heavenly piety, the Pighards, be slain." So would the most holy and perfect examples from God command: God extinguished the world with a flood, Sodom and Gomorrah with fire, the Egyptians with ten plagues, and the Canaanite with final destruction. He afflicted the Jews wandering from true piety in the desert, and in the promised land of Judea and Samaria, with captivity, the sword, and migration. He damned the East and Greece to barbarian captivity because of perpetual heresies. St. Augustine, Bishop of Hippo...

e d. 7.

# ON THE SACRAMENT OF THE EUCHARIST AGAINST THE PIGHARDS

<meta>catchword: nor</meta>

These pestilential Pighards <note>A derogatory name used for the Bohemian Brethren or Waldensians.</note> exclude your Majesty; to them, your Majesty is that very "foolish one" who said in his heart, "There is no God." <note>This is a reference to Psalm 14:1. The author is suggesting that the Pighards' ideology implicitly accuses the King of atheism or idolatry.</note> This ideology is itself corrupt and has become abominable in its pursuits; it has turned aside and become useless. Their throat is an open grave, your tongue has acted deceitfully, the venom of asps is under your lips; the feet of your Majesty are swift to shed blood. Ruin and misery are in your ways. You have not known the way of peace. There is no fear of God before the eyes of your Majesty. 

You devour the Pighard like a morsel of bread. <note>The author is likely mirroring the Pighards' own rhetoric back at them, using Psalm 14:4 to show how they view the King as a persecutor.</note> You have adored the most divine Sacrament of the altar, the undefiled Virgin Mary, and all the saints. You have not called upon the Lord. For such great offenses against God, you have trembled with fear where there was no fear. They thrust such crimes—horrendous even to speak of—upon you, the **Most Christian King**, and equally upon all Christian people. Yet they tremble at such a horrible and deadly accusation against your Royal Majesty; they shift their ground and wish it to go unnoticed. Therefore, **Most Christian King**, if they do not wish to be held for punishment by your Christian piety, it is because they do not believe your Majesty agrees with us in the faith. But you are the most Christian of all. Therefore, from whatever "graven image," from whatever "idolatry" of the saints and the Sacrament, from whatever "abominations" of the present Psalm they have defamed the Christian faith—they have also insulted your Royal Majesty with all those things. Thus, let your Majesty receive this judgment from God: let him tremble with fear regarding the saints and the Virgin Mary, where there had been no fear. 

I know your Majesty is stunned that this servile beast, the Pighard, would dare and be able to so atrociously insult you, the lord of his very life and death. But this is not even the supreme crime they commit against your Majesty. Rather, by profaning and casting out our Christian priesthood, they deny the legitimate marriage of your Majesty’s parents, the legitimate birth of your Majesty, and the just, present, and divine birth through baptism of the most illustrious Prince Louis <note>Hludouicus refers to Louis II, the young heir to the thrones of Bohemia and Hungary.</note>, the sole heir of the kingdom. The senses shudder at the atrocity with which the Pighard dissects your Majesty and every other Royal Majesty and the entire Christian state. These are the things the Pighards are now "giving birth to" <note>The author uses the metaphor of "parturition" to describe a hatching conspiracy.</note> from their different religion against Christian piety; unless you resist, most religious Prince, they will soon bring them forth. They will desire to seize by their treachery the provinces of the Christian confession, which they consider the most impure of all. And what their most triffling impiety cannot achieve by itself, it will demand by arms. For these plans, only a leader is lacking, not the will—especially since they boast that once a leader of rebellions, Zizcka <note>Jan Žižka (c. 1360–1424), the famous one-eyed Hussite military leader who successfully fought against Crusader armies.</note>, happened to this kingdom. Even at this time, unless your Royal Majesty moderates your edicts (as they say in their confession), they long for such a liberator of their impiety and a supreme defender to arise against the Royal power. In the meantime, they will possess what they conclude by this necessity, saying again: their souls are held by the command of Christ through the virtue of patience and pretense. 

Such are the Pighards. Thus they are testified by their own writing to be future bringers of ruin to the Christian cause. Therefore, most powerful Prince, turn away this most atrocious plague while it still remains within their desire and mind. Otherwise, no small evil hangs over us. In this way, the most dangerous kind of defection is attempted: while they flock together under the appearance of a better life, and while no one prevents men from becoming "better" through a religious institution, the mass of their power grows. A conspiracy gathers strength under the favor of religion and breaks out into that which was not feared—it breaks out into that which eventually undermines kingdoms. Therefore, let your Majesty resist while the affairs of the adversary are still weak. Offer your honor to God, whom alone your Majesty desires to serve in this life. Restore veneration to the saints and the Virgin Mary, as you expect them to be your only helpers before God for your offenses. Confirm this kingdom for your most illustrious blood, our most expected Prince Louis, whom your fatherly and royal affection desires to reign most happily. Persist in this work, most religious Prince, nor...

<summary>The author warns King Vladislaus II that the Pighards (Bohemian Brethren) view his Catholic devotion as idolatry and their theological positions effectively invalidate his royal legitimacy and the birthright of his son, Prince Louis. He urges the King to suppress them before they find a military leader like Jan Žižka to lead a violent rebellion.</summary>
<keywords>Pighards, Vladislaus II, King Louis II, Jan Žižka, Bohemian Brethren, royal legitimacy, idolatry, Hussite rebellions, sacraments, Catholic polemic</keywords>

--- Page 397 ---
<meta>This page continues the author’s direct address to King Vladislaus II. Having previously argued that the Pighards (Bohemian Brethren) view the King as an enemy of God, the author now addresses the Pighards' claims of divine protection and their arguments that their suffering proves their righteousness.</meta>

# THE WALDENSIANS: BOOK FIVE

Do not let the Pighards disturb your Majesty, even if they threaten that much divine wrath will be unleashed. Let your Majesty reflect that our religion is Christian, while their superstition is a persuasion of the devil. But however great they think this threat is—if they believe it themselves or want others to believe it of them—that they are pure in their religion, did not the Jews flatter themselves with the same example when they adored the calf? **"These are your gods, O Israel, who led you out of the land of Egypt."** <note>original: "hi sunt dii tui Israel qui te eduxerunt de terra Aegypti" — a reference to Exodus 32:4.</note> Does not the Saracen <note>A common medieval term for Muslims.</note> grant an apotheosis <note>The elevation of a human to divine status.</note> to his Muhammad with the same madness? Surely, must whatever anyone believes out of a naked opinion be accepted? Rather, one must look at the origins from which every opinion is taken. And the superstition with which the Pighard now flatters you is fashioned from fictions; it has no kinship with God, with the Gospel, or with the Apostles. Therefore, if they are afflicted, no guilt for the deed falls upon God.

If they offer the adversities of their lives or their constancy in torments or even in death itself as a sign of innocence; if they threaten divine wrath against you, the **Most Christian Prince**, as the avenger of the insults against God, His saints, and the Apostolic faith: let your Majesty reflect that not everyone who suffers persecution for any cause is immediately a saint. For by that logic, no one would have been more just, no one closer to God, than the Egyptians and Canaanites, whom Moses and Joshua afflicted with such great calamities and final destruction. No one would have been more just at that time than those unbelievers whose bodies God prostrated in the desert. 

But if those people, in their most bitter disasters, were nonetheless the most damned of all, then by that example, let all the pestiferous malice of the heretics be judged, even if they are driven out from their rest by dispute or struck by the sword. Even if they have the name of God in their mouths, even if they stuff their little works with the memory of sacred things, they will nonetheless be criminals against God and the saints, and harmful to heavenly piety. For Peter said: **"Let none of you suffer as a murderer, or a thief, or an evildoer, or a seeker of other people's things."** <note>original: "nemo autem vestrum patiatur quasi homicida aut fur aut maledicus aut alienorum appetitor" — 1 Peter 4:15.</note> Nor shall the disobedient, the slanderer, the schismatic, the heretic, and likewise the sacrilegious and the blasphemous possess the kingdom of God. **"Blessed,"** says Christ, **"are those who suffer persecution for the sake of justice."** <note>Matthew 5:10.</note>

And if the Pighards now boast of whatever adversities they face and think them a mark of heavenly kinship: is it only for the Pighard that this world does not go according to his wishes? Or is there not a common grievance through the whole course of every age, sex, and condition of men: the weakness of the body, the deaths of loved ones, the flooding of fields, fires by which the hopes of our old age and our children are consumed, deep poverty at home, virgin daughters—exposed, of marriageable age, but unable to be settled—the oppression of the powerful, and among these, a corrupt judge? 

If the Pighard offers the public hatred he faces because of his perfidy <note>In this context, "perfidy" refers to religious betrayal or heresy rather than just general treachery.</note> as one of these evils, so that he may glory in being received as a brave martyr, so that he may be a friend to God, so that he may be believed holy because of his betrayal—this is as far from the truth as it is that all adverse things fail to make a Christian closer to God. Nor does all stubbornness testify to a good conscience. For even little witches, sorceresses, and hags have often wished to die for their sorceries, and no torment, however grave, could at times force the guilty to name their accomplices. 

Therefore, let us imagine that the Pighard, suffering even more atrocious things, nonetheless endures in his purpose: this is not a holier conscience of his perfidy, but a displaced mind and a sense numbed by perpetual blasphemies against God and the saints, which denies pain to the Pighard and makes him obstinate toward punishment. Just as insults, adversities, and deaths were to the Manichaean, the Sabellian, and the Arian <note>Reference to early Christian heresies: Manichaeism (dualism), Sabellianism (denial of the Trinity), and Arianism (denial of Christ's full divinity).</note>—as to all enemies of God and the saints—so for the Pighard, because of the crime of his perfidy, he builds no merit in heaven, but only guilt in Gehenna <note>A biblical term for hell or a place of fiery punishment.</note>.

Therefore, you say, **Most Christian Prince**: let those enemies of God, those despisers of the saints, and that most present plague to the safety of the kingdom—the Pighards—be put to death. I say, **Most Christian Prince**: let the deniers of heavenly piety—the Pighards—be put to death. For the most holy and perfect examples from God have so commanded. God extinguished the world with a flood, Sodom and Gomorrah with fire, the Egyptians with ten plagues, and the Canaanites with final destruction. He afflicted the Jews who wandered from true piety in the desert, in the Promised Land, in Judea, and in Samaria with captivity, the sword, and exile. He condemned the East and Greece to barbarian captivity on account of their perpetual heresies. Thus says St. Augustine, Bishop of Hippo...

ee. v.

<summary>The author argues that the Pighards' suffering and stubbornness are not signs of martyrdom or holiness, but rather the result of a numbed and blasphemous mind. He calls upon King Vladislaus II to execute them, citing biblical precedents where God destroyed the wicked and heretical.</summary>
<keywords>Pighards, Bohemian Brethren, martyrdom, heresy, Moses, Joshua, persecution, divine wrath, Manichaeans, Sabellians, Arians, capital punishment, Vladislaus II, St. Augustine</keywords>

--- Page 398 ---
<meta>This page continues the author’s direct address to King Vladislaus II. Following a discussion on the nature of suffering and religious truth, the author now transitions into a historical and legal argument for the forceful suppression of the Pighards (Bohemian Brethren), citing precedents from the Old Testament and the reign of Charlemagne.</meta>

### ON THE SACRAMENT OF THE EUCHARIST AGAINST...

He [St. Augustine] judged that the **Donatist** <note>A 4th-century North African sect that argued the church must be composed only of "saints" and that sacraments administered by "traditores" (those who had surrendered scriptures under Roman persecution) were invalid.</note> heretics should also be punished by the sword. **Charlemagne** <note>original: "Carolus Magnus"</note> compelled inner Germany to the faith by arms. With the sword, he thoroughly purged the Danube of idolatry. And in the previous century, all Europe restored the faith to Jerusalem, Palestine, and Syria by the right of war. There are infinite examples, **Most Pious King**, showing that the Christian religion has been asserted through slaughter and blood. Thus, we recently recovered the Spains from the African. Moses commanded that both the one who had perjured the name of God and the prophet who had persuaded the Jewish people toward a foreign religion should be publicly stoned. As long as a sin in the Republic is committed outside the laws, whatever is sinned remains without penalty or death. But if at another time laws begin to exist against that sin, the same sin demands punishment and death by the law.

So it is in religion: until someone is deceived by the weakness of their senses into believing wrongly—outside of Scripture and the express decrees of the saints—they are not held for capital perfidy <note>A term implying a crime of "bad faith" or treason against the divine order, punishable by death.</note>. But if someone has defected from the decreed faith, they are now held guilty of capital perfidy; and impiety is expiated by exile and blood, according to those divine decrees, by what is fair and good. Therefore, you say, **Most Christian Prince**, let the **Pighards** <note>A derogatory name for the Bohemian Brethren, or Waldensians.</note>—who have violated, suppressed, corrupted, and erased the sacred Canon of the Scriptures; who have denied all holiness; who have fashioned their own opinions against the Scriptures and the most-witnessed Apostolic faith—let them pay with their blood.

This decree is well-deserved, **Most Pious King**, but out of Christian clemency, harsher measures have not yet been tried. Therefore, let them be expelled; this indeed is good for the crime of the Pighard. But, **Most Christian King**, into what lands shall they be expelled? Germany, Poland, and Hungary bring forth enough evils from themselves to irritate God without also having foreign perfidy poured into them. They do not go to the Tartar or the Turk—or if they do go, just as they have now filled Lower Moesia in great numbers, then these too will wish to go to the Tartar and the Turk. Now, as all extremes are desperate, we will have them as the most immediate betrayers of our fortunes and most bitter enemies. If you give the Pighards the barbarian sword, **Most Pious King**, you will have given a most sharp goad to the barbarian sword.

May it rather please your Majesty—otherwise most desirous of the public safety—that they be repressed within the province by some such counsel as the **Antichrist** <note>In medieval and early modern thought, the Antichrist was a literal figure expected to persecute the Church before the end of the world.</note> will one day use against the Christian confession according to the prophecy of the **Apocalypse** <note>The Book of Revelation.</note>. **No one shall buy; no one shall sell; no one shall sit in the magistracy; all private and public life shall be infamy.** <note>original: "Nemo emet. nemo vendet. nemo in magistratu sedebit. infamia oīa puata & publica erūt." — A reference to the "Mark of the Beast" in Revelation 13:17.</note> Let there be an interdiction of water and fire <note>A Roman legal formula for total social exclusion and banishment.</note> for all who do not have the mark of the beast of the Antichrist on their forehead and hand.

It is right at this time, while Christian power still stands, that you strike the devil in the Pighards by this same art of his. There are many civil ignominies by which the Pighards may be marked for their perfidy, either by one or by many. Let them be made conspicuous through towns and countryside by whatever mark, just like the **Jews**. <note>Refers to the historical practice of requiring Jewish people to wear identifying badges.</note> Let a fine be given to the magistrates for anyone who, throughout the week, has not adored at Christian rites or has not heard the Word of God. If they have not provided an account of participating in Christian Communion for a year, let it be forbidden to them—just as it is to the Jews—to speak to anyone about their own perfidy. Let transgressors be punished by a portion of their substance [property]. I think that, moved by domestic inconveniences, they will forget both their superstition and their leader **Žižka** <note>original: "Zizckae" — Jan Žižka (c. 1360–1424), the famous Hussite general and hero of the Bohemian Reformation.</note>. They will truly and from the heart want you as King.

That you may accomplish this against the Pighard hangs as lightly from the hands of your Majesty as the world hangs from the nod of God. Only let the care of God and religion be present, which is otherwise so great in your Majesty, by which you might easily contend and surpass all Royal Majesty. And, O Immortal God, what shall I say of this evil? When similar plagues have arisen at various times through Italy, the Gauls, and Germany, and these were cut down at their beginnings and along with their authors, only **Bohemia** and **Moravia** <note>original: "Collimicia Moravia" — likely referring to the Chlumec region or a specific Moravian district.</note> are places where whatever perfidy is born must immediately be retained. May your Majesty free this people from infamy; may you make it so the Christian world knows that perfidy cannot be retained in your seat. But if here someone of a different opinion should oppose your royal will...

<summary>The author argues that religious heresy should be met with state force, citing Charlemagne and Moses as precedents. He proposes that instead of simple execution or expulsion, the King should implement "civil infamy" against the Pighards, stripping them of social and economic rights to force their return to the Church.</summary>
<keywords>Pighards, religious persecution, Charlemagne, Jan Žižka, Bohemia, Moravia, Antichrist, civil law, heresy, Waldensians</keywords>

--- Page 399 ---
<meta>This page concludes the author's polemic against the Bohemian Brethren, transitioning from legal and historical precedents to a direct final appeal to King Vladislaus II and his son Louis. The text concludes with a colophon detailing the book's production in Leipzig.</meta>

<header>WALDENSIANS: BOOK FIVE,</header>

...which is in the mouths of many, let him intercede and say: "When God is unwilling [to tolerate] the **Pighards** <note>A derogatory term used for the Bohemian Brethren or Waldensians, likely derived from "Picards."</note>, He Himself will restrain them from heaven." Permit me here, most indulgent prince, to respond to that man: "Look here, you! Indeed, when God is unwilling to tolerate the wicked and evil, He will kill them all in a single work. Why then do you hasten to punish theft, robbery, and murder by laws and by your own hand? Or does it not then come to your mind that when God is unwilling, He Himself will be the first to avenge theft, robbery, and murder from heaven?" 

**Most Pious King**, this persuasion is not from God, but from the devil. God permits all things on earth to be done through human administration: good things for merit, and evil things for punishment. And just as human laws demand punishment not only for the perpetrators of a crime, but also for those aware of it and in whose power it was for the crime to happen or not—so God sends into damnation from Him not only the authors of **perfidy** <note>religious betrayal or heresy</note>, but also those aware of it. Thus in the **Books of Kings** <note>Referring to the Old Testament accounts of the Kings of Israel and Judah.</note>, not only the idolatrous kings are condemned, but also those who believed rightly yet did not remove the material of superstition—the altars, groves, high places, and all memories of demons. 

Thus we have shattered this unjust opinion, **Most Illustrious Prince**. Therefore, let Your Majesty return to your most Christian vow. With whatever countenance Your Majesty is accustomed to punish conspiracies, seditions, and defections—so that your earthly kingdom remains safe—with that same spirit, let him desire and wish, according to God, to guard Christian religion undefiled against the most deadly conspiracy and foulest perfidy of these most lost men. It is a crime even in moral discipline not to have defended a friend against a slanderer; how much greater an outrage it will be to have heard the sacrilegious insults of the Pighard against God and the Saints with indifference and to have left them undefended. 

Therefore, let Christian piety, asserted by you, be a symbol in the hand of Your Majesty whenever your piety shall be called from earth to heaven. Let this be the sign by which God recognizes the most powerful **King Vladislaus** <note>Vladislaus II (1456–1516), King of Bohemia, Hungary, and Croatia.</note> to have been His friend and the guardian of holiness on earth. Thus may your blood, the Most Illustrious **Prince Louis** <note>original: "Hludouicus." This is Louis II, the King's son and successor.</note>, have God as the preserver of his power and happiness on earth, just as Your Majesty has labored vehemently here for the preservation of celestial religion and the honor of God and the saints. May you find God favorable to you for eternal happiness at that time, as you have defended His religion on earth from every injury.

---

This work began to be established in the year of the Christian salvation 1510, on the fifth **Ides of November** <note>November 9th.</note>. However, because of travels and many other business matters, it was often interrupted and resumed; nevertheless, the total time spent upon it was exactly seven months. God, blessed above all things forever, gave the strength and the mind. The noble Lord **Heinrich Kuna of Kunstat** <note>original: "Heinricus Kuna de Chunstat." A prominent Bohemian nobleman who patronized the work.</note> redeemed the printing shop with his own money, and **Melchior Lotter**, a citizen of **Leipzig** <note>original: "Lypsensis." Lotter was a famous printer of the early Reformation era.</note>, printed it. In the year 1512, in the month of October, on its very last day.

<summary>The author concludes his argument by urging King Vladislaus II to treat heresy with the same legal severity as civil crimes, ending with a colophon identifying Heinrich Kuna of Kunstat as the patron and Melchior Lotter as the printer in 1512.</summary>

### Marbled Endpaper with Snail Pattern

This page features a high-quality example of **marbling** <term>a method of aqueous surface design which can produce patterns similar to smooth marble or other kinds of stone</term>. The specific design is a "snail" or spiral motif, characterized by large, rhythmic swirls.

The color palette consists of:
*   **Navy blue**
*   **Golden yellow**
*   **Slate grey**
*   **Rose-pink background**

The design is further textured with small white and pale yellow "stones" or droplets, a technique used to add depth and complexity to the marbled surface. 

In the left margin, the physical structure of the book is visible, showing the **gold tooling** <term>the process of decorating a book cover by pressing heated metal tools into gold leaf</term> on the inner edge of the leather binding, as well as the gathered edges of the preceding paper leaves.

<summary>This page consists of a decorative marbled endpaper featuring a snail or spiral pattern in blue, yellow, and grey. It marks the end of the manuscript's physical text block and the beginning of the rear binding.</summary>

Dear Sir,

Thank you for your letter of 2nd August. <note>A red line underlines the following passage from "The three copies" to "any of them."</note>The three copies of the **Double Confession of the Waldensians** <note>original: "Duplex confessio Valdensium"; this 16th-century document outlines the faith and grievances of the Waldensians, a medieval Christian movement that was often persecuted for its beliefs.</note> in our collection agree in every respect with the **collation** <term>Collation: A technical description of a book's physical structure, used by scholars to ensure no pages are missing by checking the sequence of printed sheets.</term> of the Harvard copies, and with **Apponyi** <note>Reference to the "Hungarica" bibliography by Count Sándor Apponyi, a standard reference work for books related to the history of Hungary and surrounding regions.</note>. There is no list of **errata** <term>Errata: A list of printing errors discovered after a book was printed, often tipped into the volume on a separate slip of paper.</term> given in any of them. <insert>red mark</insert>

->Yours faithfully,<-

Andrew C. Wale
for the Superintendent.

--- Page 414 ---
<meta>This letter continues the correspondence of Herbert Reichner, a rare book dealer, as he consults with major academic libraries to verify the physical structure and completeness of 16th-century volumes. While the previous page featured a response from the British Museum, this page is a reply from the Houghton Library at Harvard University regarding a work by the scholar Ziegler.</meta>

LIBRARY OF HARVARD UNIVERSITY
CAMBRIDGE, MASSACHUSETTS
THE HOUGHTON LIBRARY

->6 August 1965<-

Mr. Herbert Reichner
Stockbridge, Massachusetts

Dear Mr. Reichner,

After another look at our copy of <term>Ziegler<note>Likely referring to Jacob Ziegler (c. 1470–1549), a German humanist, geographer, and theologian.</note></term> it is now clear to me that the copy you have taken is correctly bound and complete in the first <term>gathering<note>A group of sheets folded together to form a section of a book.</note></term> and that the copy we have retained is also complete but is misbound <note>Meaning the pages were tucked into the binding in the wrong order during production.</note>.

The first gathering consists of six leaves, and it can be seen that all pairs are <term>conjugate<note>Two leaves (pages) that are part of the same continuous piece of paper, joined at the spine.</note></term>. If ours were correctly bound the order of contents would be exactly the same as yours. I believe as you do that <term>Schottenloher<note>Karl Schottenloher (1878–1954), a preeminent German bibliographer whose catalogs are standard references for researchers of the Reformation era.</note></term> has somehow confused matters in his description. But there may well be another issue with an <term>errata<note>original: "errata"; a list of printing errors and their corrections discovered after the book was printed.</note></term> list printed on one of the pages that is blank in your copy and ours. I shall be interested to hear what you learn of the copies in other libraries.

Very truly yours,

W. H. Bond <note>Handwritten signature</note>

W. H. Bond
Librarian

WHB:pao <note>These are the initials of the author, William H. Bond, and the typist who prepared the letter.</note>

<meta>Faint watermark in paper reads: CRANE'S DISTAFF BOND / MADE IN U.S.A. / 100% RAG CONTENT. "Rag content" indicates high-quality paper made from cotton or linen fibers rather than wood pulp.</meta>

<summary>W. H. Bond, Librarian at Harvard's Houghton Library, confirms to Herbert Reichner that Reichner's copy of a book by Ziegler is correctly bound, while Harvard's own copy contains a binding error. The letter highlights the meticulous process of comparing rare book "gatherings" to identify discrepancies in historical bibliographic descriptions.</summary>
